Aggregated inside `getSkillTreeStatBonus` alongside `stat`/`globalStat` (so it lands in the same per-(class,stat) sum and obeys the same `SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP`/`SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP_OVERRIDES` clamp, and is recomputed by exactly the existing triggers — `applySkillTreeStatBonuses` at run start, the detail panel on hover — with no new recompute path): it contributes `perOwned * countOwnedTaggedNodes(...) * skillNodeOwnedScale(...)`. **`countOwnedTaggedNodes(unlocks, classId, tag, cache)`** counts nodes that (a) carry `tag` in an array-valued `tags` field, (b) are currently owned, and (c) resolve to `classId` via `getSkillTreeNodeTab` — a node counts **once regardless of its rank**. The optional `cache` object is a per-`getSkillTreeStatBonus`-call memo keyed `classId + '|' + tag`, so N synergy effects on one stat cost one tree scan, not N. `tags` is read nowhere else and is inert on a node no `synergyStat` references. `describeSkillEffect` gained a `synergyStat` branch (`"+2% meleeDamage per owned \"brawler\" node"`) and `describeSkillEffectTotal` routes it to the new **`describeSynergyStatTotal`**, which reports the live owned-tag count and what it is currently worth. `describeStatTotal`'s "after buying" projection also folds owned `synergyStat` contributions into its raw pre-clamp total (its `globalStat` blind spot is deliberately left as-is, to keep every pre-existing node's preview text byte-identical).
    - **Rendering** — `buildSkillTreePanel`'s per-node block computes `maxRank`/`rank`/`spentGate`/`spentLocked`/`rankable`/`nextCost` and: `affordable` dropped its `!owned` term (it now defers wholly to `canBuySkillNode`, which is the only function that knows a partially-ranked node is re-buyable — behaviour for a plain node is unchanged because `canBuySkillNode` already returns `false` for anything owned and unranked); the cost badge, the `title` "need N pt" text and the sell-confirm all use the rank-aware price; new classes `.ranked`/`.rankable`/`.rank-maxed`/`.spent-locked`; a new centred-bottom **`.skilltree-node-rank`** pip badge reading `"<rank>/<maxRank>"` (gold-filled once maxed) and a **`.skilltree-node-spentgate`** `◔` badge (bottom-left, same corner as `.skilltree-node-lock` — the two never co-occur in practice since an excluded node is already unbuyable); `title` additions spelling out both the rank state and the exact unmet breadth-gate numbers. `showSkillNodeDetail` appends the name with `" (r/max)"` for a ranked node, shows the **next rank's** cost with a `"(next rank)"` suffix, and adds two new rows: `.detail-note-rank` (rank count + next-rank price + per-rank step) and `.detail-note-spentgate` (met/unmet with have/need), plus a `.detail-spent-locked` panel class. **`style.css`** gained `.skilltree-node.spent-locked`, `.skilltree-node-spentgate`, `.skilltree-node.ranked`/`.rankable`, `.skilltree-node-rank` (+ `.rank-maxed` variant) and the `.detail-note-rank`/`.detail-note-spentgate` rows, all following the existing `.excluded`/`.skilltree-node-lock` badge conventions. `index.html`'s `#skillTreeLegend` gained a "Ranked node" and a "Breadth gate (points spent)" entry.
  - **Pan/zoom persistence (Phase 8f-camera)** — `zoom`/`panX`/`panY` are now **module-level** variables (`skillTreeZoom`/`skillTreePanX`/`skillTreePanY`, declared above `buildSkillTreePanel`), not locals recreated on every call, specifically so a purchase-triggered rebuild (the `.buyable` click handler calling `buildSkillTreePanel()` again) reuses wherever the player last panned/zoomed to instead of snapping back to the default view. `skillTreeZoom` doubles as an "unset" sentinel: it starts (and is reset to) `null`; `buildSkillTreePanel()` only computes+applies the default centered-on-`start` view (`zoom 1`, `panX`/`panY` centering the root node near the top of the viewport) when `skillTreeZoom == null` — otherwise it reuses the persisted values untouched. **`resetSkillTreeCamera()`** sets all three back to their sentinel (`null`/`0`/`0`) and is the function that should be called on a genuine fresh panel OPEN (as opposed to an internal rebuild); the wheel-zoom and click-drag-pan handlers both read/write these same module-level variables directly (not local shadow copies), so panning or zooming, then buying a node, then panning again, all accumulate onto the one persisted camera state. The zoom-toward-cursor math (`world = (cursor - pan) / zoom` then `pan' = cursor - world * zoom'`) and the drag-panning mousedown/mousemove/mouseup/mouseleave listener set are unchanged from the prior pass, just reading/writing the hoisted variables instead of function-local ones.

Wired into `index.html`/`main.js` like the Achievements/Bestiary overlays but sized differently: `#skillTreeScreen` carries `.screen.hidden.overlay.achv-overlay.skilltree-overlay` — the extra `.skilltree-overlay` class overrides `.achv-overlay`'s centered/padded sizing so the panel fills the whole viewport instead (header and Close button pinned in normal flex flow, `#skillTreeList` given all remaining space), while Achievements/Bestiary keep the original `.achv-overlay` sizing untouched. Opened by `#skillTreeBtn` (main menu), `#pauseSkillTreeBtn` (pause menu), and the `KeyK` keybind, all now via `openOverlay('skillTreeScreen', () => { resetSkillTreeCamera(); buildSkillTreePanel(); })`/`toggleOverlay(...)` with the same wrapper — **only these fresh-open call sites reset the camera** (Phase 8f-camera); the purchase-triggered rebuild inside `buildSkillTreePanel` itself calls `buildSkillTreePanel()` directly, with no reset, so the camera survives a purchase. Closed by `#skillTreeCloseBtn` or backdrop click, and included in the Escape-handler's open-overlay search array. `#skillTreePointsBadge` (reuses `.new-badge` styling) shows the live point count on the main menu's Skill Tree button, refreshed by `refreshSkillTreeBadge()` (hidden when `points <= 0`) alongside `refreshAchievementsBadge`/`refreshBestiaryBadge` in `updateLifetimeStatsDisplay()`.

### achievements/skilltree-characters.js

*(Phase 8c — the 250 character skill nodes, 10 per character × 25 `CLASSES` entries, bringing `SKILL_TREE_NODES` to 278 total. Pure data appended onto `skilltree.js`'s arrays; no engine function changed. Loaded in `index.html` immediately after `achievements/skilltree.js`.)*

- **Topology (Phase 8f-topology — hand-varied per character, no longer a repeated template)** — originally every character used the identical rigid shape (two branch openers `a1`/`b1`, each forking into two 2-node subpaths). As of Phase 8f, **`SKILL_TREE_CHAR_TOPOLOGY`** — a `{classId: {key: fullParentNodeId}}` table sitting just above `buildCharacterSkillNodes` — replaces that single global parent-lookup with a hand-designed one per `classId`, so each character's tree has a genuinely different branch count/width/depth (some hubs have 4 direct children, some 1-3 with branches nested/grafted inside each other; individual branches render as a plain Y-fork, a single-file 5-node chain, a late fork, or a wide partway fork). The one hard invariant preserved per character: within each of the four original 5-node "branches" (opener + two 2-node subpath chains), a node that was deeper in its ORIGINAL chain still requires strictly more prior purchases to reach than a shallower one in that same original chain — i.e. relative power-vs-depth ordering survives even though the branch's absolute position/shape doesn't. `SKILL_TREE_CHAR_TOPOLOGY`'s values are **full** parent node ids (not bare local keys), which lets a node here be grafted under a `c*`/`d*`-branch node this file doesn't even define (from `skilltree-characters-2.js`) — resolution is purely by id-string lookup at build time, so the two files' load order doesn't matter. Node `id`/`name`/`desc`/`effect` content is completely unchanged; only this parent wiring differs. `computeSkillTreeLayout` (`skilltree.js`) needed no changes — it already handled arbitrary branching/depth. See `feature-research/phase8-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-topology-camera.md` for the full per-character shape-signature table and verification harness output. `skilltree-characters-2.js`'s analogous **`SKILL_TREE_CHAR_TOPOLOGY_2`** table (covering that file's `c*`/`d*` keys) works identically and is designed as one combined 20-node shape per character together with this file's table.
- **Stats/amounts** — each character picks exactly 2 `SKILL_TREE_STAT_FIELDS` stats (one per branch); both subpaths within a branch target the same stat as their branch's opener, so a branch is one specialization told two flavor-different ways, not two different stats. Cost is `1` per node uniformly. Amounts are the same fixed split for every character: opener `0.05`, each depth-2 subpath node `0.04`, each depth-3 leaf `0.03`. `fireCooldown`/`meleeCooldown` are deliberately never used here — at the time this file was authored, `getSkillTreeStatBonus` clamped a stat's summed bonus to `[0, SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP]`, so a cooldown-*reducing* negative amount would just get floored to 0, leaving no way to author a genuinely helpful cooldown node. **This restriction no longer holds**: Phase 8b-uniquefx made the clamp symmetric (`[-SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP, SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP]`), so a future content pass *can* author a negative-amount `fireCooldown`/`meleeCooldown` node that actually reduces the cooldown — this file's existing 250 nodes are simply never retroactively edited to add any.
- **Cap design rule** — for every character × stat, the worst-case sum (opener + *both* full subpath chains, i.e. all 5 nodes in a branch bought) is `0.05+0.04+0.04+0.03+0.03 = 0.19`, safely under `SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP` (`0.25`) with margin to spare.
- **`SKILL_TREE_CHARACTER_CONFIG`** — the 25-entry authoring table (`classId`, `statA`, `statB`, and hand-written `{name, desc}` per of the 10 node keys `a1/a2a/a3a/a2b/a3b/b1/b2a/b3a/b2b/b3b`) that `SKILL_TREE_CHARACTER_NODES` is mechanically expanded from (ids/parents/costs/effects are derived from the template; only the flavor text is authored per node). Ids follow `char_<classId>_<key>` (e.g. `char_earth_a2a`).
- At load, a closing loop pushes every entry of `SKILL_TREE_CHARACTER_NODES` onto `SKILL_TREE_NODES` and registers it in `SKILL_TREE_NODES_BY_ID`, the same append pattern `skilltree.js` itself uses for the hub nodes.

Full stat-pairing table (classId → branch A stat / branch B stat) and verification harness output: `feature-research/phase8-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-characters.md`.

### achievements/skilltree-characters-3.js

*(Phase 9 megaupdate step 3 — doubles every character's skill tree from 20 to 40 non-hub nodes: 500 new nodes, 20 per character × 25 `CLASSES` entries. **Mega A step 4** then added 26 more cursed gate nodes in the same file, so it now contributes 526 nodes and brings `SKILL_TREE_NODES` to 1054 total (528 + 526). Pure data appended onto `skilltree.js`'s arrays; no engine function changed. Loaded in `index.html` immediately after `achievements/skilltree-characters-2.js` and before `achievements/skilltree-general.js`.)*

- **Topology** — each character's 20 new nodes form four new 5-node extension branches (keys `e/f/g/h`), each grafted onto one of that character's existing deepest leaf nodes from the old 20-node set (defined across `skilltree-characters.js`'s `a*`/`b*` keys and `skilltree-characters-2.js`'s `c*`/`d*` keys) — never a brand-new branch off `char_hub_<classId>`, and the old 20 nodes/their parents are never edited. **`SKILL_TREE_CHAR_TOPOLOGY_3`** (`{classId: {key: fullParentNodeId}}`, same shape as the two prior topology tables) drives the grafting.
- **`SKILL_TREE_CHARACTER_CONFIG_3`** — the 25-entry authoring table (`classId` + hand-written `{name, desc, effect, cursed?}` per of the 20 node keys `e1/e2a/e3a/e2b/e3b/f1/.../h3b`) that `SKILL_TREE_CHARACTER_NODES_3` is expanded from. Ids follow `char_<classId>_<key>` (e.g. `char_earthpony_e2a`).
- **Cursed mandatory-gate nodes** — the "many mandatory gates" cursed-node design from this megaupdate: 174 of the 500 new nodes carry `cursed: true` and a pure-debuff (all-negative-amount) `stat` effect, and each is the sole `parent` of at least one further node in its branch — since `canBuySkillNode`'s existing single-parent-required purchase logic already enforces "must own parent to buy child," a cursed node's descendants are automatically gated behind accepting its debuff first, with no engine change needed. The remaining ~326 new nodes are ungated normal stat payoffs, for build variety.
- **`SKILL_TREE_CHAR_GATE_CONFIG_3` (Mega A step 4)** — after step 3, only ~half of the 100 payoff leaves (`e3b/f3b/g3b/h3b`) sat behind a cursed `X2b` parent; the other 26 `(classId, branch)` pairs reached their branch's deepest payoff for free. This table adds ONE extra cursed gate per such pair — id `char_<classId>_<e|f|g|h>x`, `cost:1`, `cursed:true`, a single negative `stat` effect — spliced between that branch's `X2b` node and its `X3b` payoff: the gate takes `X2b` as its parent and `X3b` is emitted with the gate as its parent (done inside `buildCharacterSkillNodes3`, so no already-built node object is mutated; `SKILL_TREE_CHAR_TOPOLOGY_3` itself is untouched). Each entry is `{curse, site, stat}`: `curse` is a curse-phrase that character's tree doesn't already use, `site` reuses that branch's own `2b` site noun, and `stat` is the SAME field that branch's cursed opener (`X1`) already reduces, at `-0.03` (the magnitude the existing cursed `X2b` nodes use) — so a gated branch reads as one escalating cost on one field. `name`/`desc` are generated from `SKILL_TREE_GATE_CURSE_FLAVOR_3` + `SKILL_TREE_GATE_STAT_LABEL_3`, reusing the exact phrasing of the hand-written cursed nodes. Net result: **all 100 payoff leaves in this file are now behind at least one mandatory curse**, and the file's cursed-node count is 200 of 526.
- **Effect types used** — 100% `stat`-type (both the cursed debuffs and their payoff descendants); no `unique*`/`unlock`/`poolWeight` content in this batch, which was scoped purely to node-count doubling + cursed gating, not new per-class mechanics (those were Phase 8c-2's job).
- **Cap discipline** — worst-case per-(classId, stat) sum across the *full* 40-node set (old 20 + new 20, every node bought including cursed negatives) verified to stay within `getSkillTreeStatBonus`'s symmetric `[-0.25, 0.25]` clamp for all 25 characters.
- At load, a closing loop pushes every entry of `SKILL_TREE_CHARACTER_NODES_3` onto `SKILL_TREE_NODES` and registers it in `SKILL_TREE_NODES_BY_ID`, same append pattern as the two prior character-node files.

Verification harness output (dupe/parent/cap/cursed-gate/layout checks) and recovery notes (this phase's implementer was cut off mid-task by a session rate limit; the file it had already written was independently verified complete and correct, and only the script tag + this audit were still needed): `feature-research/phase9-megaupdates/audit-skilltree-double-cursed.md`.

### achievements/skilltree-general.js

*(Phase 8d — the 25 general-upgrade skill nodes, attached under the existing `general_hub` node; **Mega A step 4** added 2 cursed gate nodes, so this file contributed 27. At the time this file was written `SKILL_TREE_NODES` totaled 553 (528 + 25); Phase 9's `skilltree-characters-3.js` — loaded before this file — plus step 4 brought the running total to 1081 (1054 + 27) by the time this file's original nodes were appended. **A later data-only pass ("Global Mastery")** then appended 9 more nodes (`gen_global_*`), bringing this file's total to 36. Pure data appended onto `skilltree.js`'s arrays; no engine function changed. Loaded in `index.html` immediately after `achievements/skilltree-characters-3.js`.)*

- **Design** — deliberately simple compared to the character branches: most nodes carry exactly one `poolWeight`/`startingPickup`/`globalStat` effect; a few bundle two related effects (`gen_rare_generous`, `gen_global_gate`, `gen_global_capstone`). Real hand-written `name`/`desc` per node, each `desc` stated in terms of the actual effect (no templated flavor text). Cost is `1` per node for the original 25 nodes; the Global Mastery branch varies cost 1→3 with depth (see below).
- **Topology** — six hand-shaped sub-branches off `general_hub` (varied width/depth, not a repeated template):
  - **Loot Weights** (7 nodes, `gen_loot_*`) — `COMMON_CATEGORY_POOL` penny/heart category nudges, each forking into `COMMON_PENNY_POOL`/`COMMON_HEART_POOL` sub-tier nudges (nickel, dime, luckypenny, heartBlue, doubleheart).
  - **Supply Drops** (6 nodes, `gen_supply_*`) — `COMMON_CATEGORY_POOL` bomb/key category nudges, each chaining into `BOMB_TIER_POOL`/`KEY_TIER_POOL` double/gold tier nudges.
  - **Starting Supplies** (5 nodes, `gen_start_*`) — `startingPickup` effects: +1 bomb, +1 key, +3 then +2 more coins (two-node chain), +1 blue heart.
  - **Rare & Legendary Fortune** (6 nodes, `gen_rare_*`/`gen_leg_*`) — `RARE_POOL` (star/sack/battery) and `LEGENDARY_POOL` (trinket/familiar) nudges; `gen_rare_generous` is the one two-effect node, nudging both `RARE_POOL.battery` and `COMMON_HEART_POOL.halfheartBlue` together ("Generous Recovery").
  - **Chest Fortune** (1 node, `gen_chest_hub`) — a single `CHEST_TYPE_POOL.cursed` nudge, a deliberately small standalone branch (organic width variation, not padded out to match the others).
  - **Global Mastery** (9 nodes, `gen_global_*`) — the first branch in this file to use `{type:'globalStat', stat, amount}` instead of pool weights/starting pickups: every node here is a small flat stat bonus that applies to every character's run, not just one class (see `getSkillTreeStatBonus`'s classId-agnostic accumulation pass). `gen_global_hub` (cost 1, `+1%` `speed`) roots the branch off `general_hub`; two more cost-1 nodes fork off it (`gen_global_crit` `+1%` `critChance`, `gen_global_magnet` `+1%` `magnetRadius`); three cost-2 mid nodes deepen each fork (`gen_global_melee` `+2%` `meleeDamage`, `gen_global_ranged` `+2%` `rangedDamage`, `gen_global_reload` `-2%` `fireCooldown`); `gen_global_gate` (cost 2, `cursed:true`) bundles a further `+2%` `rangedDamage` with a universal `-2%` `luck` debuff via `skillTreeGlobalDebuffEffects('luck', -0.02)`; past the gate, two cost-3 nodes close the branch (`gen_global_boltspeed` `+3%` `boltSpeed`, then `gen_global_capstone` `+2%` `speed` and `+2%` `rangeTiles` together). Because a `globalStat` bonus on stat X shares the same clamped `[-0.25, 0.25]` total as any per-class `stat` bonus on X for that character (`SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP`), every amount here is kept small (1-3%) to leave headroom for that character's own per-class nodes on the same stat.
- **Cursed gates + `skillTreeGlobalDebuffEffects(stat, amount)` (Mega A step 4, extended by the Global Mastery pass)** — the two strongest reward-pool sub-branches used to hang free off `general_hub`; each now sits behind one mandatory cursed gate spliced in between (`gen_rare_gate` → `gen_rare_hub`, `gen_leg_gate` → `gen_leg_hub`; each gate's `parent` is `general_hub` and the hub node's `parent` was re-pointed at its gate — the only existing field that step rewrote in the file). Both are `cost:1`, `cursed:true`, `-0.02` on `luck`. The Global Mastery branch adds a third gate, `gen_global_gate` (`cost:2`, mid-chain rather than hub-adjacent, also `-0.02` `luck`, paired with its own `+2%` `rangedDamage` buff in the same `effects` array). Because `getSkillTreeStatBonus` matches `eff.classId === classId` against a **real** class id — the engine has no `'ALL'` wildcard — a genuinely class-agnostic debuff is expressed via **`skillTreeGlobalDebuffEffects(stat, amount)`**, a tiny module-level helper defined at the top of this file that returns `Object.keys(CLASSES).map(classId => ({type:'stat', classId, stat, amount}))`, i.e. an `effects` ARRAY with one identical negative entry per class. The four `skilltree-unlocks-*.js` files (all loaded after this one) reuse the same helper for their own gates.
- **Weight-sizing rule** — every `poolWeight` bonus was sized so that the worst case (every node targeting a given pool+id bought at once) leaves that entry's weight at roughly ≤2x its base (e.g. `COMMON_CATEGORY_POOL.penny` 25→27, `RARE_POOL.battery` 15→20 combining `gen_rare_battery`+`gen_rare_generous`, `COMMON_PENNY_POOL.luckypenny` 1→2 exactly at the 2x line since it's a single node on an already-negligible-weight entry). Verified by harness (`feature-research/phase8-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-general.md`).

### achievements/skilltree-unlocks-familiars.js

*(Phase 8e slice 3/4 — 1 hub (`unlock_familiars_hub`, child of `unlock_hub`) + 25 leaf nodes, one per new `sk8f_`-prefixed familiar in `data/familiars-1.js`; **Mega A step 4** added 7 cursed gate nodes (`sk8f_gate_1..7`), so this file now contributes 33. Pure data appended onto `skilltree.js`'s arrays; no engine function changed — `applySkillTreeUnlockEffect` already handled `{type:'unlock', category:'familiar', id}` generically. Loaded in `index.html` immediately after `achievements/skilltree-general.js`.)*

- **Topology** — five hand-shaped sub-branches off `unlock_familiars_hub` (varied width/depth, not a repeated template): Orbiting Menagerie (`fam_orbit_*`, 4 nodes, single chain), Ranged Menagerie (`fam_ranged_*`, 6 nodes: 4 shooters then 2 mirrors grafted on), Support Menagerie (`fam_support_*`, 7 nodes: 3 procs / 2 blockers / 2 scavengers in three sub-branches), Skirmisher Menagerie (`fam_skirmish_*`, 6 nodes: 2 thieves / 2 growers / 1 berserker+1 swarmer in three sub-branches), Blast Menagerie (`fam_blast_*`, 2 nodes, a flat sibling pair). Each leaf carries exactly one `{type:'unlock', category:'familiar', id:'sk8f_...'}` effect, cost 1, real hand-written name/desc describing that familiar's actual behavior/stats.
- **Cursed capstone gates (Mega A step 4)** — every branch here that runs two or more steps past a hub now ends behind ONE mandatory cursed gate, spliced between that branch's deepest leaf ("capstone") and the capstone's old parent; the capstone's `parent` field is the only existing field the step rewrote. Leaves that hang straight off a hub (`fam_ranged_tarpitcher`, `fam_skirmish_ravensnatch`) are deliberately left free. 7 gates: `sk8f_gate_1..7`, `cost:1`, `cursed:true`, `-0.02` `magnetRadius` each (one stat for the whole file, so the worst case with everything bought is `-0.14` — comfortably inside `getSkillTreeStatBonus`'s `[-0.25, 0.25]` clamp). Because the engine has no `'ALL'` classId wildcard, each gate's penalty is a genuinely universal one built with **`skillTreeGlobalDebuffEffects`** (defined in `skilltree-general.js`, which `index.html` loads before this file) — an `effects` array with one identical negative entry per class, rather than punishing one arbitrary class.
- Verification harness (loads the real data/achievements files via `node:vm`, checks id collisions, behavior-string validity against `familiars.js`'s real dispatch, tree connectivity/no-cycles/no-orphans, and every unlock effect resolving to a real familiar) + full 25-id/behavior/flavor table: `feature-research/phase8-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-unlocks-familiars.md`.
- **Pool-nudge coverage extended** — `js/systems/room.js`'s `spawnClearRoomPickup` previously left `BOMB_TIER_POOL`/`KEY_TIER_POOL` (common-tier bomb/key rolls) and `CHEST_TYPE_POOL` (legendary-tier chest roll) unwrapped. This phase wraps those three room-clear call sites with `applySkillTreePoolNudge(pool, 'PoolName')`, matching the pattern already used for `COMMON_CATEGORY_POOL`/`COMMON_PENNY_POOL`/`COMMON_HEART_POOL`/`RARE_POOL`/`LEGENDARY_POOL`. For `BOMB_TIER_POOL`/`KEY_TIER_POOL` the existing `.filter(t => !t.locked || isPickupKindUnlocked(t.id))` now runs **before** the nudge (the nudge's cloned array only carries `{id,w}` and would silently drop the `locked` flag the filter needs). `rollGenericPickupKind()`'s own `BOMB_TIER_POOL`/`KEY_TIER_POOL` rolls (the generic-pickup re-roll used by chests/sacks/sacrifice spikes — not room-clear) and the two procedural room-population `CHEST_TYPE_POOL` rolls (also not room-clear) are intentionally left unwrapped, out of scope for "room-clear reward pool" nodes.
- **`startingPickup` fields** — `bombs`/`keys`/`coins`/`blue`, matching `applySkillTreeStartingPickups`'s exact recognized set (`blue` maps to `player.blueCurrent`).

Full node-by-node table and verification harness output: `feature-research/phase8-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-general.md`.

- Every leaf is a single `{type:'unlock', category:'trinket', id:'sk8t_...'}` effect, cost `1`, real hand-written `name`/`desc` describing that trinket's actual effect.
- **Topology** — no extra sub-hub nodes (only 26 nodes exist: 1 hub + 25 leaves); organic branching comes from letting leaves parent other leaves. 12 branches hang directly off `unlock_trinkets_hub`, ranging from single standalone leaves (`sk8t_fourleafpin`, `sk8t_eelskinwrap`) up to a 4-deep chain (`sk8t_hungryfangcharm → sk8t_direstingpin → sk8t_rimeclasp → sk8t_boneshakerpouch`).
- The 25 trinkets are mostly single-slot stat trade-offs in the same tone as the file's existing entries (a buff paired with a small drawback, e.g. `sk8t_ironclasp` +1 damage/-10% speed, `sk8t_glasscannon` +8% crit/-1 damage) wired as `t === 'sk8t_...'` terms into `js/systems/items-1.js`'s `recalcPlayerStats` (speed, melee/ranged damage, fire rate, range, crit chance/multiplier, luck, dodge, magnet radius, bomb radius, pierce, multishot, lifesteal, flat venom/freeze chance, shop discount). A handful (4) touch a different effect shape instead: coin value (`sk8t_giltclasp`, `combat-2.js`'s coin-pickup `coinMult` ternary), an on-kill bomb-drop chance (`sk8t_boneshakerpouch`, `combat-2.js`'s kill-drop `else if` chain, same shape as `powderpouch`), an extra-bomb-per-pickup (`sk8t_direkegcharm`, `combat-2.js`'s `case 'bomb'`, same shape as `powderflask`), and a familiar attack/proc-rate speedup (`sk8t_stormcollar`, `familiars.js` — factored the pre-existing repeated `swarmcollar` ternary out into a shared `familiarRateMult(player)` helper so both trinkets fold into the same 7 call sites without duplicating them).
- **Cursed capstone gates (Mega A step 4)** — all 10 chains here run two or more steps past `unlock_trinkets_hub` except the two standalone leaves, so all 10 now end behind ONE mandatory cursed gate spliced between the chain's deepest leaf and its old parent (the capstone's `parent` field is the only existing field the step rewrote). 10 gates: `sk8t_gate_1..10`, `cost:1`, `cursed:true`, `-0.02` each, built with **`skillTreeGlobalDebuffEffects`** from `skilltree-general.js` (universal across classes — the engine has no `'ALL'` classId wildcard). This file has twice any sibling's gate count, so unlike the other three it splits them across **two** stats — `sk8t_gate_1..5` on `speed`, `sk8t_gate_6..10` on `boltSpeed`, `-0.10` apiece — keeping every per-(classId, stat) worst-case sum well inside the `[-0.25, 0.25]` clamp instead of parking a single stat at `-0.20`.
- Full trinket/node table and verification harness output (id-collision check against the full `TRINKETS` table, reachability/no-cycles/no-orphans/no-duplicate-ids over the 26 nodes, `effect.category==='trinket'`+`effect.id` validity, and a grep cross-check that every `sk8t_` id has a `recalcPlayerStats`/combat/familiar wiring): `feature-research/phase8-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-unlocks-trinkets.md`.

### achievements/skilltree-unlocks-starroom.js

*(Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4 — a small 3-node linear chain hanging off the existing `unlock_hub`, unrelated to the sibling `skilltree-unlocks-{stars,items,trinkets,familiars}.js` "unlock a locked X" files despite the similar filename: this one raises the star **room's** per-floor appearance odds, not any pickup/item/trinket/familiar unlock. Pure data appended onto `skilltree.js`'s `SKILL_TREE_NODES`/`SKILL_TREE_NODES_BY_ID`, same append pattern as every other `skilltree-*.js` file; no engine function changed. Loaded in `index.html` after `achievements/skilltree.js` (must load after, since it pushes onto `SKILL_TREE_NODES`) and before `js/systems/dungeon.js`.)*

- **`SKILL_TREE_STARROOM_NODES`** — 3 nodes, one linear chain: `unlock_hub → unlock_starroom_1 → unlock_starroom_2 → unlock_starroom_3`. Each is `{id, parent, cost:1, name, desc, effect:null}`.
- **`effect:null`** — unlike most skill-tree leaves, these have no engine-recognized `effect`/`effects` shape the generic buy/apply pipeline (`applySkillTreeUnlockEffect`) knows how to handle; there is no `unlockedStars`-style bucket for "star room chance." `effect:null` is the same pattern `unlock_stars_hub` (a pure-gating node) uses, purely so the generic skill-tree buy/sell/render code doesn't choke on an unrecognized effect type. The actual bonus is read directly by `achievements/core.js`'s `getStarRoomChanceBonus()` via `isSkillNodeOwned()`, and applied by `dungeon.js`'s `generateDungeon()` when rolling the star room's chance for the floor.
- Each owned node adds `+0.25` to the star room's base chance (`DUNGEON_CONFIG.specialChances.star`, 0.25 — see `dungeon.js`'s entry below), so owning all three plus the base chance reaches exactly `1.0` (still defensively clamped with `Math.min(1, ...)` at the call site in `getStarRoomChanceBonus`/`generateDungeon`).
- Names/costs: `unlock_starroom_1` "Stargazer's Charm", `unlock_starroom_2` "Wishing Star", `unlock_starroom_3` "Celestial Beacon" — each `cost:1`.

### achievements/skilltree-characters-4a.js … -4e.js — Phase 10 Part B (25 more nodes/character)

*(5 files, 5 characters each, same `build(classId, defs)`-registration convention throughout: each file is a self-contained IIFE that pushes its group's nodes straight onto `SKILL_TREE_NODES`/`SKILL_TREE_NODES_BY_ID`. Loaded in `index.html` immediately after `skilltree-characters-3.js`. Full per-group design notes and cap-safety audits: `feature-research/phase10-metaprogression/audit-skilltree-group{1-5}.md`.)*

### achievements/skilltree-characters-5a.js … -5e.js — Phase 11 item 3 (50 more nodes/character, redesigned)

*(Same 5-file/5-characters-each split and `build(classId, defs)` convention as the `4a`-`4e` files above; 1250 nodes total, generated from `feature-research/phase11-skilltree-v2/`'s scratch generator rather than hand-authored — see that phase's `scope.md` for the full design log.)*

- **Topology per character**: exactly 5 branches (`m/n/o/p/q`), 10 nodes deep each — a cursed gate opener, two 3-node reward subpaths, a 2-node spine, and a cost-2 capstone. Branches `m/n/o/q` are plain stat branches (core stats only — melee/ranged damage, speed, critChance, luck, rangeTiles, boltSpeed, magnetRadius; deliberately **no status-effect chance stats** in this batch). Branch `p` ("Technique") is the one new per-character mechanic: a real Braced-vs-Reckless build choice using `uniqueField:'damageTakenMult'` (safely seeded as a real number for every class in `entities.js`'s `Player` constructor, so it needed no per-class engine work). 125 cursed gate nodes total (5/character).
- **Cap-safety**: the generator's final pass (`capacityFit` in `gen_phase11b.js`) computes each character's own new positive contribution per `(classId, stat)`, looks up the exact pre-existing sum for that pair from every OTHER skill-tree file, and scales down ONLY the stats that would actually break `SKILL_TREE_STAT_CAP` once stacked — leaving every stat with headroom untouched. Result: this batch contributes **zero** new stat-cap overages; the 11 (classId,stat) pairs that remain over cap anywhere in the full tree are confirmed 100% pre-existing (inherited from Phases 8c/9/10, predating this pass).

### data/items-6.js + achievements/skilltree-unlocks-items-2.js — Phase 11 item 4 (2nd item-unlock branch)

*(15 new `locked:true` passive items, `sk11i_`-prefixed, appended to `ITEMS` in `data/items-6.js`; unlocked one-for-one by leaf nodes under a new hub, `unlock_items2_hub` ("Sealed Reliquary"), sibling to Phase 8e's `unlock_items_hub`. Same generic gating as every other locked item — `room.js`'s `!i.locked || isItemUnlocked(i.id)` pool filter, no new engine code. `data/items-6.js` loaded in `index.html` right after `items-5.js`; `skilltree-unlocks-items-2.js` loaded right after `skilltree-unlocks-items.js`.)*

- **Topology**: hub + 6 free single-node caches (Luck/speed/pierce/magnet/lifesteal/shop-discount — cheap, broadly useful, no gate) + two 3-5-node chains each behind its own cursed gate (chain A: stun→venom→crit, gated by a universal `-2% dodgeChance`; chain B: fear→bomb-radius→dodge→crit-multiplier→on-kill-heal, gated by a universal `-2% fearChance`), both gates built with `skillTreeGlobalDebuffEffects` (`skilltree-general.js`) the same way every other cursed unlock-branch gate in the game is.
- **Stat wiring**: every item is one appended `+ amount * (p.sk11i_id || 0)` term on the matching stat's existing formula line in `js/systems/items-1.js`'s `recalcPlayerStats` (tagged `// Phase 11 item 4` at each site) — the exact same generic per-item-id counting convention `sk8i_`/every other passive item uses; no new formula lines, no `applyPassiveEffect` special-casing needed since none of the 15 is a heart-container or other non-formula effect.
- Full node/item table, generator scripts, and cap-safety verification output: `feature-research/phase11-skilltree-v2/scope.md` (Item 3 + Item 4 sections).

# Part 5 — systems/ (dungeon, room, attack layers, combat)

## systems/ (part 1) — dungeon generation, room population, the layered-attack system, and core combat

### dungeon.js — procedural map graph generation

Header comment summary: the dungeon is built on a shared BLOCK grid (each block is `BLOCK` tiles square). Every room reserves the exact set of blocks its shape (polyomino `mask`) occupies, so a room's size actually shapes the map. Doors are per-BLOCK, not per-room: every block edge that faces *outside* the room's own shape is a door-slot candidate; an edge facing another block of the *same* room is an interior opening, not a candidate. Two rooms that end up touching get a door wherever both sides still have open, unpaired, un-disabled slots — so a wide shared wall between two ordinary rooms can end up with several doors — except "special" rooms (boss/treasure/shop/secret/petshop/curse/sacrifice/vault/challenge/crystal/sombra/star/cpathgate), which are always capped at exactly one entrance regardless of how many blocks they span.

Compact template fields consumed here (produced by room-editor.html): `m` (mask, required), `f` (allowed floor indices, 0-based, optional), `d` (disabled door sides — either a legacy direction string like `"NW"` disabling that whole facing across the template, or an array of `[col,row,dirLetters]` per-block entries), `p` (path tag: `'C'` means C-branch exclusive), `s` (spawners, consumed by room.js).

**Module state / constants**
- `DIRS` — the 4 compass directions as `{d,o,dx,dy}` (`d`=this direction, `o`=opposite).
- `SPECIAL_ROOM_TYPES` (Set) — every room type capped at exactly 1 door: boss, treasure, shop, secret, petshop, curse, sacrifice, vault, challenge, crystal, sombra, star, cpathgate, shrine, — Phase 4 overhaul — arcade, — Phase 7a — planetarium (the D-branch gate, matching cpathgate's membership in both sets exactly), and — **Secret Room Revamp Slice 3** — `supersecret` (see below; despite the name it's still capped at 1 door same as everything else in this set — only `secret` itself was widened past 1, via a post-placement override rather than membership in this set). Centralizing this avoids a long `type==='x'||...` chain scattered through the code.
- `MANDATORY_ROOM_TYPES` (array) — **updated (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)**: `['boss', 'treasure', 'shop', 'secret', 'supersecret']`, the 5 room types `generateDungeon` always attaches on every floor (boss/treasure/shop via `attachSpecial`'s guaranteed-fallback path; secret via `attachSecretRoom`'s widening-retry best-position scan; supersecret via `attachSuperSecretRoom`, now wired in as of Slice 4 — see below). Still purely documentation/intent — nothing iterates the array itself — but it's the canonical list of the 5 attaches whose success is checked by `generateDungeon`'s bounded retry loop (see point 9 below).
- `AUTO_OPEN_ROOM_TYPES` (Set) — room types whose doors start open at creation: start, secret, **supersecret** (Slice 3), petshop, curse, sacrifice, challenge, crystal, sombra, cpathgate, planetarium (Phase 7a), shrine. Everything else (normal/boss/treasure/shop/vault, and — Phase 4 overhaul — arcade) starts locked (normal/boss lock behind combat via the safety net in room.js's `populateRoom`; treasure/shop/vault lock behind a key via combat.js's `keyLockedRoomFor`; arcade locks behind a flat coin toll via combat.js's `coinLockedRoomFor`/`tryUnlockCoinDoor` — the one special type that is neither auto-open nor key-locked).
- `let _roomIdSeq = 1` — monotonically-incrementing room id counter, consumed by `makeRoomInstance`.
- `DUNGEON_CONFIG` (object) — **new (dungeon-generation rework)**: centralizes every tunable spawn-odds/room-count number that used to be a literal scattered through `generateDungeon`. Structural/progression gates (the floor-1 C-branch gate, floor-2 D-branch gate, floorfeature's `floorNum > OLD_MAIN_ROUTE_FINAL_FLOOR` gate, crystal/sombra's every-other-floor gate, the floorNum 8-11 second-boss-room gate) are deliberately **not** in it — those are progression logic, not spawn-odds tuning, and stay as explicit `floorNum`/path conditions in `generateDungeon`. Fields:
  - `roomCount: {base:12, perFloor:2, spread:4, floorMin:6}` — the per-floor NORMAL room target is now a random int in `[min,max]` (not a fixed number), so back-to-back generations of the same floor vary in size instead of being identical every time: `min = base + perFloor*floorNum - spread/2`, `max = base + perFloor*floorNum + spread/2`, both clamped so `min >= floorMin`. `base`/`perFloor` reproduce the *old* fixed formula's midpoint exactly (old: `targetNormal = 10 + 2*(floorNum+1) = 12 + 2*floorNum`; at floorNum=0 that's 12, matching `base=12`'s midpoint precisely) — this pass widens the target into a range, it doesn't change the game's overall room-count scale.
  - `radiusBase:8, radiusPerFloor:1, radiusHeadroom:2` — map extent (`radius = radiusBase + radiusPerFloor*floorNum + radiusHeadroom`). Same base shape as the old fixed `8 + floorNum`, plus a fixed `+2` headroom term so the placement loop has room to reach the new range's `max` (not just the old formula's single midpoint) without starving.
  - `specialBudget: {base:3, perFloors:4, max:6}` — **now vestigial (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)**: pre-Slice-4 this capped how many of the 9 *discretionary* special room types could attach on one floor. Slice 4 replaced 8 of those 9 (all but `star`) with the exactly-one-per-group guarantee described under `specialChances` just below, which can never exceed 2 total attaches (1 from group A + 1 from group B) — always within even this field's minimum value of 3 — so the field is kept unchanged (per the Slice 4 plan) but is no longer read anywhere in `generateDungeon`.
  - `specialChances` — **Floor Generation Revamp (Slice 4)**: `petshop:0.25, curse:0.50, sacrifice:0.50, vault:0.10, challenge:0.25, star:0.25, shrine:0.20, arcade:0.18, miniboss:0.25`. 8 of these 9 types no longer roll independently: curse/sacrifice/challenge/miniboss ("group A") and shrine/petshop/vault/arcade ("group B") each guarantee **exactly one** member per floor, chosen by a single normalized-weight draw (`weightedGroupPick`, see `generateDungeon` below) that uses these numbers as relative weights within the group, not as independent coin-flip odds. `star` is the one exception — it still rolls independently via `Util.chance`, but its base chance dropped `0.30 -> 0.25` since it can now also be boosted by the `skilltree-unlocks-starroom.js` mini-tree (`achievements/core.js`'s `getStarRoomChanceBonus()`, up to +0.75, summed and clamped to 1.0 total at the call site).
  - `totalRoomCap: {base:15, perFloor:2, max:30}` / `tileFootprintCap: {base:30, perFloor:4, max:50}` — **new (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)**: overall per-floor caps used only to bound `generateDungeon`'s retry loop (see point 9 below), each computed as `min(max, base + perFloor*floorNum)`. `totalRoomTarget` bounds how many total rooms (normal + all specials) the floor aims for when deriving `targetNormal`; `footprintCap` bounds the summed `roomBlockCells(...).length` across every placed room once the 5 mandatory + 2 guaranteed-group specials are attached. Neither cap is a hard ceiling enforced by rejecting placements mid-generation — they only decide whether a generation attempt is accepted as-is or retried (up to `MAX_GRAPH_ATTEMPTS`).

**`blockKey(x, y)`** → `x + ',' + y`. String key for the `blockGrid`/pit `Map`s used throughout. Called everywhere a block-grid or per-cell lookup happens in this file.

**`isDoorDisabled(template, col, row, dir)`** → boolean. Reads `template.d`. If it's a string, checks `.includes(dir)` (legacy whole-facing disable). If it's an array, scans entries `[col, row, dirLetters]` for one matching this `(col,row)` whose `dirLetters` includes `dir`. Returns `false` if the template has no `d` at all. Called by `computeDoorSlots` and `tryPlaceAdjacent`.

**`obstacleAllowedOnFloor(kind, floorNum, floorPath)`** — THOROUGH. Obstacle-kind floor/path gating, deliberately independent of which template an obstacle kind happens to be baked into, so it retroactively applies to every ROOM_TEMPLATES entry (hand-authored or procedural) without editing any of them. **Procedural room generation batch 1** replaced the former hardcoded if-chain (sandtrap/cactus/mud/current\*/thornbush) with a table lookup — the rules now live as `floorRules` on the `OBSTACLES` entry itself (see `data/collectibles.js` above), so adding or retuning a gate is a data edit, never a code edit. Logic:
  - Reads `OBSTACLES[kind].floorRules`. Missing/empty → `true` (unrestricted; the default for most kinds).
  - Otherwise returns `true` iff **some** rule in the array matches. A rule matches when every constraint it declares holds: `minFloor` ≤ `floorNum`, `floorNum` ≤ `maxFloor` (both inclusive, 0-indexed engine `floorNum`, not HUD floor), `floorPath === path`, `floorPath !== pathExclude`. Constraints the rule omits are not checked, so `[{ path:'C' }]` means "any C floor" and `[{ minFloor:15, maxFloor:16 }]` means "floors 15-16 on any path". Multiple rules OR together (`mud` = main-path floors 2-3 **or** C-branch floors 4-5).
  - Returns `false` if the kind has rules and none matched.
  Reads global `OBSTACLES`. Called only from `templateAllowsFloor`. Signature unchanged, so the call site needed no edit.

**`templateAllowsFloor(tmpl, floorNum)`** — THOROUGH. Gate that decides whether a ROOM_TEMPLATES entry is eligible for a given floor:
  1. `if (tmpl.f && !tmpl.f.includes(floorNum)) return false;` — respects the template's own explicit floor list.
  2. `const floorPath = currentFloorPath();` then `if (tmpl.p === 'C' && floorPath !== 'C') return false;` — a template tagged `p:'C'` is C-branch exclusive.
  3. If `tmpl.s` (spawners) exists, scans every spawner entry; for any obstacle spawner (`sp[2] === 'o'`) whose `obstacleAllowedOnFloor(sp[3], floorNum, floorPath)` returns false, the whole template is rejected. This is how a template that merely *contains* a path/floor-exclusive obstacle spawner gets excluded on floors/paths where that obstacle can't appear, without the template author having to separately set `f`/`p`.
  Reads: `currentFloorPath()` (defined below, or in room.js — see note), `obstacleAllowedOnFloor`. Called by `pickMaskForType`, `attachSecretRoom`, `attachSuperSecretRoom` (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3), `attachSpecial`, `attachNextTo` — i.e. every place a template pool is filtered before picking.

**`computeDoorSlots(mask, originBx, originBy, template, room)`** — THOROUGH. For every occupied cell `(c,r)` in `mask`, for every one of the 4 `DIRS`, checks whether the neighboring cell in that direction is *interior* (in-bounds and also occupied by the mask) — if so, skip (no door slot there, it's inside the room's own shape). Otherwise pushes a slot object: `{ room, localCol, localRow, dir, bx, by, disabled, type:null, pairedSlot:null, opened:false, cells:null }`, where `bx/by` are the slot's absolute block coordinates (`originBx+c`, `originBy+r`) and `disabled` comes from `isDoorDisabled`. Returns the array of slots. This is the per-block door-eligibility computation the whole doors system is built on. Called by `makeRoomInstance`.

**`connectDoorSlots(a, b, type)`** — mutates: sets `a.type=b.type=type`, `a.pairedSlot=b`, `b.pairedSlot=a`. The only place two slots actually become "one door."

**`countRoomConnections(room)`** → number of *distinct* other rooms `room` has any paired door to (a Set of `pairedSlot.room.id`, so multiple doors to the same neighbor still count once). Called by `connectRoomDoors`.

**`connectRoomDoors(room, blockGrid, rooms, doorType)`** — THOROUGH. Called right after a room is placed to wire up doors to whatever it now touches:
  1. Bails immediately if `countRoomConnections(room) >= room.maxDoors`.
  2. Builds a `candidates` list: for every open (`!disabled && !pairedSlot`) slot on `room`, looks up the block on the far side in `blockGrid`; if it belongs to a different room, finds that other room's matching opposite-facing open slot at the same cell; if found, adds `{slot, oppSlot, other}`.
  3. If `room.maxDoors < Infinity` (a special room), shuffles the candidates — so which single entrance a special room gets isn't always whichever slot the mask happened to scan first (north/west-biased).
  4. Iterates candidates, connecting each pair via `connectDoorSlots` unless doing so would push `room` over its own cap OR push the far room over *its* own cap (checked from both ends, so neither side can be forced over its limit by the other's placement).
  Reads `blockKey`, `DIRS`, `Util.shuffle`. Mutates door slots via `connectDoorSlots`. Called by `tryPlaceAdjacent`. **Secret Room Revamp Slice 3**: no longer called by `attachSecretRoom` — secret/supersecret rooms now wire their doors via the new `connectSecretRoomDoors` instead (see below), because a widened secret room needs one door per *distinct touching neighbor* up to a dynamically-computed cap, not the single shuffled-candidate connection this generic function makes.

**`makeRoomInstance(type, originBx, originBy, mask, template)`** — constructs and returns a full room node object: `id` (from `_roomIdSeq++`), `type`, `gx/gy` (origin block), `shape:{mask}`, `template`, `doorSlots` (computed via `computeDoorSlots`), `tiles:null` (built lazily by room.js's `ensureRoomBuilt`), `doorsOpen: AUTO_OPEN_ROOM_TYPES.has(type)`, various state flags (`discovered/seen/revealed/visited/cleared` — `cleared` is `true` only for `type==='start'`), `populated:false`, empty content arrays (`enemies/obstacles/pickups/chests/itemPedestals`), `shopSlots:null`, `bossDefeated:false`, `stairsSpot:null`, `keyToastCooldown:0`, and `maxDoors: SPECIAL_ROOM_TYPES.has(type) ? 1 : Infinity`. Called by every placement function in this file (`tryPlaceAdjacent`, `attachSecretRoom`, `attachSuperSecretRoom`, `generateDungeon`'s start room, `attachSpecial`'s fallback loop). **Secret Room Revamp Slice 3 note**: `attachSecretRoom` still gets its initial `maxDoors` of `1` from this function (since `'secret'` is in `SPECIAL_ROOM_TYPES`), but then directly overwrites `room.maxDoors` post-construction with the actual distinct-touching-neighbor count (clamped 2-4, or down to 1 in the rare fallback case) — a deliberate judgment call to avoid threading a new parameter through this shared constructor for one caller's use case.

**`roomBlockCells(room)`** → array of `{bx,by}` for every occupied mask cell, in absolute block coordinates. Called by `canPlace`, `commitPlace`, `attachSecretRoom`, and indirectly by `touchingRoomIds` (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3, see below).

**`touchingRoomIds(blockGrid, candidate)`** — **new (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3)** → `Set` of distinct room ids that `candidate` (an unplaced room instance) would be adjacent to if placed at its current position. For every cell in `roomBlockCells(candidate)`, checks all 4 `DIRS` neighbors in `blockGrid`; any neighbor belonging to a different, already-placed room has its id added to the set. This is the building block for both the widened-secret-room touch-count constraint (2-4 neighbors) and supersecret's opposite constraint (exactly 1 neighbor). Called by `scanSecretPlacement`.

**`PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES`** — **new (procedural-room-generation batch 4), extended (batch 5)** `Set` of the room types that are fully procedural and never template-backed: `normal` (batch 3), `boss`/`miniboss`/`floorfeature` (batch 4), and — as of batch 5 — every remaining template-backed type: `shop`, `treasure`, `petshop`, `shrine`, `vault`, `karma`, `arcade`, `curse`, `sacrifice`, `challenge`, `bosschallenge`, `crystal`, `sombra`, `mirror`, `secret`, `supersecret`, `star`, `start`, `cpathgate`, `planetarium`. `ROOM_TEMPLATES` is therefore now dead data for dungeon generation (the room editor and `tools/lint-room-templates.js` still read it). Read by `pickMaskForType`, `procgenTemplatePoolFor`, `procgenMaskFor`, `procgenSecretPick`.

**Template data no longer shipped to the game (batch 6)** — because every type `generateDungeon` produces is in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES`, the hand-authored template arrays are dead weight in the real runtime, so `index.html` no longer loads 11 of the 13 `js/data/roomTemplates/*.js` files: `normal-1.js`, `normal-2.js`, `normal-3.js`, `normal-4.js`, `firecolors.js`, `dnbfly-rooms.js`, `floorfeature.js`, `miniboss.js`, `stage4-6-floorfeature.js`, `stage7-9-floorfeature.js`, `stage10-13-floorfeature.js` (~2200 template objects that were parsed and held in memory for nothing). The files stay on disk — `room-editor.html` still loads all 12 non-wavearena files for the authoring UI, and `tools/lint-room-templates.js` loads them through its own `vm` sandbox; neither is affected by the `index.html` change. Only two files remain in `index.html`, and only for wave defense: `core.js` (declares `const ROOM_TEMPLATES`, which `wavearena.js` mutates and therefore requires to exist first) and `wavearena.js` (read live by `wavedefense.js`'s `wdWaveArenaPool` → `ROOM_TEMPLATES.wavearena`). `core.js` also still seeds real arrays for `start`/`boss`/`treasure`/`shop`/`secret`/`supersecret`/`petshop`/`curse`/`sacrifice`/`vault`/`challenge`/`crystal`/`sombra`/`shrine` — every one of those keys is in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES`, so that data is harmless leftover that nothing in dungeon generation reads. The `ROOM_TEMPLATES[type] || []` fallback branches inside `pickMaskForType`, `procgenTemplatePoolFor` and `procgenSecretPick` are deliberately kept: they are correctly guarded, degrade to an empty pool for any type whose data file is now absent, and are unreachable from `generateDungeon` regardless.

**`procgenTemplatePoolFor(type, floorNum)`** — **new (batch 4)** → array. For a type in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES` returns `[null]` (no template is ever consulted); otherwise the original behaviour — `ROOM_TEMPLATES[type]` filtered through `templateAllowsFloor`, shuffled, or `[null]` when empty. Called by `generateDungeon`'s `attachSpecial` and `attachNextTo`.

**`procgenMaskFor(type, tmpl, fallbackMask)`** — **new (batch 4)** → mask. For a type in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES` returns `pickProceduralMask(type).mask` (a fresh roll on every placement attempt, so retries also retry the shape); otherwise `tmpl.m` if a template was given, else `fallbackMask` (the caller's `chooseShapeForNode({type}).mask` or, in the last-resort pass, `[[1]]`). Called by `attachSpecial` (both passes) and `attachNextTo`. These two helpers exist because `boss`/`miniboss`/`floorfeature` rooms are placed by `attachSpecial`/`attachNextTo`, which build their own template pools and never call `pickMaskForType` — extending `pickMaskForType` alone would not have routed them.

**`pickMaskForType(type, floorNum)`** → `{mask, template}`. First line: any `type` in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES` (`normal` since batch 3; `boss`/`miniboss`/`floorfeature` since batch 4) returns `pickProceduralMask(type)` (procgen-rooms.js), i.e. a procedural mask with `template:null`, so those rooms never use a `ROOM_TEMPLATES` entry any more and `populateRoom`'s existing `node.template ? populateRoomFromTemplate : populateRoomProcedural` dispatch routes them all to `populateRoomProcedural`. `pickProceduralMask` itself forces a single-block mask for any type outside `PROCGEN_FREE_ROOM_TYPES` — which since the visual-overhaul batch A shape pass is `normal`/`floorfeature`/`boss`/`miniboss`, so all four now get the full weighted multi-block variety and only the fixture/special types are pinned to 1 block. All other types fall through to the original behaviour: filters `ROOM_TEMPLATES[type]` through `templateAllowsFloor`; if any survive, picks one via `Util.choice` and returns its mask+template; otherwise falls back to `chooseShapeForNode({type})` (room.js) with `template:null`. Reads global `ROOM_TEMPLATES`. Called by `generateDungeon` (for `start` and repeatedly for `normal` rooms).

**`canPlace(blockGrid, room, radius)`** → boolean. `false` if the room has no cells, if any cell exceeds the Chebyshev `radius` bound (`Math.max(|bx|,|by|) > radius`), or if any cell is already occupied in `blockGrid`. Called by `tryPlaceAdjacent`, `attachSecretRoom`.

**`commitPlace(blockGrid, rooms, room)`** — mutates: adds `room` to the `rooms` Map keyed by id, and stamps every cell of `room` into `blockGrid` keyed by `blockKey`. Called by `tryPlaceAdjacent`, `attachSecretRoom`, `generateDungeon`.

**`tryPlaceAdjacent(blockGrid, rooms, fromRoom, dir, mask, template, type, radius)`** — THOROUGH. Attempts to attach a new room of the given `mask/template/type` to `fromRoom`'s `dir` side:
  1. Collects `fromRoom`'s own open door slots facing `dir` (`!disabled && !pairedSlot`), shuffled.
  2. Computes the new mask's own boundary cells that face the opposite direction (`dir.o`) and aren't door-disabled there, also shuffled.
  3. For every `(fromSlot, maskBoundaryCell)` pairing (nested loop, from-slots outer), computes the candidate room's origin so that boundary cell lands directly across from the from-slot, builds the room via `makeRoomInstance`, and if `canPlace` succeeds, commits it (`commitPlace`) and wires its doors via `connectRoomDoors(candidate, blockGrid, rooms, 'normal')`, returning the new room immediately (first successful placement wins — this is how the frontier-growth BFS-ish loop in `generateDungeon` places rooms one attempt at a time).
  4. Returns `null` if nothing fit.
  Called by `generateDungeon`'s normal-room growth loop, `attachSpecial`, and `attachNextTo`.

**`procgenSecretPick(type, floorNum)`** — **new (procedural-room-generation batch 5)** → `{pick, mask}`. The template/mask resolution that `attachSecretRoom` and `attachSuperSecretRoom` each used to inline. For a type in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES` (both `secret` and `supersecret` are, as of batch 5) returns `{pick:null, mask: pickProceduralMask(type).mask}` — i.e. the single-block procedural mask, never a template. Otherwise the original behaviour: `ROOM_TEMPLATES[type]` filtered through `templateAllowsFloor`, one entry via `Util.choice`, mask `pick.m`, falling back to `{pick:null, mask:[[1]]}` when the pool is empty. This helper exists because these two attach functions bypass `pickMaskForType`/`procgenTemplatePoolFor` entirely (they need a mask *before* the best-position scan), so extending only those would have left secret/supersecret rooms template-backed.

**`scanSecretPlacement(blockGrid, searchRadius, placeRadius, mask, pick, minTouch, maxTouch, type)`** — **rewritten (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3)**, signature grew 3 new trailing params. The best-position scan logic factored out of `attachSecretRoom`/`attachSuperSecretRoom` so it can be retried at a wider radius. Scans every `(ox,oy)` in `[-searchRadius,searchRadius]^2`, builds a candidate room instance of the given `type` there, and if `canPlace(blockGrid, candidate, placeRadius)` succeeds, computes `touching = touchingRoomIds(blockGrid, candidate)` and **filters out any candidate whose `touching.size` falls outside `[minTouch, maxTouch]`** — this is the new part; previously every placeable candidate was scored regardless of touch count. Surviving candidates are scored by `touching.size + RNG.random()*0.5` (small jitter to break ties without always favoring the first-scanned position) and the best-scoring one is returned as `{ room: candidate, touching }` (unplaced — not yet committed), or `null` if nothing in range satisfied the touch-count filter. Called by `attachSecretRoom` (with `minTouch/maxTouch` of `2/4`, then a fallback pass of `1/Infinity`) and `attachSuperSecretRoom` (with `minTouch/maxTouch` of `1/1`).

**`connectSecretRoomDoors(room, blockGrid, rooms, doorType, touchIds)`** — **new (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3)**. Replaces `connectRoomDoors` for secret/supersecret rooms, because those need one door connected to *each distinct touching neighbor* (up to `room.maxDoors`), not just one shuffled candidate total. For every id in `touchIds`, collects that neighbor's open, matching door-slot candidates (mirroring `connectRoomDoors`'s candidate-finding logic but grouped per-neighbor), shuffles the neighbor order, then connects one door per neighbor via `connectDoorSlots(slot, oppSlot, doorType)` until `room.maxDoors` is reached — also respecting the neighbor's own `maxDoors` cap so a normal room's door budget can't be forced over its limit by a secret room reaching for it. Used by both `attachSecretRoom` (with `doorType:'secret'`) and `attachSuperSecretRoom` (with `doorType:'supersecret'`, a deliberately distinct doorType string — see the dormant-gap note under `attachSuperSecretRoom` below).

**`attachSecretRoom(rooms, blockGrid, radius, floorNum)`** — **batch 5**: gets its `{pick, mask}` from `procgenSecretPick('secret', floorNum)`, which now always returns `pick:null` and a procedural single-block mask (`secret` is in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES`); previously it picked a secret-room template (filtered by `templateAllowsFloor`) or fell back to a bare `[[1]]` mask. **Hardened (dungeon-generation rework)**: previously this was a single `scanSecretPlacement`-equivalent scan at the base `radius` — if nothing scored on that one pass (rare, but a real gap since secret is one of the 4 `MANDATORY_ROOM_TYPES`), the floor silently shipped with no secret room at all. Now it retries `scanSecretPlacement` at `[radius, radius+2, radius+4]` (both the search window and the `canPlace` bound widen together) and stops at the first radius that finds a candidate; only if all three attempts come up empty does it give up (same "silently skip" behavior as before, now just a much rarer edge case). **Widened (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3)**: the primary scan now requires the winning candidate to touch **2 to 4** distinct existing rooms (`minTouch:2, maxTouch:4`), so a secret room reads as genuinely secret — reachable via more than one hidden wall — instead of always having exactly one. If the primary `2-4` scan finds nothing across all three radii, the whole retry ladder runs again with `minTouch:1, maxTouch:Infinity` as a graceful fallback (so secret rooms still never fail to generate outright — a 1-touch secret room is a legal, if less interesting, outcome). Once a candidate is found, `room.maxDoors` is overwritten to `Math.min(4, Math.max(1, touchIds.size))` (see `makeRoomInstance`'s note above on why this is a direct mutation rather than a constructor parameter), then commits it (`commitPlace`) and wires doors via the new `connectSecretRoomDoors(best, blockGrid, rooms, 'secret', touchIds)` — one hidden-wall door per distinct touching neighbor, up to the computed cap. Returns the placed room or `null`. Called once by `generateDungeon`.

**`attachSuperSecretRoom(rooms, blockGrid, radius, floorNum)`** — **new (Secret Room Revamp Slice 3)**. Mirrors `attachSecretRoom`'s structure exactly, but with the opposite touch constraint: the winning candidate must touch **exactly 1** existing room (`scanSecretPlacement(..., 1, 1, 'supersecret')`), no widening fallback needed since the constraint is already the narrowest possible (any placeable room touches at least 1 neighbor once past the very first room). **Batch 5**: mask/template now come from `procgenSecretPick('supersecret', floorNum)` — always `pick:null` plus a procedural single-block mask, since `supersecret` is in `PROCGEN_ROUTED_ROOM_TYPES`; it previously picked from `ROOM_TEMPLATES.supersecret` (filtered by `templateAllowsFloor`, falling back to `[[1]]` if the pool was empty for this floor). `maxDoors` stays at its `makeRoomInstance`-assigned `1` (supersecret is in `SPECIAL_ROOM_TYPES`, and the touch constraint guarantees exactly 1 neighbor anyway, so no override is needed the way `attachSecretRoom` needs one). Wires its single door via `connectSecretRoomDoors(best, blockGrid, rooms, 'supersecret', touchIds)`, using **`'supersecret'` as a doorType distinct from `'secret'`** — this is a deliberate choice (the plan's checks are worded as "also match `'supersecret'`," which only makes sense if it isn't already matching `'secret'`). **Floor Generation Revamp (Slice 4)**: this function is now called from `generateDungeon` (inside the §9 retry loop, alongside `attachSecretRoom`, as one of the 5 `MANDATORY_ROOM_TYPES` attaches), and the two places flagged in Slice 3 as not-yet-supersecret-aware have both been widened to match: combat-2.js's `checkDoorTransition` now also matches `'supersecret'` when gating a walk through an opened hidden door, and this file's own `generateDungeon` BFS-distance and `degree()` helpers now exclude both `'secret'` and `'supersecret'` doors from graph-distance/leaf calculations (previously-dormant gap, now fixed). Returns the placed room or `null`. Called once by `generateDungeon`.

**`generateDungeon(floorNum)`** — THOROUGH, the top-level entry point. Algorithm:
  1. Computes this floor's normal-room range from `DUNGEON_CONFIG.roomCount`: `minNormal = max(floorMin, round(base + perFloor*floorNum - spread/2))`, `maxNormal = max(minNormal, round(base + perFloor*floorNum + spread/2))`.
  2. `radius = DUNGEON_CONFIG.radiusBase + DUNGEON_CONFIG.radiusPerFloor*floorNum + DUNGEON_CONFIG.radiusHeadroom` — grows every floor (not just every other), with fixed headroom so the placement loop can reach `maxNormal`, not just the old formula's single midpoint.
  3. Places the start room at block `(0,0)` via `pickMaskForType('start', floorNum)` + `makeRoomInstance` + `commitPlace`.
  4. `targetNormal = Util.randi(minNormal, maxNormal)` — **changed (dungeon-generation rework)**: this floor's actual generation target is now a random int within the range, not a fixed formula result, so repeated generations of the same floor vary in room count instead of always being identical.
  5. Frontier-growth loop (bounded by `guard < 3000`): picks a random room from the growing `frontier` array; for each of the 4 shuffled directions, with 60% probability (the code is `if (Math.random() >= 0.6) continue;`, i.e. a 60% chance to attempt), picks a normal-type mask/template via `pickMaskForType` and tries `tryPlaceAdjacent`; on success pushes the new room onto the frontier and increments `normalCount`. If a room produced no successful placement in any direction, it's spliced out of the frontier (dead branch pruning).
  6. **New (dungeon-generation rework) — undersized-floor hardening**: if `normalCount < minNormal` after the loop (e.g. the 3000-attempt guard tripped before reaching even the minimum), runs the *same* frontier-growth loop **once more** with `radius+3` and a reset frontier (every existing start/normal room) and guard counter, continuing to grow `normalCount` toward `targetNormal`. If it's still short after this one retry, the floor ships undersized anyway — the existing 3000-attempt guard already prevents an infinite loop, so a single bounded retry is the extent of the hardening (not a retry-until-success loop).
  7. Picks one random normal room and flags `.forceSwarm = true` — every floor forces exactly one group of 5 low-HP Swarmer DNBs into a single random normal room, consumed later by room.js's `populateRoom`.
  8. **New (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)** — computes `totalRoomTarget = min(DUNGEON_CONFIG.totalRoomCap.max, base + perFloor*floorNum)` and `footprintCap = min(DUNGEON_CONFIG.tileFootprintCap.max, base + perFloor*floorNum)` from the two new `DUNGEON_CONFIG` fields, then decides this floor's group picks up front via a local `weightedGroupPick(types)` helper (normalizes `DUNGEON_CONFIG.specialChances` values across the given `types` into weights and draws one `RNG.random()`-based pick): `groupAType = weightedGroupPick(['curse','sacrifice','challenge','miniboss'])`, `groupBType = weightedGroupPick(['shrine','petshop','vault','arcade'])`, and `starRolled = Util.chance(min(1, DUNGEON_CONFIG.specialChances.star + getStarRoomChanceBonus()))` — all three decided before the frontier walk so `decidedSpecialCount = 5 + 2 = 7` (the 5 `MANDATORY_ROOM_TYPES` plus the 2 guaranteed group picks; `star` doesn't count here since it attaches separately) can be subtracted from `totalRoomTarget` to derive `targetNormal = min(maxNormal, max(minNormal, totalRoomTarget - decidedSpecialCount))`, which point 4's `Util.randi` used to derive on its own.
  9. **New (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4) — bounded retry loop**: the start-room placement, frontier-growth loop (points 5-7), BFS distances, and the 5 mandatory + 2 guaranteed-group attaches (points 11-12 below) are now all wrapped in a `for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_GRAPH_ATTEMPTS; attempt++)` loop (`MAX_GRAPH_ATTEMPTS = 5`), with `rooms`/`blockGrid`/`startRoom`/`distances` reset and rebuilt from scratch each attempt. After each attempt's 7 attaches, computes `footprintSum = sum of roomBlockCells(r).length across every placed room` and checks `ok = normalCount >= minNormal && bossNode && treasureNode && shopNode && secretNode && supersecretNode && groupANode && groupBNode && footprintSum <= footprintCap`; breaks out on the first `ok` attempt or on the last attempt regardless (so the floor never fails to generate outright — a late attempt that still doesn't satisfy `ok` ships anyway, same "accept a rare shortfall" philosophy as the pre-Slice-4 hardening pass). Deliberately does **NOT** wrap: the crystal/sombra deal-room placement (point 15 below — it mutates live, non-idempotent `game` state such as `game.dealAlignment`, so re-running it on a retry would double-roll/corrupt that state), `star`'s attach (attached once, after the loop settles, using the `starRolled` decision from point 8), `cpathgateNode`/`planetariumNode`/`floorfeatureNode`/`secondBossNode` (all structural/progression gates keyed on `floorNum`, not chance, so retrying them serves no purpose).
  10. BFS from the start room (inside the retry loop) over paired doors, now excluding doors of type `'secret'` **or** `'supersecret'` (**Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4** — previously only `'secret'` was excluded, a dormant gap flagged in Slice 3 since `attachSuperSecretRoom` wasn't wired in yet; now that it is, both hidden-door types are excluded so distances reflect only the real traversable graph) to compute `distances` (room.id → hop count from start) — used to find "farthest leaves."
  11. Local helper `degree(room)` — count of distinct neighbors via non-secret, non-supersecret doors (same Slice 4 fix as the BFS exclusion just above). `farthestLeaves()` — every `normal` room with `degree===1` (a dead end), sorted by descending distance from start (farthest-first).
  12. Local helper `attachSpecial(type)` — for each floor number's farthest-first leaf, for each shuffled direction, for each entry in `procgenTemplatePoolFor(type, floorNum)`, tries `tryPlaceAdjacent` with `procgenMaskFor(type, tmpl, chooseShapeForNode({type}).mask)`; returns the first success. If nothing at any leaf fit, falls back to a last-resort pass over *every* room in the map with radius `+3`, same pool, with `[[1]]` as the fallback mask. **Changed (procedural-room-generation batch 4):** for `boss`/`miniboss`/`floorfeature` the pool is forced to `[null]` and the mask comes from `pickProceduralMask`, so those three types are now placed procedurally here rather than from `ROOM_TEMPLATES`.
  13. Inside the retry loop, attaches (in order) `bossNode`, `treasureNode`, `shopNode` via `attachSpecial`, `secretNode` via `attachSecretRoom`, and — **new (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)** — `supersecretNode` via `attachSuperSecretRoom`: these 5 are `MANDATORY_ROOM_TYPES`. Then attaches the two guaranteed group picks decided back in point 8: `groupANode = attachSpecial(groupAType)` and `groupBNode = attachSpecial(groupBType)`.
  14. **Rewritten (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4) — replaces the old discretionary special-room budget entirely.** The old model (independent `Util.chance` coin-flips for 9 types, capped by a shuffled-iteration `specialBudget` counter) is gone. Now, after the retry loop settles, the 8 named `*Node` variables for group A/B members are derived by a simple ternary against which type each group actually rolled in point 8: `curseNode = groupAType==='curse' ? groupANode : null` (and identically for `sacrificeNode`/`challengeNode`/`minibossNode` off `groupAType`, and `shrineNode`/`petshopNode`/`vaultNode`/`arcadeNode` off `groupBType`) — so exactly one of the 4 group-A names and exactly one of the 4 group-B names is ever non-null per floor, and every downstream consumer/return-value name is unchanged from before.
  15. `starNode` — **changed (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)**: attached via `starNode = starRolled ? attachSpecial('star') : null`, using the `starRolled` decision from point 8 (chance now `min(1, DUNGEON_CONFIG.specialChances.star + getStarRoomChanceBonus())`, base dropped 0.30→0.25 but boostable up to +0.75 by the `skilltree-unlocks-starroom.js` mini-tree). Attached **after** the retry loop settles, not inside it (see point 9's list of what's deliberately excluded from the loop).
  16. `cpathgateNode` — only on `floorNum === 1` (HUD Floor 2), the sole room in the game gated on a specific floor number rather than a coin flip. Always attaches when the floor is right (never randomly denied). Walking onto its pit calls `descend('C')` (game.js), diverting the run onto the 3C-10C branch. Outside the §9 retry loop (floor-number-keyed, not chance-keyed — see point 9).
  17. Local helper `attachNextTo(anchor, type)` — like `attachSpecial` but tries only the specific `anchor` room's free sides (no leaf search, no fallback) — returns `null` outright if nothing fits beside the anchor. Uses the same `procgenTemplatePoolFor`/`procgenMaskFor` pair (batch 4).
  18. Crystal/Sombra ("deal room") placement — **rewritten, QOL Slice F** (see the "Slice F — devil/crystal deal overhaul" section below for the full writeup): rolled on EVERY floor that has a `bossNode` (the old `everySecondFloor` odd-floorNum gate is gone), at most ONE of crystal/sombra ever spawns per floor (mutually exclusive by construction), chosen either by the run's `game.dealAlignment` lock or randomly via `Util.choice`. `bossNode.maxDoors` is still temporarily raised to 3 (for the single `attachNextTo` call) and restored to 1 afterward, same as before. **Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4**: explicitly outside the §9 retry loop (point 9) — it mutates live, non-idempotent `game` state (e.g. `game.dealAlignment`), so it must only ever run once per floor generation, after the loop has already settled on its final room graph.
  19. `secondBossNode` — attached via `attachSpecial('boss')` only on `floorNum` 8/9/10/11 (9A/9B..12A/12B in HUD terms) **and only when `currentFloorPath()` is null** — a bonus, optional fight on top of the floor's real superboss. Deliberately not on floors 13/14/15 (floorNum 12/13/14), which get a single boss room only. The `currentFloorPath()` guard is a **Phase 7a bug fix**: the condition used to test floorNum alone, so the C-branch's floorNum 8/9 (9C/10C) incidentally satisfied it and generated a bonus boss room that path was never meant to have — and Phase 7a's new C floors (11C/12C) plus the whole D-branch (floorNum 3-9) would have widened the collision. The mechanic is main-route-only by design (it exists because 9A/9B..12A/12B each have a superboss *and* a spare branch-tagged boss roster). game.js's `onBossDefeated` withholds a `stairsSpot` here so clearing it can't skip the floor, and its `isBonusBossRoom` check is written to exactly the same shape — **keep the two in lockstep**. Outside the §9 retry loop (floor-number-keyed).
  20. `planetariumNode` *(Phase 7a)* — the D-branch gate. Only on `floorNum === 2` (HUD Floor 3) and only when `currentFloorPath()` is null; like `cpathgateNode` it always attaches when the floor is right, so the choice is never randomly denied. The two gates deliberately sit on floors the other cannot appear on, so one run is never offered both. Stepping onto its platform calls `descend('D')` (game.js), diverting the run onto the 4D-10D branch. Its room is also the game's one room with a completely bespoke tile-layer paint pass — see render.js's `rebuildPlanetariumTiles`. Outside the §9 retry loop (floor-number-keyed).
  21. `floorfeatureNode` — guaranteed via `attachSpecial('floorfeature')` on every floor past `OLD_MAIN_ROUTE_FINAL_FLOOR` (floorNum > 14), never on any floor at/below it. Outside the §9 retry loop (floor-number-keyed).
  22. Computes map `bounds` (`minX/maxX/minY/maxY`) by scanning every room's `gx/gy`.
  23. Returns `{ rooms, start, bossNode, treasureNode, shopNode, secretNode, supersecretNode, petshopNode, curseNode, sacrificeNode, vaultNode, challengeNode, starNode, crystalNode, sombraNode, secondBossNode, cpathgateNode, planetariumNode, shrineNode, arcadeNode, floorfeatureNode, minibossNode, bounds, floorNum }` — **Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4**: `supersecretNode` added to the returned object (previously the function existed but wasn't called at all, so there was nothing to return).
  Reads: `ROOM_TEMPLATES` (indirectly), `DUNGEON_CONFIG`, `RNG.random`, `Util.choice/shuffle/chance/randi`. Mutates: builds the entire `rooms` Map and `blockGrid` from scratch. Called by game.js (once per floor, presumably from `startFloor`/`descend`).

**Verification (dungeon-generation rework)**: a standalone Node harness loaded every script in `index.html`'s order into a `vm` sandbox (DOM/canvas/audio stubbed) and called `generateDungeon(floorNum)` for floorNum 0/1/5/10/14/15/20, 50 iterations each, 3 full passes (350 runs/floorNum-set total). Results: 0 throws, 0 missing boss/treasure/shop, 0 missing secret room, 0 discretionary-budget overruns, across every run; room count landed outside a `[min-2, max+2]` diagnostic window in only 4/350 runs (~1%), consistent with the documented "accept a rare shortfall after one retry" edge case. **Note (Floor Generation Revamp Slice 4)**: this run predates Slice 4's retry-loop/group-pick rewrite and is kept here as a historical record of the pre-Slice-4 algorithm's soundness; see `feature-research/floor-generation-revamp/audit.md` for Slice-4-specific verification (`node --check` across all touched files plus manual code-path tracing of the new retry loop and weighted-group-pick logic).

---

### room.js — tile-grid construction and room population

Header: turns a room node's polyomino shape into a tile grid, places doors/secret walls, and populates room contents.

**Tile constants**: `T_VOID=0, T_FLOOR=1, T_WALL=2, T_DOOR=3, T_SECRET=4, T_SECRET_OPEN=5`.

**`chooseShapeForNode(node)`** → `{name, w, mask}`-ish shape descriptor. `start` type always returns a fixed 1x1 `[[1]]`. `boss` picks `pickRoomShape(2,4)` (2-4 blocks, defined elsewhere — presumably utils/shapes). Treasure/shop/secret/petshop/curse/sacrifice/star/cpathgate/planetarium roll 65% chance of a 1-block shape (`pickRoomShape(1,1)`) vs 35% a 2-block shape (`pickRoomShape(2,2)`). Everything else (normal) gets `pickRoomShape(1,4)`. Called by `dungeon.js`'s `pickMaskForType` and `attachSpecial`/`attachNextTo` as the no-template fallback.

**`doorSlotCells(slot)`** — THOROUGH. Converts a door slot (block-space, from dungeon.js) into the exact 2 tile coordinates it occupies in its own room's *local* tile grid — always the middle 2 tiles of that block's 10-tile (`BLOCK`-tile) wall edge. For N/S doors: `y = dir==='N' ? r*BLOCK : (r+1)*BLOCK+1`, `x0 = 1 + c*BLOCK + 4`, returns `[{x0,y},{x0+1,y}]`. For E/W: mirrored on x/y. Called by `buildRoomTiles` (to carve door tiles) and by combat.js's `checkDoorTransition` (indirectly via `slot.cells`, which is populated by `buildRoomTiles` using this function).

**`buildRoomTiles(node)`** — Builds the actual 2D tile grid from `node.shape.mask`: sizes it `blockW*BLOCK+2` by `blockH*BLOCK+2` (1-tile void border all around), fills every occupied block's `BLOCK x BLOCK` footprint with `T_FLOOR`, then a second pass turns every `T_VOID` tile that orthogonally touches a `T_FLOOR` tile into `T_WALL` (the wall ring). Then, for every door slot on `node.doorSlots` whose `type` is `'normal'`, `'secret'`, or — **Secret Room Revamp Slice 3** — `'supersecret'`, computes its 2 cells via `doorSlotCells`, clips them to the grid bounds, stores them back onto the slot (`slot.cells = cells` — mutates the slot in place rather than a separate parallel doors structure), and stamps those grid cells `T_DOOR` (only for `'normal'`) or `T_SECRET` (both `'secret'` and `'supersecret'` — no new tile constant was added; supersecret walls render identically to secret walls) accordingly (slots with no live door get `slot.cells = null`). Returns `{grid, tileW, tileH}`. Called by `ensureRoomBuilt`.

**`ensureRoomBuilt(node)`** — Idempotent (`if (node.tiles) return;`). Calls `buildRoomTiles`, stores `node.tiles/tileW/tileH`. Note: `doorsOpen` is deliberately NOT set here (it's set at room creation time in dungeon.js's `makeRoomInstance`) — see header comment explaining why (treasure/shop rooms must already be correctly unlocked/relocked *before* their tiles are first built, since `ensureRoomBuilt` only runs on first entry, which for treasure/shop is always after the unlock already happened). Called by game.js (on entering a room) and combat.js's `openSecretPassage` (to force-build the neighbor room behind a just-opened secret wall).

**`roomFloorTiles(node, opts)`** → array of `{x,y}` floor-tile coordinates. Optionally excludes tiles within `opts.avoidCenter` of room center, and/or within `opts.avoidDoors` of any door slot's cells. Called by `populateRoomProcedural` (spot picking) and `rerollRoomEnemies` (reroll spot picking).

**`tileToPx(t)`** → `t*TILE + TILE/2`. Tiny helper, seemingly unused elsewhere in this file's own logic (present for callers wanting a quick tile→pixel-center conversion — not found being called from these 4 files' bodies besides its own definition, but kept as small shared utility).

**Room population — `populateRoom(node, dungeon, opts)`** — THOROUGH. The single entry point for filling a room with content, idempotent via `node.populated`.
  1. Resets all content arrays (`enemies/obstacles/pickups/chests/itemPedestals`), `shopSlots/donationMachine/rerollAltar = null`, and — Phase 4 overhaul — `fillies/machines = []`.
  2. `resetRoomEnemyBias()` — clears the module-level featured-enemy bias so this room rolls its own fresh bias on its first `resolveGenericEnemy` call.
