vulnerable), `mbtr_batteredlocket` (+1 Luck, -3% crit tradeoff), `mbtr_stillwaterdrop` (+5%
charm), `mbtr_gnarledtwig` (+bomb damage). Trinkets are a single equip slot, so each is one
`t === 'id' ? amount : 0` term on the matching formula — same idiom every other trinket already
uses, no stacking counter needed.

**Wiring — `js/systems/items-1.js`**: 101 items + 22 trinkets wired via explicit appended
formula terms across every channel listed above (`luck`, `speed`, `meleeDamage`, `rangedDamage`,
fire-rate/`rateDenom`, `rangeBonusTiles`, `bossDamageBonus`, `bossDamageTakenMult`,
`lifestealChance`, `critChance`, `onKillHealChance`, `venomChance`, `stunChance`, `charmChance`,
`freezeChance`, `fearChance`, `vulnerableChance`, `magnetRadius`, `bombRadiusMult`,
`bombDamageMult`, `dodgeChance`, `critMultiplier`, `dealDiscount`/`shopDiscountBonus`,
`tearFlags.pierce`/`.homing`/`.spectral`/`.explosive`/`.multishot`); 5 items need zero formula
wiring (picked up by the pre-existing generic `attackLayer` loop); the 6 `classSynergy` items
each got one manual base-effect formula line plus (at the time) automatic classSynergy handling
via `applyItemClassSynergyBonuses`, since removed. Every insertion point is tagged with an inline "Phase
34" comment (see the numbering note above). `node --check` passed on `items-1.js`.

**Deviations from the original spec**: no achievement-gated items/trinkets were added — all 128
new entries are plain, immediately-available pool content, matching the "variety batch" framing.
No new stat fields, UI, or mechanics were introduced anywhere in this pass; every effect reuses
an existing `recalcPlayerStats` channel or one of the two existing generic auto-wiring
mechanisms.

**Verification**: `node --check` passed on `items-10.js`, `trinkets-4.js`, and `items-1.js`. A
Node `vm` sandbox harness loading the real `index.html` script chain (84 files, through
`js/systems/items-2.js`) and calling the real `recalcPlayerStats` confirmed all 106 new item ids
and 22 new trinket ids load with no missing entries; ran every new item individually at x1 and
x5 stacked, every new trinket individually, an all-new-items-x3-stacked stress test across every
class, an extreme-stress case equipping literally every item in the entire game (old+new) at
once plus the 106 new items x10 and a trinket, and 40 randomly sampled multi-item/trinket/class
combos — checking for `NaN`/`Infinity`/thrown exceptions and sane bounds (`speed > 0`,
`meleeDamage`/`rangedDamage` non-negative, `0 <= dodgeChance <= 0.6`) throughout. Two harness-only
false positives were found and fixed in the harness itself (the synthetic test player was
missing `pillLuckBonus`/`pillSpeedBonus`/`pillFireRateBonus`/`pillDamageBonus`/
`starDamageBonus` — five pre-existing fields `recalcPlayerStats` reads unguarded, with no `|| 0`
fallback, unlike every item/trinket term in the same formulas; real `Player` objects always
initialize them elsewhere in the engine, e.g. `pills.js`/`stars.js`). After that fix, the only
remaining finding was `dodgeChance` reaching `0.68` in the one extreme-stress-full-inventory
case; traced to a pre-existing, unrelated mechanism — `js/systems/items-synergy.js`'s
classSynergy/combo system applies its own additive `dodgeChance` bonuses via
`applySynergyFieldBonuses`, called separately from `recalcPlayerStats`'s own internal
`Math.min(0.6, ...)` clamp with no re-clamp afterward — and reproduces with old-game items alone
at that same unreachable "equip everything simultaneously" scale, so it is not a defect
introduced by this batch's wiring and was left untouched (out of scope: fixing it would mean
changing `items-synergy.js`'s clamp behavior, a pre-existing mechanic, not reusing an existing
stat channel). See `feature-research/item-trinket-massive-batch/audit.md` for the full audit.

### Status-effect tear rebalance + QOL batch — `items-1.js`, `entities.js`, `combat-1.js`, `combat-2.js`, `combat-3.js`, `render.js`, `room.js`, `data/core.js`, `systems/stars.js`

Status-chance fields (`freezeChance`, `stunChance`, `vulnerableChance`, `charmChance`,
`fearChance`, `venomChance` — exact names per `items-1.js`'s `STATUS_EXCLUSIVITY_FIELDS`) were
**briefly made mutually exclusive** (`recalcPlayerStats` picked one winning field — highest chance,
ties broken by priority order — and zeroed the rest) but this has since been **reverted** (see the
"Turret/wisp tear-fidelity + status-chance exclusivity fix" section further below) — the zeroing
loop force-zeroed every status chance but one project-wide, which was the root cause of some
classes' secondary status chances (e.g. Crystal Pony's charm chance) never being able to proc.
All of a player's status chances can be simultaneously nonzero again. `player.primedStatus`
(highest-priority winning field) is still computed and drives tear-color display priority, but
`rollTearStatus` no longer limits *application* to that one field — see the later
"`rollTearStatus` multi-status redesign" section: it now independently rolls every status field
and returns an array, so the player's own ranged tears can apply multiple statuses per shot just
like melee/turret/wisp hits. Per-status caps remain lowered (see `items-1.js`'s
`STATUS_CHANCE_CAPS` for the exact table).

- **`rollTearStatus(player)`** (new function, `items-1.js`) — the actual per-tear determination.
  Called once per tear at spawn (`combat-1.js`'s main bolt, `combat-2.js`'s volley shard — each
  shard rolls independently). Originally rolled only `Math.random() < player[player.primedStatus]`
  and returned a single field name or `null`; superseded by the multi-status array redesign
  described later in this document. This replaced an earlier, buggy version of the mechanic that
  recolored/ringed *every* tear unconditionally whenever any status chance was nonzero (even a
  stray 4% from one trinket showed the ring on ~100% of tears) — the ring now reflects a real
  per-tear coin flip, not just "some chance exists somewhere".
- **`Projectile.appliedStatus`** (new field, `entities.js`) — the field name `rollTearStatus`
  returned for this specific tear (or `null`). Set at both spawn sites alongside `color`/
  `statusColor` (recolored/ringed only when the roll succeeded; plain default color and no ring
  otherwise). Carried through to hit resolution so the visual promise and the actual effect can't
  diverge.
- **`applyOnHitStatuses(game, enemy, scale, tearStatus)`** (`combat-2.js`) — gained a 4th param.
  When called with `tearStatus` (from `combat-3.js`'s `updateProjectiles`, passing
  `pr.appliedStatus`), it applies deterministically whatever was rolled at spawn (no re-roll) —
  originally exactly one field, now (see the "`rollTearStatus` multi-status redesign" section)
  an array of every status that hit for that tear; the branch normalizes a single value or array
  and applies each. When called without a 4th arg (every non-tear call site: melee, zone/aura,
  laser, wisp bolts in `attackStyles.js`/`familiars.js`/`combat-1.js`/`combat-2.js`), it falls back
  to the original independent `Math.random() < player.XChance * scale` roll per field, unchanged —
  those attacks have no tear/ring visual to stay in sync with. A pierced tear applies its locked-in
  status set to every enemy it hits, not a fresh roll per enemy.

- **`STATUS_CHANCE_CAPS`** / **`STATUS_GRANTING_ITEMS`** (new consts, `items-1.js`) — the former
  maps each status field to its cap, the latter maps each status to the item/trinket ids that
  grant it. `room.js`'s `pickItemFromPool`/`pickTrinketFromPool` now skip any item/trinket whose
  status grant is already at the player's cap for that status, so a maxed-out status chance stops
  cluttering item pools.
- **Active items ~50% rarer while holding one** — `pickItemFromPool` (`room.js`) halves an active
  item's pool weight when `player.activeItem` is already set.
- **`Player.healBlue(amount)`** (`entities.js`) — single choke point for every blue-heart grant in
  the game (pills, stars, combat-2.js pickups, `witchbrew`, `soulcandle`, shop's filly reward all
  route through it). Now starts with `if (this.def.noBlueHearts) return;`. **Kirin's def**
  (`data/core.js`) has the new flag `noBlueHearts:true`, alongside its existing `noRedContainers`
  — Kirin can no longer gain blue heart containers or blue heart pickups by any means. Pure
  single-effect blue-heart stars (`atlas`, `kraz`, `sk8s_wren`) simply no-op for Kirin rather than
  being rerouted to an alternate reward — accepted trade-off, not a bug.
- **`Projectile.statusColor`** (new field, `entities.js`) — set only on player bolts whose
  `rollTearStatus` roll succeeded (spawn sites: `combat-1.js`'s main ranged bolt, `combat-2.js`'s
  volley/shard bolt — both player-tear paths; enemy/familiar/turret projectiles are untouched), to
  `STATUS_TEAR_COLORS[appliedStatus]`. `render.js`'s `drawProjectiles()` draws an extra stroked
  ring (`radius + 3`, colored/glowed via `statusColor`) around any bolt that has one, on top of the
  existing fill/glint. No ring is drawn when `statusColor` is `null` (tear rolled no status).
- **Compass-star teleport auto-unlock** (`systems/stars.js`, in the shared `teleport_*` dispatch
  right after `game.enterRoom(target, null)`) — compass stars drop the player in the middle of the
  target room rather than at a door, so `checkDoorTransition`'s (`combat-2.js`) door-approach check
  — the only other code path that ever sets `doorsOpen = true` — never runs for that entry. Left
  alone, teleporting into an unopened key-locked room (`KEY_LOCKED_ROOM_TYPES` =
  `treasure`/`shop`/`vault`/`star`, `combat-2.js`) would softlock the player behind its still-
  closed doors. Fixed by force-setting `target.doorsOpen = true; target.tileLayerDirty = true;`
  right after entry when `KEY_LOCKED_ROOM_TYPES.has(target.type) && !target.doorsOpen` — free
  unlock (no key spent), since the player didn't choose to walk up to the door.

## QOL Slice F — devil/crystal deal overhaul

**Files touched:** `js/systems/dungeon.js`, `js/systems/room.js`, `js/game.js`,
`js/entities/entities.js`, `js/achievements/logic.js`, `js/ui/render.js`, `js/ui/ui.js`,
`index.html`.

**Spawn roll** (`generateDungeon`, `dungeon.js`) — the old rule spawned both a crystal room and a
sombra room, unconditionally, off the boss room on every odd `floorNum` (`everySecondFloor`
gate). That's gone. Now, on **every** floor that has a `bossNode` (no odd-floor gate), the game
rolls once via `RNG.random()` — never `Math.random()`, per Slice D1's determinism rule:
`chance = player.tookDamageThisFloor ? 0.16 : 0.50`. Because `generateDungeon(floorNum)` runs
*before* `game.js`'s `startFloor` resets `tookDamageThisFloor = false`, the flag it reads is
still the **previous** floor's damage status — intentional, so the roll reflects "did the player
get hit on the floor they just cleared." If the roll succeeds, exactly **one** of
`'crystal'`/`'sombra'` is chosen — never both, they're mutually exclusive per boss room now —
using `game.dealAlignment` if the run has locked onto an alignment already, else a random pick
via `Util.choice(['crystal','sombra'])` (RNG-backed, see `core/utils-1.js`). `bossNode.maxDoors`
is still bumped to 3 for the single `attachNextTo` call and restored to 1 afterward. If Kirin has
already spent her one free deal item this run (`game.player.dealFreebieUsed`), the roll is
skipped entirely — no deal room spawns for her at all after that.

**Global-`game` access, a wiring note:** `generateDungeon(floorNum)`'s signature wasn't widened
to take the player/alignment as explicit params. Instead it reads the ambient global `game`
variable directly (`typeof game !== 'undefined' && game`), the same pattern `currentFloorPath()`
already used elsewhere in this file. This is a mechanical wiring choice made to keep the change
small and consistent with existing precedent in the file, not a design decision — documented here
and in `feature-research/qol-slice-f-deal-overhaul/audit.md`.

**Alignment lock** — `game.dealAlignment` (`null` by default, set in `startRun()`) is set to
`'crystal'` or `'sombra'` the first time the player actually **takes** an item from either
pedestal type — inside `game.js`'s `updateItemPedestal()`, in the `isDeal` branch, after a
successful purchase (`if (!this.dealAlignment) this.dealAlignment = ped.dealType || 'sombra';`).
It is deliberately *not* set when a deal room merely spawns or is walked into — a player can see
both crystal and sombra deal rooms across a run before ever buying anything. Once they buy from
one, the lock is set and every subsequent deal-room roll for the rest of the run picks that same
alignment (skipping the random `Util.choice`). This is the intended "pick a side" mechanic.

**Crystal is now a paid deal type, not a free-item room.** `room.js`'s `instantiateSpawner`,
`case 'item':` branches on `node.type === 'crystal'`: crystal rooms route their `"i"`
spawner-letter items through `addDealPedestal(node, item, tx, ty, 'crystal')` instead of the free
`addItemPedestal`. Every other room type (`secret`/`curse`/`challenge`/`treasure`/etc.) is
untouched and still free. Sombra rooms' `case 'deal':` still calls
`addDealPedestal(node, item, tx, ty, 'sombra')`, drawing from the `'sombra'` item pool as before.
Room-template data itself (`data/roomTemplates/core.js`) was **not** rewritten — crystal
templates still use `"i"`, sombra templates still use `"d"` — the branch lives entirely in
`instantiateSpawner`.

**`addDealPedestal(node, item, tx, ty, dealType)`** (`room.js`) gained a 4th parameter,
`dealType` (`'crystal'`|`'sombra'`, defaults to `'sombra'` if omitted), stored on the pushed
pedestal struct as `dealType`. `rerollOnePedestal` was updated to reroll from
`pickItemFromPool(ped.dealType || 'sombra')` instead of a hardcoded `'sombra'`, so a rerolled
crystal deal pedestal still draws from the crystal pool.

**Cost overhaul** (`game.js`'s `updateItemPedestal`, `isDeal` branch):
- **Kirin exception** — Kirin (`player.def.id === 'kirin'`) gets her first deal item free. On take,
  if `player.dealFreebieUsed` is already true, the purchase is denied (deny sound + toast,
  "You've already used your free deal this run.") and the loop `continue`s — defensive, since the
  spawn roll in `dungeon.js` already stops offering deal rooms once the freebie is spent, so this
  path should be unreachable in normal play but guards against any pre-existing/leftover deal room
  from before the freebie was spent. Otherwise `player.dealFreebieUsed = true;` is set and the item
  is taken for free. `Player.dealFreebieUsed` is a new field, initialized `false` in the
  `entities.js` constructor.
- **Non-Kirin cost** — `const q = ped.item.quality || 1;` (defensive fallback in case an item
  lacks `quality`), `containerCost = q <= 2 ? 1 : 2`, `blueCost = q <= 2 ? 2 : 3`. Preference order:
  pay with a **permanent heart container** (`player.grantHeartContainer(-containerCost)`) if the
  class can take red containers at all (`!player.def.noRedContainers`) **and** it's safe — the
  safe-floor rule is `(player.redMax - containerCost) >= 1`, i.e. never let `redMax` drop below 1;
  chosen after surveying class `redMax` values in `data/core.js` so no class can be zeroed out by a
  deal. Otherwise, fall back to paying `blueCost` blue hearts (`player.blueCurrent -= blueCost`) if
  affordable. Otherwise deny (deny sound + toast, "Not enough hearts for this deal.") and
  `continue` — item stays on its pedestal.
- **Stat tracking** — `bumpStat('sombraDealsTaken', 1, this)` (pre-existing) now has a parallel
  `bumpStat('crystalDealsTaken', 1, this)` for crystal-type pedestals, keyed off `ped.dealType`.
  `crystalDealsTaken:0` was added to the stats-init dict in `achievements/logic.js` alongside the
  existing `sombraDealsTaken:0`.

**`dealDiscount` follow-up — now wired into the cost formula.** The `dealDiscount` player stat
(granted by items like Deal Maker, Pawnbroker's Chit, and class synergies such as Engineer
Pony/Crystal Pony) is applied as a percentage-of-cost reduction AFTER the container-vs-blue-heart
tier is chosen (tier selection itself is unchanged — it still keys off `redMax`/`blueCurrent`
against the undiscounted `containerCost`/`blueCost`). Formula, applied identically in `game.js`,
`render.js`, and `ui.js`:
```
discount = Math.min(1, player.dealDiscount || 0);
effectiveCost = Math.max(0, Math.round(tierCost * (1 - discount)));
```
If `effectiveCost` rounds to 0 the item is free — the `grantHeartContainer`/`blueCurrent`
deduction is skipped entirely (mirrors Kirin's free path, but `dealFreebieUsed` is untouched;
that flag is Kirin-only). Does not apply to Kirin's freebie cost (already 0) or her post-freebie
deny path. See `feature-research/qol-slice-f-deal-overhaul/audit.md` for the original gap writeup
and this follow-up note.

**UI — cost readout.** `render.js`'s `drawItemPedestal()` draws a small text label under any
unclaimed `isDeal` pedestal: `'FREE'` for Kirin's unspent freebie (nothing drawn once she's spent
it, since no further deal pedestal should exist), otherwise `'-<effectiveCost> ❤'` or
`'-<effectiveCost> 💙'` depending on which the player would actually pay (mirrors the same
container-vs-blue-heart branch as the cost logic in `game.js`, including the `dealDiscount`
formula above — shows `'FREE'` too when the discount rounds the tier cost to 0). `ui.js`'s
`showItemExamine(ped, player)` shows the equivalent as a full sentence ("Cost: -N heart
container(s)" / "Cost: -N blue hearts" / "Cost: FREE" when discounted to 0 / nothing for Kirin's
freebie) in a new `#itemExamineCost` div, added to `index.html` right after `#itemExamineSwap`
(reuses the `.item-examine-swap` CSS class), hidden/shown via the `hidden` class exactly like the
existing swap-notice div.

## Protected basic items — flat speed / flat fire rate / +1% chance tier + `data/protectedBasicItems.js`

76 existing items whose old effects had drifted into one-off special-case code (shop discounts,
map reveals, bonus coin drops, free keys, bomb-fuse tweaks, invuln extensions, …) were converted
into plain numeric stat items. Their old effect code was **deleted** from `entities.js`,
`combat-2.js`, `combat-3.js`, `game.js`, `room.js`, `render.js` and `systems/items-2.js`; each id
now has exactly one term, in `recalcPlayerStats` (`systems/items-1.js`), except the four
heart-container ones (which are in `items-2.js`'s `grantHeartContainer(1)` id branch). Two new
stat channels were added for them.

- **`flatSpeedBonus`** — applied *after* `player.speed = player.baseSpeed * Util.clamp(1 + …, 0.25,
  2.2)`, so it is deliberately **outside** the multiplicative clamp: `+20` per stack for each of 10
  items, then `player.speed = Math.min(player.speed + flatSpeedBonus, 700);`. The 700 ceiling is
  the only cap on it — a flat additive lane that percentage speed items cannot scale.
- **`flatFireRate`** — applied immediately after `player.fireCooldown = player.fireCooldownBase *
  rateMult;`, `+0.02` shots/sec per stack across 20 items. Because cooldown is the reciprocal of
  rate, it is converted through rate space and only when non-zero:
  `if (flatFireRate > 0) { const effRate = (1 / player.fireCooldown) + flatFireRate;
  player.fireCooldown = Math.max(0.1, 1 / effRate); }`. The `Math.max(0.1, …)` is the floor (10
  shots/sec).
- **+1% flat chance tier** — a `0.01 * (p.<id> || 0)` term for 5 items appended to each of the 7
  existing chance sums (`critChance`, `lifestealChance`, `freezeChance`, `venomChance`,
  `stunChance`, `charmChance`, `fearChance`) **before** their existing `Math.min(cap, …)`, so every
  pre-existing cap still applies unchanged. Unlike the luck-scaled sources above them in the same
  expression, these are flat — they do not multiply by `luckBonus`. The 25 freeze/venom/stun/charm/
  fear ids were also added to `STATUS_GRANTING_ITEMS` (the hand-maintained reverse index
  `room.js` reads when biasing pools), which has no crit/lifesteal keys, so those 10 are absent
  there by design.

Two wiring gaps were closed so the new descriptions are truthful: 4 ids were added to the
`grantHeartContainer(1)` branch in `items-2.js`, and 7 ids were added to `rangeBonusTiles` in
`items-1.js`.

### `js/data/protectedBasicItems.js` — `PROTECTED_BASIC_ITEM_IDS`

New data file, same convention as the other `js/data/*.js` globals (plain `<script src>` load —
tag sits right after `items-10.js` in `index.html` — a bare `const PROTECTED_BASIC_ITEM_IDS = {…}`,
no exports). It is a **pure reference list, read by no runtime code**: 130 item ids grouped by the
single stat each grants — `heartContainer` (25), `speed` (10), `damage` (20), `tileRange` (15),
`luck` (5), `fireRate` (20), and `critChance` / `lifestealChance` / `freezeChance` / `venomChance`
/ `stunChance` / `charmChance` / `fearChance` (5 each).

The file's header comment marks it SET IN STONE. **Any future item revamp/rebalance pass must check
this list first** and leave every listed id alone — same id, same single stat effect, same
magnitude, same pools — so the game always retains a dependable supply of plain numeric upgrades
underneath the synergy/attackLayer items. Adding new items is always fine; the list is a floor, not
a ceiling. Note it is a curated subset for `damage` and `luck`: the codebase contains ~50 pure
`+1 damage` and ~47 pure `+1 Luck` items (most of them trophy/mastery unlock rewards), of which the
20 and 5 most canonical are protected here.

## Tear-flag system — `systems/tearShapes.js`, declarative `tearEffect` items, and the on-hit pipeline

The old tear mechanics (`pierce` / `homing` / `spectral` / `explosive`) are each
hand-summed in `recalcPlayerStats` (`systems/items-1.js`) from a hardcoded list
of item ids. Those four lines are untouched and still work exactly that way.
Everything added from here on instead goes through a generic **data-driven**
pathway, so a new tear modifier is a data entry, not new stat code.

### `tearEffect` — the declarative item field

An item in `js/data/items-*.js` can carry a `tearEffect` object. Right after the
four legacy sum lines, `recalcPlayerStats` resets the new flags and walks
`ITEM_LIST` once, folding in every held item's `tearEffect`:

| `flag` | how it combines |
| --- | --- |
| `'sizeMult'` | **additive** — `sizeMult += amount * count`, then clamped to `0.5..2.5` |
| `'shape'` | **exclusive** — highest `SHAPE_PRIORITY[te.shape]` wins, only one shape is ever active |
| anything else | **stacking counter** — `tearFlags[flag] += (amount ?? 1) * count` |

The results live on `player.tearFlags` (`chainLightning`, `splitOnHit`,
`knockbackPulse`, `sizeMult`, `shape`), rebuilt from scratch on every recalc
alongside the legacy four.

### `TEAR_SHAPES` (`js/systems/tearShapes.js`)

A registry of whole-tear archetypes: `round` (default), `heavy`, `needle`,
`bouncy`, `boomerang`, `orbiter`. Each entry may define `radiusMult`,
`speedMult`, `damageMult`, an `onSpawn(pr)` hook (attaches per-tear state) and
an `onUpdate(pr, dt, game)` hook. `SHAPE_PRIORITY` is declared **once**, here —
the file is script-tagged before every consumer, and `items-1.js` reads that
global rather than declaring its own copy (plain script tags share one global
scope, so a second `const` of the same name would throw).

- `bouncy` rides the pre-existing `pr.ricochet` field (wall bounces only).
- `boomerang` flies 260px out, flips velocity, despawns near its origin; its
  explosive flag is re-armed for the return leg.
- `orbiter` hard-sets its position around the player each frame and sets
  **`ignoresHoming: true`** — a bolt driven by an orbit cannot also be steered
  toward enemies, so `updateProjectiles`' homing steer explicitly skips shapes
  with that flag and the orbit wins.

`onUpdate` is called in `updateProjectiles` **before** the standard move/life
step, so a shape's velocity flip or position set takes effect the same frame.

**Collision stays circular for every shape** — `needle`'s elongated render (a
rotated, scaled ellipse) and `heavy`'s fatter glow/glint in
`Renderer.drawProjectiles` are purely cosmetic; the hitbox is always
`pr.radius`.

### `resolveTearMods(player, familiar)`

One spawn-time resolver, used by `playerRangedAttack` (combat-1.js),
`playerCrystalVolleyAttack` (combat-2.js) and the familiar spawn sites
(familiars.js), so every site applies shape + size identically. It returns
`{ shape, shapeDef, sizeMult, radiusMult, damageMult, speedMult }`.

`sizeMult` carries a **built-in tradeoff**, stacking multiplicatively with
whatever the shape does:

```
damage x (1 + (sizeMult - 1) * 0.50)      // bigger tears hit harder
speed  x clamp(1 - (sizeMult - 1) * 0.25, 0.5, 1.5)   // ...and fly slower
radius x sizeMult
```

`familiar: true` forces `shape: 'round'` and applies **sizeMult only** —
shapes are deliberately a player-tear-only mechanic so a wisp keeps its
dye-driven identity instead of turning into a boomerang or an orbiter.

### The on-hit pipeline (`updateProjectiles`, combat-3.js)

The player/familiar enemy-collision block is an explicit, numbered sequence.
**New on-hit abilities must slot in as a step at the right position, not be
bolted onto an existing one.**

1. **Damage calculation + application** — crit roll, boss bonus, `takeDamage`.
2. **On-hit statuses** — `applyOnHitStatuses` (full for player bolts, scaled by
   `pr.statusScale` for wisp bolts), sound, crit bookkeeping, float text.
3. **Chain lightning** — nearest *other* living enemy within 140px, one jump
   only, for `round(dmg * min(1.5, 0.5 * pr.chainLightning))`. Because it reads
   the post-crit `dmg`, it inherits crits and the boss bonus for free. A chained
   hit never chains again. Flash reuses the single-slot `game.laserFX` pattern.
4. **Split on hit** — spawns 2 children at ±35° from travel direction with
   `damage * 0.5`, `radius * 0.6`, `life 0.7`, `homing * 0.5`, inherited
   `spectral`/`chainLightning`, and `isSplitChild: true`. Children are forced to
   `shape: 'round'` and inherit **no** pierce, explosive or splitOnHit, so the
   `isSplitChild` guard makes recursion impossible.
5. **Knockback pulse** — adds `2.2 * pr.knockbackPulse` along the bolt's
   heading into the enemy's existing `knockX`/`knockY` channel (the same one
   `Enemy.takeDamage(dmg, kx, ky)` writes to).
6. **Shape on-hit** — intentionally empty; no shape needs an `onHit` hook today.
7. **Explosive detonation** — fired by the shared `if (pr.dead)
   detonateExplosiveProjectile(...)` guard just after the loop.
8. **Pierce / death resolution — ALWAYS LAST.** `hitEnemies.push`, then decrement
   `pierce` or kill the bolt. It is last on purpose: earlier steps read
   `pr.pierce` / `pr.dead` and must see the pre-hit state.

### Items

`js/data/items-10.js` ships 11 plain `tearEffect` passives (no `classSynergy`,
no `attackLayer`), all `tf_`-prefixed: 5 shapes (`tf_leadenpearl` heavy,
`tf_slenderquill` needle, `tf_rubberknuckle` bouncy, `tf_returnfang` boomerang,
`tf_ringkeeper` orbiter), 3 × `sizeMult 0.15` (`tf_swollendrop`,
`tf_bloatedgland`, `tf_glutbulb`), plus `tf_splitnucleus`, `tf_stormcoil` and
`tf_thunderjack`.

### Basic-item rework additions (2026)

35 previously plain stat-bump items (none of them in `PROTECTED_BASIC_ITEM_IDS`,
none of them carrying `attackLayer` / `classSynergy` / `tearEffect`) were
repurposed in place through the pathways above. Their old hand-written stat
terms in `recalcPlayerStats` were deleted; ids, pools, icons and colors are
unchanged.

**Two new shapes** in `TEAR_SHAPES`:

- `spiral` — `radiusMult 1, speedMult 1.05, damageMult 1`, plus an `onUpdate`
  that accumulates `pr.__spiralT += dt * 6` and offsets the bolt by
  `sin(__spiralT) * 70 * dt` along the unit normal of its own velocity
  (`(-vy, vx)`), so it corkscrews around whatever heading it was fired in.
- `razor` — pure stat archetype, no hooks: `radiusMult 0.45, speedMult 1.5,
  damageMult 0.65`.

`SHAPE_PRIORITY` was renumbered to keep one **total order with no collisions**
(the original five keep their relative ranking, the two new shapes sit below
them):

```js
const SHAPE_PRIORITY = { boomerang: 7, orbiter: 6, bouncy: 5, needle: 4, heavy: 3, spiral: 2, razor: 1 };
```

**`tearShield`** — folded by the generic `tearEffect` pass like any stacking
counter, then clamped in `recalcPlayerStats` so stacked copies can never make
you fully immune:

```js
player.tearFlags.tearShield = Util.clamp(player.tearFlags.tearShield, 0, 0.75);
```

It is a **probability**, consumed by a gated pass in `updateProjectiles`
(combat-3.js) placed after both existing collision blocks and immediately before
the final `game.projectiles = game.projectiles.filter(p => !p.dead)`. For each
live player/familiar tear it scans enemy bolts; on circle overlap it rolls
`Math.random() < tearShield` and, on success, marks **both** projectiles dead and
`break`s — at most one intercept per tear per frame. Header comment:
`// --- TEAR SHIELD: player/familiar tears can intercept enemy bolts ---`.

**Class-attack borrowing — the `grantAttack` item field.** This reuses the
skilltree `uniqueFlag` mechanism (`player[field] = value`) rather than inventing a
parallel gate. An item may set `grantAttack:'laser'` or
`grantAttack:['charged','crystalVolley']`; a pass in `recalcPlayerStats`
(immediately after the tearShield clamp) walks `ITEM_LIST` and sets each named
flag to `true` on the player, then seeds the two flags that would otherwise be
inert: `crystalVolley` gets `crystalShardCount = 3` (+ default spacing) because
its dispatch bails on `crystalShardCount <= 0`, and `charged` gets
`chargeTime = 0.5` because a 0 charge time fires instantly. Like `uniqueFlag`,
grants are **one-way within a run** — the fields are never reset per recalc.
Note that `greenFireAttack` and `innateFireRing` *suppress* the normal attack
(guard in combat-1.js), `shockwaveAttack` only applies inside
`playerMeleeAttack`, and `laser` only matters for ranged classes.

**`pullPulse`** — knockback pulse mirrored, direction negated. On-hit pipeline
step 5b, right before the shape on-hit step:

```
ang = atan2(pr.vy, pr.vx);  mag = 2.2 * pr.pullPulse
e.knockX -= cos(ang) * mag;  e.knockY -= sin(ang) * mag
```

**`chaosStatus`** — pipeline step 5c, player bolts only. Picks one of
`['freezeChance','venomChance','stunChance','charmChance','fearChance']` with
equal weight and passes it as the 4th argument of the **existing**
`applyOnHitStatuses(game, e, undefined, name)` call — the same deterministic
single-status path `pr.appliedStatus` uses, so it stacks *in addition to*
`appliedStatus` rather than replacing it.

Both fields ride new `Projectile` opts (`pullPulse`, `chaosStatus`, defaulting to
`0`) in `entities/entities.js`, passed through at the player spawn sites in
combat-1.js and combat-2.js next to `knockbackPulse`.

**"More tears, slower gun" trio** (`mb_talonshot`, `martyrsvow`,
`nbat_berserkersbrand`) uses the plain `multishot`/`mb_splitshot` idiom rather
than a tear flag: `+2 / +3 / +4` into the `multishotExtra` hand-sum (still inside
`Math.min(4, ...)`) paid for by `-0.25 / -0.40 / -0.50` in `rateDenom`.

## Room render polish 2 — `ui/render.js`

Five purely-visual additions. Nothing here reads or writes gameplay state; all
per-frame animation is driven by `game.now` / `fxDt` (never `performance.now()`).

### Stage flavor detection — `roomFlavor(node, pal)`

`roomFlavor(node, pal)` (module-level in render.js) returns `'crystal'` for
`treasure`/`crystal` room types (room type wins over stage), otherwise
`paletteFlavor(pal)` (stages.js), otherwise `'dust'`. Shared by the ambient
particles (piece 2) and the baked surface accents (piece 3).

**Visual-overhaul batch B moved the table itself into stages.js.** render.js's old
lazily-built `flavorMap()`/`_flavorMap` (which hardcoded four stage flavors plus a
handful of branch/C/D palettes) is gone; the palette→flavor map is now
`PALETTE_FLAVORS` in stages.js, seeded from each `STAGES` entry's own `flavor`
field. Reason for the move: room.js needs the same flavor at room-population time
to choose a decor-prop pool, and it must not depend on render.js.

### 1. Player light — `LIGHT_R`, `playerLightSprite()`, `Game.prototype.drawPlayerLight()`

`playerLightSprite()` bakes ONE `280×280` offscreen canvas holding a warm radial
gradient (peak `rgba(255,226,170,0.10)` → transparent) and caches it in
`_lightSprite` forever. `drawPlayerLight()` runs after `drawVignette()` (it
layers with the static vignette, it does not replace it): one `drawImage`
centered on the player's screen position, offset by `FX.shakeX/Y`, culled when
off-camera, drawn under `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'` so it can only
brighten and never hazes sprites. O(1) per frame.

### 2. Ambient particle drift — `Ambient`

A second particle pool that mirrors `FX`'s ring-buffer shape but owns its **own**
array with `MAX: 14`, deliberately separate from `FX.MAX = 260` so combat bursts
are never starved. `init()`, `reset()` (called on room change alongside
`FX.reset()`), `_take()` (reuses dead slots — no allocation after init),
`alive()`, `spawn(camX, camY, flavor, pal)`, `update(dt, camX, camY, flavor, pal)`,
`draw(ctx)`.

`kind`: `0` dust mote (default, `Theme.particle.dustSolid`), `1` ember (fire —
`Theme.particle.hitSpark`, accelerating upward), `2` snow (ice — falling, lateral
sway `Math.sin(q.phase + q.life * 1.6)`, tinted `pal.accent`), `3` sparkle
(crystal — `Theme.particle.sparkle`, twinkling alpha). Particles spawn in world
coords inside the camera rect. Spawn throttle: `0.28s` fire / `0.34s` crystal /
`0.42s` otherwise; cap drops to `reducedCount(MAX)` under
`prefersReducedMotion`. Driven from `updateAmbientFX(dt)`
(`Ambient.update(dt, camX, camY, roomFlavor(node, currentPalette()), pal)`) and
drawn right after `FX.draw(ctx)`.

### 3. Baked material accents — inside `rebuildTileLayer`

Zero runtime cost; all four previously-dead `Theme.shadow` tokens are now used.

* **ice** — walls get a `Theme.shadow.rim` top highlight when the tile above is
  open, plus a diagonal `Theme.shadow.sheen` streak on ~38% of wall tiles.
  New `tileRand` salts **61–65** (presence, x/y offset, length x/y).
* **crystal** — the existing boss/treasure ornate diamond motif is *extended*
  (not duplicated) with a small `Theme.shadow.glint` dot; `ornateFloor` is now
  `type === 'boss' || type === 'treasure' || flavor === 'crystal'`.
* **fire** — 2px `Theme.shadow.groundHard` floor accent on each floor edge that
  abuts a solid tile.

### 4. Locked-door idle pulse — `node._lockedDoorCells`, `Game.prototype.drawLockedDoorPulse()`

`rebuildTileLayer` collects locked door cells into a `Map` keyed by
`y * node.tileW + x` (the special door-slot pass repaints cells the `T_DOOR`
grid branch already visited — the map dedupes them so those doors don't pulse at
double alpha; later, more specific color wins) and stores
`node._lockedDoorCells = [{x, y, color}]`. `drawLockedDoorPulse()` (called right
after `drawTiles()`) early-outs on `doorsOpen` or an empty list, then fills each
cell inset by 3px with `alpha = 0.05 + 0.05 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(this.now / 560))`
under `'lighter'`. Flat `0.05` under `prefersReducedMotion`. No per-frame grid
scan.

### 5. Directional transition wipe — `game.roomFadeDir`, `Game.prototype.fadeGradient(dir)`

`enterRoom(node, enteredSlot)` records `this.roomFadeDir = enteredSlot ?
enteredSlot.dir : null` next to the existing `roomFadeTimer` assignment (room
setup only — no movement/collision/input change; `enteredSlot.dir` was already
in hand there for spawn placement). `fadeGradient(dir)` lazily builds and caches
one linear gradient per direction in `this._fadeGrads`, running from `0.8` →
`0.45` alpha of `Theme.rgb.fadeVeil` oriented along the direction of travel; the
fade block animates strength via `globalAlpha` so the gradient is never rebuilt.
`dir === null` (run's first room, stairs, star-map teleports) returns `null` and
the original flat veil fill is used. Still entirely inside the existing
`ROOM_FADE_TIME` timer.

## Obstacle visual pass — `core/utils-1.js`, `ui/render.js`, `data/collectibles.js`

### 1. Obstacle variant salts 200–211, 300–314 — `Util.drawObstacle`

`drawObstacle` computes `vtx = ob.tx | 0`, `vty = ob.ty | 0` once at the top and
each branch rolls its own look inline with
`Math.floor(tileRand(vtx, vty, SALT) * n)` — no closure (per-obstacle-per-frame
hot path), no new field on `Obstacle`, deterministic per tile. **Every branch
now has 5 hand-built variants** (was 2–3 pre-2026 visual-overhaul-phase1), each
genuinely distinct in silhouette/composition, not just a parameter tweak.
**Variant 0 reproduces the pre-pass art** for every branch that had prior art;
brand-new branches (spikedrock, tintedrock, dustvent, crushvent, lurehorn) have
no baseline to preserve, so all 5 of their variants are new. The `spike` branch
is also a full redesign start to finish (see below) — its old 8-point-star
look was the thing being replaced, so variant 0 does not reproduce it either.
Salts, reserved in a comment block above the function (floor tiles own 3–12,
29, 41, 50, 53, 60–70, 91–130; 203 is retired, never reused; new salts are
≥300):

`200` pit (lip **tone** — 5 bands, geometry untouched since it would break the
`PIT_N` mask seam between adjacent pit tiles — plus, on 3 of the 5 rolls, a
floor decal (rubble / crack / bone flecks) scattered on the void floor so a
cluster reads as distinct tiles), `201` cactus (arm offsets/body height/rib
count, now including a barrel no-arms body and a twin-raised-arms body),
`202` fire (log arrangement + flame lean, one roll drives both, now up to 4
crossed logs or 4 vertical logs — shared by all 7 colored fires), `204` turret
(housing decoration only — bare / 4-corner rivets / crossed plates / collar
ring / 6-bolt ring; barrel angles and eye always encode firing directions and
never vary), `205` thornbush (thorn count/rotation/length, now including a
clustered one-sided burst and a double ring of mixed-length thorns),
`206` luckcrystal (facet layout, now including a 4-shard cross and a
dominant-shard-plus-chips arrangement), `207` mud (blob placement, now
including a single ripple-ringed blob and 4 tiny scattered blobs — puddle
outline never changes), `208` sandtrap (ripple ring count/gap, now including
an off-center sink and a single ring with scattered grit specks),
`209` bombbarrel/pushablebombbarrel (band count/style and fuse curl direction,
now including rivets at the band seams and a hazard-stripe pair — fuse spark
size/height are fixed regardless of variant, the "this thing explodes" tell),
`210` current (chevron `lineWidth`/embellishment only — count/spacing feed the
scroll-wrap animation math and never vary — now including a tip-bubble accent
and a thin double-stroke), `211` rock/hardrock/tallrock/tallhardrock fallback
(rim-arc start angle plus a face detail: dark pit / hairline crack / twin
small pits — radius and body untouched, since rocks are the most common
obstacle and their silhouette is their hitbox read).

`phantomwall` is gated out of salt 211 (`const plain = ob.kind !== 'phantomwall'`
→ `rkV = 0`) so it stays pixel-identical to `tallhardrock`; variation would be a
tell.

**Spike redesign (`spike`/`spiketrap`/`movingspike`, salt 300, replaces the
retired salt 203).** The old 8-point jagged star is gone. New look: a small
dark base disc plus a cluster of individually rendered tapered nail/spike
polygons jutting outward — a taper-polygon technique (base-circle point ±
perpendicular half-width → a far tip point, filled + stroked per spike) reused
below for spikedrock's studs. 5 variants vary spike count/angle-offset/length:
8 spikes evenly spaced (tip length 13, the closest analog to the old look),
6 spikes off-angle (length 14), 5 spikes in a narrow forward arc, 10 short
spikes (length 9, a "bed of nails" density read), and 8 spikes alternating
long/short (14/8) for a jagged asymmetric silhouette. Tip lengths are capped
at 14 to match the old star's `outerR=13` so the hitbox read doesn't change.

**`spikedrock` (salt 301, new dedicated branch — previously fell through to
the generic rock branch with no studs at all).** A solid rock body (reusing
the rock branch's fill/shade) plus protruding studs drawn with the same
taper-polygon technique as the redesigned spike branch, capped to project
only ~5px past `ob.radius`. 5 variants vary stud count/placement (4 corner
studs, 6 evenly spaced, a dense front-facing cluster, 3 large studs, 8 short
studs) so a spikedrock field doesn't read as one stamped sprite.

**New dedicated branches (salts 302–305), added because these `OBSTACLES`
kinds previously had no branch of their own and fell through to the generic
rock catch-all — rendering as a plain grey boulder with no barrels/vent/horn
drawn at all, which under-communicated their projectile/reward behavior:**

- **`tintedrock` (salt 302)** — same rock body as the generic branch, plus a
  bright crystal vein (`Util.shadeColor(def.color, 0.55)`, glow via
  `shadowBlur`) so its better bomb-reward status reads visually. 5 variants:
  single diagonal vein, branching Y vein, cross vein, an inset ring vein, and
  a cluster of 3 small diamond facets.
- **`dustvent` (salt 303)** — a low ground-level fissure (walkable, so kept as
  a decal rather than a raised body): a dark oval vent with grit lines along
  `def.angles` (the 4 diagonals) in `def.boltColor`. 5 variants vary line
  length and add dust-puff dots at 2 or 4 of the vent mouths, or an
  off-center puff cluster.
- **`crushvent` (salt 304)** — a bigger, blacker chimney-vent (same
  body/shading proportions as the turret branch) firing on all 8 bearings via
  `def.angles`/`def.boltColor`, reading as heavier/more dangerous than
  dustvent. 5 variants add a soot crack, a collar ring, 4-corner soot flecks,
  a longer crack, or a dark center scorch mark.
- **`lurehorn` (salt 305)** — a curved horn (quadratic-curve body, `lineCap:
  'round'`) with a glowing tip in `def.boltColor` (the homing-bolt origin —
  `shadowBlur` glow, bigger on one variant). 5 variants vary curl direction
  (left/right), horn sweep (tight/wide), an added base ring, and tip-glow
  intensity.

**New dedicated branches (salts 306–314), added for the 2026
new-objects-and-rooms batch's 10 new `OBSTACLES` kinds. None of these had any
prior branch or fallback art to preserve, so all 5 variants on every one of
them are new, and — unlike the 302–305 batch above, which needed a follow-on
1b pass — the glow+glint quality-bar treatment (`ctx.shadowColor`/
`ctx.shadowBlur` ambient glow, skipped under `flash`, plus a
`Theme.shadow.glint` highlight dot) was built into each branch from the
start. `driftstone` (the batch's 10th kind) is the one exception: it
deliberately reuses the existing `current` branch and salt 210 rather than
getting a new dedicated branch, since it is a diagonal-push pad with no
visual need beyond `current`'s existing chevron treatment — see
`data/collectibles.js`'s comment on that entry.**

- **`glimmerrock` (salt 306)** — same dark-rock base as the generic rock
  branch, plus 1–3 crystal shard polygons on top (glow in `def.color`) so the
  attackable/heart-drop reward reads distinctly from a plain rock or from
  `tintedrock`'s vein treatment. 5 variants: single tall shard, twin shards,
  a 3-shard crown, a low wide pair, and an off-center pair.
- **`frostvent` (salt 307)** — a flat ground puff (walkable, never blocks
  movement, same non-raised decal treatment as `dustvent`/`mud`) with small
  ice motes drifting upward instead of `dustvent`'s fire-line spokes, since
  this vent freezes rather than damages. 5 variants vary mote count/spread:
  three even, two wide, four tight, one tall central, five scattered.
- **`thornspire` (salt 308)** — drawn taller than Spike Trap, with its own
  ground-shadow ellipse and base disc, so the silhouette visually explains
  why it also sets `tall`/`blocksFlight` (unlike the ground-hugging spike
  branches). 5 variants vary spire lean (straight, left, right) and width
  (thin/thick), with one variant adding a side barb.
- **`cinderkeg` (salt 309)** — same fuse-and-spark visual language as
  `bombbarrel`/`pushablebombbarrel`, but a narrower rounded-cylinder keg
  silhouette (vs. the barrel's round one) so the two pushable-explosive props
  read as different objects at a glance. 5 variants vary band count/placement
  (two bands, one wide band, three thin bands, one off-center band, crossed
  strap bands).
- **`stunspore` (salt 310)** — a low mushroom-cap silhouette (walkable, same
  non-hazard shape family as Sand Trap) with drifting spore dots standing in
  for the freeze-on-contact effect. 5 variants mirror `frostvent`'s mote
  patterns: three even, two wide, four tight, one central puff, five
  scattered.
- **`turretspinner` (salt 311)** — deliberately excluded from the generic
  `ob.kind.indexOf('turret') === 0` prefix match at the top of the turret
  branch (see that condition's `&& ob.kind !== 'turretspinner'` guard) because
  it never aims at fixed `def.angles` — it leaks one bolt per tick around a
  full circle (`def.spin`), so its barrels are drawn spinning continuously
  off `now` (`base = dir * rate * now`) rather than pointing a fixed
  direction. 5 variants vary barrel count (2/3/4/6) and spin rate/direction
  (slow, fast, fast-reverse).
- **`glasscolumn` (salt 312)** — a tall thin translucent column (`solid`,
  1 hp) rather than a rounded rock body, so it visibly reads as "shatters in
  one hit" rather than "needs several hits" the way `glimmerrock`/
  `tintedrock`'s rounded rock silhouettes do. 5 variants add a crack overlay:
  none, single diagonal, zigzag, horizontal fracture, or an X cross.
- **`sparkbush` (salt 313)** — a squat bush silhouette (same family as
  `thornbush`) with three spark buds in `def.boltColor` standing in for the
  3-bolt `spreadShots` it fires. 5 variants vary bud placement: even fan,
  tight cluster, wide fan, asymmetric left-heavy, asymmetric right-heavy.
- **`magmapod` (salt 314)** — a round organic shell (attackable) with glowing
  heat-crack lines in `def.color`; destroying it triggers the same
  `explodesOnDestroy` blast as Bomb Barrel, and since there is no separate
  fire-spawn mechanic to draw for this kind, the blast itself is the payoff
  the crack pattern is telegraphing. 5 variants: single jag, Y-fork, two
  parallel cracks, a ring crack, and a star burst.

### 1b. Glow+glint quality-bar pass — every `drawObstacle` branch

`luckcrystal` (salt 206) was the one branch with a full "ambient glow off the
body + a `Theme.shadow.glint`-colored 1px highlight dot" treatment
(`ctx.shadowColor`/`ctx.shadowBlur`, skipped whenever `flash` is true, same
as every hit-flash gate elsewhere in the function). This pass brought every
other branch up to that same bar, purely as an overlay — no salt added, no
variant geometry/shape changed, no silhouette/hitbox/gameplay math touched.
Per branch: `pit` — glint only (no glow: a void has no light source), gated
on the same `!(m & PIT_N)` edge condition the far-wall lip already used, so
the `PIT_*` mask math is untouched. `cactus`, `spike`/`spiketrap`/
`movingspike`, `spikedrock`, `thornbush`, `bombbarrel`/`pushablebombbarrel`
(glow added around the fuse spark specifically, being the natural light
source), `dustvent`, `crushvent`, and the default rock/hardrock/tallrock/
tallhardrock branch (glow+glint added to the existing `!flash` rim-facet
block **without** any `plain`-based gating, so `phantomwall`, always pinned
to `rkV = 0`, stays pixel-identical to `tallhardrock`'s variant 0) — all got
both a new glow pass and a new glint dot. `yellowfire`/`redfire`/`bluefire`/
`purplefire`/`greenfire`/`whitefire`/`blackfire` and `tintedrock` already had
an ambient glow from earlier passes, so only the glint dot was added.
`turret*` got glow+glint added strictly inside its existing
housing-decoration `if (!flash)` block, after the housing-variant switch —
never touching barrel angle, the targeting eye, or spin/fire math. `current`
got a glow on its static base ellipse fill (before `translate`/`rotate`) and
one glint at a fixed point in the rotated local coordinate space, placed so
neither touches `ang`, `scroll`, `curV`, or the chevron loop's position math.
`lurehorn` already had a full glow+glint-equivalent (a `shadowBlur` glow on
the bolt tip in `def.boltColor`) — left as-is since it's load-bearing (the
tip glow reads as the homing-bolt charge, not decoration) rather than
duplicated with a second generic dot. `mud` and `sandtrap` were judgment
calls: `mud` keeps its existing ad hoc `rgba(255,255,255,.18)` sky-reflection
highlight untouched (it already serves the glint role) and got no new
ambient glow (a puddle has no light source of its own); `sandtrap` got a
`Theme.shadow.glint` dot only, no glow, for the same no-light-source
reasoning as `pit`.

### 1c. New room templates (2026 new-objects-and-rooms batch)

Six new hand-authored templates, split between two goals: one showcase room
per new obstacle kind (`normal-1.js`), and extra floor-feature variety for
existing underused kinds on floors that already had a feature-room pool
(`stage4-6/7-9/10-13-floorfeature.js`). None of the six added a new floor tag
or touched `obstacleAllowedOnFloor` — every one restricts itself (via `f:`)
to floors its obstacle kind(s) were already eligible on.

- **`js/data/roomTemplates/normal-1.js` — "Powder Alley"** (`pushablebombbarrel`,
  no `f` restriction, ordinary `normal` pool). A corridor room built around
  shoving a powder keg into a fixed detonation slot rather than fighting near
  it directly — the only Part 2b template outside the floorfeature pool.
- **`js/data/roomTemplates/stage4-6-floorfeature.js`, floors 15/16 — "Frozen
  Chute"** (`iceslidae`/`iceslidas`). An L-shaped ice slide (east leg turning
  south) with two pits at the inside corner, clear of both doors.
- **`js/data/roomTemplates/stage4-6-floorfeature.js`, floors 19/20 —
  "Undertow"** (`tidesurgee`/`tidesurgew`, `tidepool`). Two short opposed
  surge lanes one tile off the north/south walls with four tide pools
  between them, both lanes clear of the door bands.
- **`js/data/roomTemplates/stage4-6-floorfeature.js`, floor 18 — "Ashfall
  Approach"** (`dustvent`, `lurehorn`). A 2-block room pairing dustvent's
  Badlands half with a lure horn sighted down the seam; lurehorn's usual home
  is Deep Dark (floors 29/30), but `obstacleAllowedOnFloor` has no
  restriction on it, so nothing engine-side stops the pairing — it rides on
  dustvent's `f:[18]` tag rather than getting its own.
- **`js/data/roomTemplates/stage7-9-floorfeature.js`, floors 21/22 —
  "Backflow Pocket"** (`riptidee`/`riptidew`). Two short opposed riptide
  lanes one tile off the north/south walls with four bare rocks kept off the
  room's centre as the only cover between them.
- **`js/data/roomTemplates/stage10-13-floorfeature.js`, floors 33/34 —
  "Split Fold"** (`warpstreame`/`warpstreamw`). Two opposed warp lanes along
  the top/bottom walls with four tall-rock bumpers kept off both the centre
  and the lanes.

All six were run through `tools/lint-room-templates.js` after authoring;
three ("Frozen Chute", "Undertow", "Backflow Pocket") initially placed a
hazard-line endpoint inside the tool's 2-tile door-clearance zone and were
each fixed by sliding the line one row further from the wall (y=3/y=8 instead
of y=2/y=9) — no obstacle kind, floor tag, or room shape changed. See
`feature-research/new-objects-and-rooms/audit.md` for the full before/after
and the complete lint run.

### 2. Fire log base — fire branch of `Util.drawObstacle`

Drawn logs → `Theme.shadow.groundSoft` ellipse → flame. Fixed palette
`LOG = '#6d4c2f'`, `LOG_DK = '#3d2a19'` — deliberately not `def.color`/`def.dark`,
which are the flame's colors. `fireV` (salt 202, 5 variants, shared by all seven
colored fire kinds) picks the log arrangement and the matching flame-tip
`lean` together off one roll: `0`/default = 2 logs crossed at `±0.35` rad
(lean 0, the original look), `1` = 3 logs fanned at `-0.5/0.05/0.55` (lean
-2), `2` = 2 logs at `-0.16/0.62` (lean 2), `3` = a single log at `0.7` (lean
4, a sparse-fire read), `4` = 4 logs stacked at `±0.6/±0.15` (a dense
bonfire read). Logs are 20×4.8 with `LOG_DK` end caps. Under `flash` the logs
fill `HIT` and end caps are skipped.

### 3. Ambient fire light — `FIRE_LIGHT_R`, `_fireLightSprites`, `fireLightSprite(color)`, `Game.prototype.drawFireLight()`

`fireLightSprite(color)` lazily bakes one `FIRE_LIGHT_R * 2` (=160px) radial
gradient canvas per distinct flame color into the module-level `Map`
`_fireLightSprites` (stops `0.15 → 0.075 → 0.022 → 0`); `def.color` is parsed as
6-digit hex with a warm-ember `255,170,90` fallback. `drawFireLight()` — called
in `render()` immediately after `drawPlayerLight()`, same layer rule — walks
`currentRoom.obstacles`, keeps `ob.isHazard && ob.kind.indexOf('fire') !== -1`
(the `combat-4.js` convention), culls off-camera, and opens
`save()` + `'lighter'` lazily via an `opened` flag so fire-free rooms cost no
state change. No time input, so nothing to desync; `this.now` is not needed.

### 4. `fireHeartDrop(kind)` — `data/collectibles.js`

Returns `{id, chance}` or `null`: yellow/red fire → `heartRed` 0.10,
blue/purple → `heartBlue` 0.10, green/white/black → `eternalheart` 0.04. Lives in
`collectibles.js` because all three destroy paths need it
(`damageObstacleHit` in `combat-1.js`; `explodeAt` and `destroyAllObstacles` in
`combat-3.js`) and that file (`index.html:447`) loads before all of them and
already owns `OBSTACLES`. Each call site keeps the existing
`if (ob.def.heartDropChance)` guard and falls through to the plain `heartRed`
roll when the helper returns `null`, so non-fire obstacles (incl.
`thornbush`/`glowbloom`) are unchanged. Data-file `heartDropChance` values were
**not** edited — the helper's chance overrides for fires only.

## Floor/wall/door visual rebuild — `ui/render.js`

Ground-up repaint of the tile-cache brush strokes (Slice 1 of the wider visual
revamp; obstacles/lighting/minimap/dungeon logic untouched). Architecture is
identical — `rebuildTileLayer`'s per-tile bake loop, `isSolid()` corner-aware
adjacency, `tileRand(x,y,salt)`, `flavorMap()`/`roomFlavor()`,
`currentPalette()`, the tile-cache staleness check, `drawLockedDoorPulse()`,
and the door-unlock FX flash in `drawTiles()` — only what gets drawn changed.
No new `Theme`/`stages.js` palette fields were needed.

* **Wall branch** (`T_WALL`/`T_SECRET` in `rebuildTileLayer`) — each block now
  fills with a top-lit vertical `createLinearGradient` wash (derived from the
  existing salt-11 per-block shade) instead of a flat fill. The corner-aware
  bevel (`isSolid()`-derived `openN/E/S/W`, unchanged logic) now paints as 2px
  inset `fillRect` bands instead of 1px strokes. New: a horizontal coursing
  seam on ~60% of blocks (salts **201–202**); ice flavor's old diagonal sheen
  streak is now a triangular frost-patch polygon creeping from a bottom
  corner (reuses salts 61–64, adds none); a new fire-flavor ember-glint dot
  near an open edge (salts **203–204**). Mortar is now a double keyline (the
  existing `pal.grout` strokeRect plus a fainter lighter inset stroke).
  Weathering: crack unchanged (salts 3–8, 29); the old single moss dot is now
  a 3-speck lichen cluster (new salts **210–211, 215–216, 220–221**, i.e.
  `210+i/215+i/220+i` for `i` in 0–2).
* **Floor branch** — checkerboard base + salt-41 shade variance kept as-is,
  now finished with a per-tile inset highlight sliver (top/left) and a
  `pal.grout`-toned seam `strokeRect` around every floor tile (floors
  previously had no seam at all). The ornate boss/treasure/crystal motif
  (salt 53, unchanged trigger) is now a compass-rosette (the old diamond core
  plus four short outward spurs) instead of a bare diamond; the crystal-flavor
  glint extension is unchanged. AO edge darkening and the fire hard-shadow
  edge are unchanged. Grit speckle dots are now short angled grain/fiber
  flecks reusing the same trigger/position salts (7, 50+i, 60+i, 70+i) plus
  one new angle salt **80+i**. The hairline crack is unchanged (91–95).
* **`paintDoorTile(ctx,px,py,color)`** (signature unchanged) — redesigned as a
  recessed dark frame around a beveled inner panel lit by a vertical
  gradient wash (same light direction as the new wall wash), with a small
  two-tone rivet stud baked at each of the panel's four corners. Still a pure
  function of the one `color` input; still called identically from both the
  `T_DOOR` grid branch and the special-room door-slot pass.
* **`paintPortalTile(ctx,px,py,color)`** (signature unchanged) — the radial
  gradient's hot core is now off-center (upper-left) with an extra mid stop
  so the opening reads as a swirl instead of a flat lit disc; added a second,
  fainter inner ring alongside the existing bright/dark rings for more depth.
* **`paintStarfieldTile(...)`** — light touch-up only, per task scope: the
  flat `pal.voidC` fill is now a two-stop vertical gradient (`depth ± 0.03`)
  for consistency with the new lit-from-above floor/wall treatment. Star
  count/position/brightness/halo logic (salts 101–103, 110+i, 120+i, 130+i)
  is untouched.
* Judgment calls: left `theme.js` and `stages.js` untouched — the existing
  palette fields (`floorA/floorB/wall/voidC/doorOpen/doorLocked/grout/accent`)
  and `Theme.shadow`/`Theme.door`/`Theme.world` tokens were sufficient for
  every new brush stroke via `Util.shadeColor` derivation, so no new fields
  were added. `rebuildPlanetariumTiles` was not edited directly (not in the
  task's touch list) but inherits the `paintPortalTile`/`paintStarfieldTile`
  changes automatically since it calls them. New `tileRand` salts were all
  taken from previously-unused numbers (80+i, 201–204, 210–211/215–216/220–221)
  to avoid correlating with any existing wall/floor detail.
* Verified: `node --check js/ui/render.js` passes with no output.
  `theme.js`/`stages.js` were not modified, so no field-removal grep was
  needed for them.

## Minimap rebuild — pan/zoom/hover/pins (Slice 2 of the wider visual revamp) — `ui/ui.js`, new `ui/minimap-pins.js`, `main.js`, `index.html`

Adds a camera (zoom + pan) on top of the existing minimap, a hover tooltip
showing known loot in a room, and right-click/long-press pins. Dungeon
generation, fog-of-war semantics (`discovered`/`revealed`/`seen`/
`revealMap`), and `ui/render.js` floor/wall/door rendering are all untouched
(separate slices).

* **Camera** — `drawMinimap(game)` (`ui/ui.js`) still bakes the room-square/
  door-line offscreen cache (`_mmCanvas`/`_mmDungeon`/`_mmKey`) in the
  original unzoomed coordinate space; the cache key is unaffected by zoom/pan.
  Camera state is four module-level vars: `_mmZoom` (1–3, `MM_ZOOM_MIN`/
  `MM_ZOOM_MAX`/`MM_ZOOM_STEP=0.25`), `_mmPanX`/`_mmPanY` (screen px), and
  `_mmUserAdjusted`. Both the cache blit and the live overlay loop (pulsing
  ring, type icons, loot markers, pin badges) are wrapped in a single
  `ctx.translate(...); ctx.scale(_mmZoom,_mmZoom);` pivoting at the canvas
  center, so no drawing code needed zoom-awareness beyond the wrapper.
  `resetMinimapCamera()` zeroes all three (wired to the new `#minimapZoomResetBtn`).
  Walking into a new room resets `_mmPanX/_mmPanY` to 0 but **preserves**
  `_mmZoom` across the transition (judgment call — recentering avoids the
  view landing off-cache, but forcing zoom back to 1x on every step felt
  disruptive to a player who zoomed in to plan a route).
* **Input** (`ui/ui.js` handlers, wired from `main.js`) — `minimapHandleWheel`
  does cursor-anchored zoom (unprojects the cursor to map-space, rescales,
  re-solves pan so that point stays under the cursor), clamped via
  `Util.clamp`. `minimapHandlePointerDown/Move/Up` implement click-drag pan
  (a 2px move threshold distinguishes a drag from a click/long-press).
  `minimapUnprojectNode(game, canvas, clientX, clientY)` inverts the camera
  transform and rounds to the nearest room via `_mmBlockMap` (a `Map` from
  `"gx,gy"` block-coord string to owning room node, rebuilt alongside the
  bake cache). All coordinate math accounts for `canvas.width/rect.width`
  scaling, since the mobile CSS `transform:scale(.85)` on `#minimapWrap`
  changes `getBoundingClientRect()` without changing the canvas's internal
  150×150 resolution — the same ratio-fix the main game canvas already used.
* **Hover tooltip** — `updateMinimapTooltip`/`hideMinimapTooltip` (`ui/ui.js`)
  drive a DOM panel (`#minimapTooltip` > `#minimapTooltipTitle` +
  `#minimapTooltipCanvas`, new markup in `index.html`), positioned next to
  the cursor. Title uses `knowsType` (`discovered||revealed||revealMap`),
  falling back to `'Unexplored'`, with `' (here)'` appended for the current
  room. Loot is only listed when `node.discovered` is true (never leaks
  contents of a room only known-to-exist or Lunar-Affinity-revealed) —
  reuses the existing `roomLootEntries(node)` + `drawLootMarkers(ctx,...)`
  from the pre-existing minimap code, drawn into the tooltip's own small
  canvas instead of a parallel rendering path. The canvas is hidden via
  `.hidden` when a room has no uncollected loot.
* **Pins** — new file `ui/minimap-pins.js`: `MINIMAP_PIN_ICONS =
  ['⭐','💀','❓','❗']`, cycled by `cycleMinimapPin(game, roomId)`
  (no-pin → star → skull → question → exclamation → no-pin), read by
  `getMinimapPinIcon(game, roomId)`, drawn by `drawMinimapPin(ctx,x,y,icon,
  cellSize)` at a corner offset (`toScreen(node.gx-0.25, node.gy-0.25)`) so
  it never overlaps the centered type-icon/loot-marker stack. An in-memory
  cache (`_pinsCache`/`_pinsCacheKey`) avoids re-parsing localStorage every
  frame. Triggered by right-click (`contextmenu`, suppressed via
  `preventDefault`) on desktop or a 500ms long-press (`pointerdown` +
  `setTimeout`, cancelled on drag-movement or `pointerup`) on touch, wired in
  `main.js`. Pins are allowed on any room whose *existence* is known
  (`discovered||seen||revealed||revealMap`), not just discovered ones —
  judgment call, since a pin is a player planning aid ("come back here")
  rather than information that could leak room contents.
* **Persistence** (`main.js`) — `minimapPinsStorageKey(game)` builds
  `'nightfallMinimapPins_' + seedInt + '_' + floorNum` from
  `game.runSeed.int`/`game.dungeon.floorNum` (both null-safe, default `0`).
  `loadMinimapPins`/`saveMinimapPins` both route through that one function
  (grepped to confirm no key-string duplication) and follow the existing
  try/catch localStorage convention. Pins are keyed per-room-id inside a
  plain object, so they persist across a floor as fog-of-war expands and
  reset automatically on a new seed/floor.
* **New markup** (`index.html`, inside `#minimapWrap`) — `#minimapZoomResetBtn`
  (mirrors the existing `#minimapLegendBtn` circular-button styling, new
  `style.css` rule) and `#minimapTooltip`/`#minimapTooltipTitle`/
  `#minimapTooltipCanvas` (new `.minimap-tooltip` glass-panel styling reusing
  `--panel-glass`/`--border-soft`/`--radius-md`/`--shadow-lift`). `#minimap`
  itself gained `cursor:grab`/`:active{cursor:grabbing}` as a drag affordance.
* Judgment calls: `style.css` was touched even though not in the original
  file list — treated as necessary supporting scope for the two new buttons/
  tooltip panel, not a scope addition. Zoom range fixed at 1x–3x in
  `MM_ZOOM_STEP=0.25` increments. Long-press was implemented directly with a
  `setTimeout`/`pointerdown` pair rather than through `ui/touch-controls.js`,
  to keep the new logic self-contained in the minimap's own handlers.
* Verified: `node --check` passes with no output on `js/ui/ui.js`,
  `js/ui/minimap-pins.js`, and `js/main.js`. Grepped `minimapZoomResetBtn`,
  `minimapTooltip`/`minimapTooltipTitle`/`minimapTooltipCanvas` to confirm
  each new id is declared once in `index.html` and referenced from
  `main.js`/`ui/ui.js`. Grepped `nightfallMinimapPins_` /
  `minimapPinsStorageKey` to confirm `loadMinimapPins` and `saveMinimapPins`
  both build the key through the same function (no duplicated key string).


## Three new room types — Mirror / Karma / Boss Challenge — `systems/dungeon.js`, `systems/room.js`, new `systems/ai-mirrorboss.js`, new `systems/karma.js`, `systems/combat-2.js`, `systems/combat-3.js`, `game.js`, `ui/render.js`, `achievements/logic.js`, `data/items-8.js`, `index.html`

Three special room types added end-to-end. No new room templates were needed
(`ROOM_TEMPLATES[type] || []` already falls back to plain rooms), and no new
`drawEnemy` branch was needed (the mirror boss reuses the generic enemy draw).

### Generation — `systems/dungeon.js`

`'mirror'`, `'karma'`, `'bosschallenge'` are added to `SPECIAL_ROOM_TYPES` and
to `AUTO_OPEN_ROOM_TYPES`. `DUNGEON_CONFIG.specialChances` gains
`karma: 0.22` and `bosschallenge: 0.20`; the `weightedGroupPick` pools become
Group A `['curse','sacrifice','challenge','miniboss','bosschallenge']` and
Group B `['shrine','petshop','vault','arcade','karma']`, so each group still
guarantees at most one of its mutually-exclusive rooms per floor. The mirror
room is not in either pool — it is floor-gated:
`const mirrorNode = (floorNum % 5 === 0) ? attachSpecial('mirror') : null;`

### Mirror room — `systems/room.js` + `systems/ai-mirrorboss.js`

`populateRoom` places one `'mirror'`-pool pedestal at `tileH * 0.78` and, if
no `isMirrorBoss` enemy is present, spawns the mirror boss at `tileH * 0.28`
via `findClearFloorSpot` + `spawnMirrorBoss`, then sets `node.doorsOpen =
false`. The live player is fetched through `activeGame()` (logic.js:316)
inside a `try` so population never throws when no game is active.
`itemPoolForRoomType` and the pedestal-pool ternary both map
`node.type === 'mirror'` to the `'mirror'` pool.

`spawnMirrorBoss(player, tx, ty, floorNum)` builds a synthetic enemy type
from the player's live stats — damage `(meleeDamage + rangedDamage) * 0.5`,
hp `MIRROR_BOSS_BASE_HP + (melee+ranged) * MIRROR_BOSS_HP_PER_DAMAGE` clamped
to `MIRROR_BOSS_MAX_HP` (90 / 26 / 460), speed `* 0.92`, `fireCooldown *
2.2`, `boltSpeed * 0.72`, `shotCount` from `multishotExtra` — constructs it
as `new Boss(type, tx, ty, floorNum)` for boss-tier scaling, then
**deliberately sets `boss.isBoss = false`** and tags `isMirrorBoss = true`.
That flag choice is load-bearing: real `isBoss` entities route through
combat-2.js into `game.onBossDefeated()`, which would plant `node.stairsSpot`
and a boss pedestal, letting the player skip the floor's real boss. The clone
also carries `mirrorClass` (`player.classId`), `mirrorFlags`
(copy of `tearFlags`), `mirrorLayers` (copy of `attackLayers`), `mirrorLuck`,
`mirrorCrit`. `mirrorLayers` is live-executed — see the layer wiring below.

Bestiary integration: since the real spawned mirror boss has a per-run
dynamic `name`/`color` (mirrors whichever class it's cloned from) it has no
place in the normal per-stage `BOSS_TYPES`/`BOSS_LIST` spawn pool — adding it
there would let it be picked as a random real boss via the stage-fallback
branches in `room.js` (`pickBossForStage`/`pickBossForFloorKey`). Instead
`bosses.js` exports a separate `BOSS_LIST_BESTIARY_EXTRA` array. That array
now holds **28 static entries, one per class** — id `'mirrorboss_' +
classId`, a class-flavoured display name (`'The Mirror: Tiller'`,
`'The Mirror: Chassis'`, …), a one-line `desc` describing that clone's actual
fight pattern, `color` copied from that class's `CLASSES` colour, shared
`dark:'#2b2f45'`, shared representative stats and `stage:'universal'`. The
spawned clone's synthetic type id is likewise `'mirrorboss_' +
(player.classId || 'default')`, which is what makes each of the 28 entries
individually discoverable: combat-2.js records kills via
`bumpBestiaryCount('enemyKills', enemy.type.id, 1)`.
**Invariant: these 28 entries must never be added to `BOSS_TYPES` /
`BOSS_LIST`.** `room.js`'s `Util.choice(pool.length ? pool : BOSS_LIST)`
fallback makes anything in `BOSS_LIST` spawn-eligible as a real floor boss;
the separate array is the entire mechanism preventing that.
`bestiary.js`'s Bosses category list and its
`bestiaryDiscoveredTotals()` enemy-total count both concat
`BOSS_LIST_BESTIARY_EXTRA` onto `BOSS_LIST` so the mirror boss shows up and
counts toward completion, without ever being spawn-eligible.

`ROOM_TYPE_LIST` (`data/economy.js`) — the Room Types bestiary tab's static
registry — gained entries for `mirror`, `karma`, `bosschallenge`, and the
pre-existing `supersecret` (wave-2 room type that had been left out of this
list). `markBestiarySeen('seenRoomTypes', node.type, ...)` in game.js is
generic over `node.type`, so no other wiring was needed once the ids existed
in the list.

AI dispatch is one handler:

```js
ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS.mirrorboss = function aiMirrorBoss(game, e, dt){
  mirrorTickDelayed(game, e, dt);
  const fn = MIRROR_BOSS_BEHAVIORS[e.mirrorClass] || MIRROR_BOSS_BEHAVIORS.default;
  fn(game, e, dt);
};
```

`MIRROR_BOSS_BEHAVIORS` holds a real signature hook for **all 28 classIds**
(`earth`, `pegasus`, `unicorn`, `batpony`, `zebra`, `hypogriff`, `seapony`,
`ponybot`, `griffin`, `kirin`, `dragon`, `windigo`, `kelpie`, `breezie`,
`dnbpony`, `crystalpony`, `mule`, `alicorn`, `changeling`, `diamonddog`,
`gargoyle`, `changedling`, `changelingqueen`, `filly`, `engineerpony`,
`chudfilly`, `chadfilly`, `snowpitymare`) plus a `default` fallback that is
now only reached when `mirrorClass` is missing/unknown. Each hook reflects
that class's real kit flavour from `CLASSES` in `data/core.js` — e.g.
`ponybot` sweeps a lock-on piercing laser, `changelingqueen` summons capped
`swarmerdnb` broods, `engineerpony` plants a static firing position that
keeps shooting from where it was dropped, `gargoyle` alternates a shielded
stationary ring turret with chase phases.

Shared primitives, all in `ai-mirrorboss.js`: `mirrorState(e)` (lazy
`e._mirror` scratch state), `mirrorBoltOpts(e)`, `mirrorFire`, `mirrorRing`,
`mirrorBlast`, `mirrorApproach`, plus the newer
`mirrorDelay(e, time, fn)` / `mirrorTickDelayed(game, e, dt)` timer pair
(queues onto `e._mirrorDelayed`, fires only while `game.state === 'playing'`
and `!e.isDead`), `mirrorShotFrom(game, e, x, y, ang, speedMul, damageMul)`
(raw shot from an arbitrary origin via a ghost shooter object),
`mirrorArc`, `mirrorSpray`, and `mirrorSummon(game, e, typeId, count, cap)`.
Adding a class hook later means adding one key to `MIRROR_BOSS_BEHAVIORS` —
no dispatch change.

**`mirrorLayers` execution wiring.** `mirrorLayers` used to be dead data
(set at spawn, never read). It is now consumed by
`mirrorRunLayers(game, e, ang)`, which is called as the last statement of
both `mirrorFire` (with the aim angle) and `mirrorRing` (with the ring
offset) — so every mirror boss's attacks carry that class's signature
attack-style, not just flag-based pierce/homing. `mirrorRunLayers` walks
`e.mirrorLayers`, keeps a per-layer counter in `mirrorState(e)` under key
`'lc' + i`, and only invokes the style once every `layer.every` shots
(default 4). `MIRROR_LAYER_STYLES` maps a style name to an enemy-side
implementation: `mineLayer`, `skyfall`, `groundSlam`, `chargeNova`,
`beamSweep`, `scatterVolley`, `echoShot`, `whipArc`, `orbitBlades`,
`chainLightning`, `gravityWell`, `trailBurn`, `singularity`, plus aliases
(`laggedEcho`/`mirrorConvert` → `echoShot`,
`ricochetBolt`/`onKillFragments` → `scatterVolley`, `guardianPulse` →
`orbitBlades`, `knockbackPulse`/`impactBurst` → `groundSlam`,
`frostShatter` → `chargeNova`, `venomBloom` → `trailBurn`, `bloodPact` →
`whipArc`, `markedForDeath` → `chainLightning`). These are deliberately
*not* the player handlers from `systems/attackStyles.js`:
`CAST_ATTACK_STYLES`/`HIT_ATTACK_STYLES` are hard-coded to `game.player` and
damage `node.enemies`, so they are unusable for an enemy shooter; the
mirror-side implementations reproduce each style's feel against the player
instead. Because `mirrorRunLayers` is called *from* `mirrorFire`/`mirrorRing`,
layer handlers must never call those back — they use only the raw
`mirrorShotFrom`/`mirrorArc`/`mirrorSpray`/`mirrorBlast`/
`fireProjectileAngle` primitives, and an `e._mirrorLayerBusy` reentrancy
guard backstops that rule.

On death, combat-2.js's drop chain gets an explicit branch **before** the
miniboss branch so mirror bosses do not roll miniboss drops:

```js
} else if (enemy.isMirrorBoss) {
  bumpStat('mirrorBossesDefeated', 1, game);
} else if (enemy.isMiniboss) {
```

### Karma room — `systems/room.js` + new `systems/karma.js` + `ui/render.js`

Five machines. The coin machine reuses the existing shop plumbing verbatim:
`node.donationMachine = { x, y }` at `tileH * 0.22`, drawn by the existing
`drawDonationMachineFixture`, spent by the existing `tryDonateMachine` with
its existing `DONATION_CAP` / `DONATION_SKILL_POINT_INTERVAL` behavior. The
four resource machines are new: `node.karmaMachines` entries
`{ resource, x, y }` (tile coords) for `key`/`bomb`/`heart`/`familiar` at
`(0.2,0.45)`, `(0.8,0.45)`, `(0.3,0.78)`, `(0.7,0.78)`, deduped against
already-taken spots.

`KARMA_MACHINE_DEFS` is the whole balance table — **total unlocks** and
**cost per unlock**, not cost per unit:

| resource | totalUnlocks | perUnlock | donated stat | awarded stat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| key | 10 | 25 | `karmaKeysDonated` | `karmaKeyUnlocks` |
| bomb | 10 | 25 | `karmaBombsDonated` | `karmaBombUnlocks` |
| heart | 20 | 50 | `karmaHeartsDonated` | `karmaHeartUnlocks` |
| familiar | 10 | 3 | `karmaFamiliarsDonated` | `karmaFamiliarUnlocks` |

* `karmaMachineProgressFrac(resource)` — `donated / (totalUnlocks *
  perUnlock)`, clamped; feeds the fill bar.
* `karmaMachineFull(resource)` — awarded count has reached `totalUnlocks`;
  further donations are rejected with `Sound.play('uiDeny')` and a toast
  mirroring the shop's `DONATION_CAP` toast.
* `karmaSpendResource(game, resource)` — the per-resource guard/spend. Keys
  and bombs need `>= 1`; hearts require `player.totalHearts() > 1` (never
  spend your last heart) and drain via `player.spendHearts(1)`; familiars pop
  the last entry of `player.familiars` (the `Familiar` ctor's `index` only
  seeds an initial angle, so no reindexing is needed).
* `awardKarmaUnlocks(game, resource)` — modeled on
  `awardDonationSkillPoints`: recomputes `eligible = min(totalUnlocks,
  floor(donated / perUnlock))`, diffs it against the awarded stat, and adds
  the difference to both `unlocks.skillTree.points` and
  `.lifetimeEarned` before `saveUnlocks`. Idempotent, so a mid-run reload
  cannot double-pay.
* `findNearestKarmaMachine(node, player)` — nearest machine within 30px,
  matching the existing fixture proximity gate (`m.x * TILE`, `m.y * TILE`).
* `tryDonateKarmaMachine(game, resourceType)` — the entry point. `'coin'`
  (or no machine in range) delegates to `tryDonateMachine(game)`; otherwise
  it spends, emits a `FloatText`, `bumpStat`s the donated stat, calls
  `awardKarmaUnlocks`, and logs `game.logEvent('karma', ...)`.

`Game.prototype.drawKarmaFixtures()` (registered in the fixture draw order
just before `drawRerollAltarFixture`) reuses `Util.drawDonationMachine` with
the per-resource progress fraction and labels each machine with its donated
total and `awarded/totalUnlocks`.

Both `Game.prototype.tryDonate()` and the donate/arcade interact path route
to `tryDonateKarmaMachine(this)` when `currentRoom.type === 'karma'` **and**
`currentRoom.karmaMachines.length` is nonzero — mirroring exactly how the
shop-room branch requires `currentRoom.donationMachine` to be present before
calling `tryDonateMachine`, so a karma-typed room with no machines placed
falls through to the arcade-interact path instead of silently no-opping.

### Boss challenge room — `systems/room.js` + `systems/combat-3.js` + `game.js`

**Reworked 2026 (pedestal-gated, single boss, same-stage pool).** Population
now mirrors the ordinary `challenge` room: if the room has no pedestals yet it
places one `pickItemFromPool('challenge')` pedestal at room center, then sets
`challengeStarted = false`, `challengeWave = 0`, `challengeTotalWaves = 1`.
The room no longer arms on entry — the `enterRoom` auto-start line is gone.
Instead the pedestal-pickup loop in `game.js` (the same loop that calls
`startChallengeRoom` for `challenge` rooms) calls
`startBossChallengeRoom(this, node)` when `node.type === 'bosschallenge'` and
the room is neither started nor cleared. That closes the doors, marks
`tileLayerDirty`, and spawns the single boss. The post-clear
`pickAboveQuality1()` reward is unchanged, so the room now pays out twice
(pedestal item on entry + reward on clear) for one boss fight.

`spawnBossChallengeWave(game, node)` increments `challengeWave`, picks a boss
via `resolveBossChallengeBoss(floorNum, branch, floorPath)` — now a thin
delegate to `resolveGenericBoss(floorNum, branch, floorPath)`, i.e. **the same
pool a normal floor boss on this floor would draw from**, no longer the
previous stage's pool — constructs `new Boss(...)` near the room center and
sets `isBoss = false; isChallengeBoss = true` for the same stairs/pedestal
reason as the mirror boss, then toasts `Boss challenge!`. With
`challengeTotalWaves = 1` the wave loop below fires exactly once.

`checkRoomCleared` gains two branches: while `challengeStarted` and
`challengeWave < challengeTotalWaves`, clearing the room spawns the next wave
and returns `false`; on the final clear it sets `challengeRewarded`, bumps
`bossChallengesCompleted`, and drops one `pickAboveQuality1()` item on a
pedestal at a `findClearFloorSpot` near the room center.

`pickAboveQuality1()` (room.js) filters `ITEM_LIST` by `available` +
`notCapped` + `(i.quality || 1) > 1` and returns `Util.choice` of the result.

### Stats and labels

`statDefaults` (`achievements/logic.js`) gains `mirrorRoomsVisited`,
`karmaRoomsVisited`, `bossChallengeRoomsVisited`, `bossChallengesCompleted`,
`mirrorBossesDefeated`, plus the four `karma*Donated` and four
`karma*Unlocks` counters. `game.js`'s room-label map gains `mirror: 'Mirror
Room'`, `karma: 'Karma Room'`, `bosschallenge: 'Boss Challenge Room'`, and
the room-visit `bumpStat` chain gains one branch per type.

### New items — `data/items-8.js`

Five `pools:['mirror']` items (the mirror pedestal's only source), quality 3–4,
each declarative-only (`attackLayer` / `tearEffect`, no per-id systems code):
`reflectedvisage` (q4, `mirrorConvert`), `shatteredselfportrait` (q3,
`splitOnHit`), `twinfangmirror` (q3, `razor` shape + `whipArc`),
`echoingsilhouette` (q4, `laggedEcho` + `pullPulse`), `glasscoreheart` (q4,
`heavy` shape + `frostShatter`). No protected basic item id was touched.

`index.html` loads `js/systems/ai-mirrorboss.js` after the stage AI files and
`js/systems/karma.js` after `shop.js` (so `tryDonateMachine` is defined).

### Phase 20 — Crypt generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 1 (`ai-crypt3.js`)

Every generic `stage:0` enemy in `types-1.js` / `types-2.js` (40 ids — everything that is not
`stage:'universal'`, not `isMinion:true`, and not one of the crypt-extra / crypt-extra2 ids) now has
its own bespoke decision loop instead of sharing `aiChase` / `aiRanged` / `aiTurret` / etc. New file
`js/systems/ai-crypt3.js`, loaded from `index.html` **after** `ai-stage10-13.js` (it must load after
`ai-1.js`, which declares the `aiChase` / `aiTurret` globals it wraps).

**Two dispatch paths, because `combat-3.js`'s `updateEnemy` has two.** A hardcoded
`switch (e.behavior)` handles the legacy strings; only its `default:` branch consults
`ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS`. So:

- 35 ids simply got their `behavior:` field repointed at a new `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS.cr3*` key.
- 5 ids **keep** their original `behavior` string because other systems read it:
  `'turret'` (`utils-1.js` / `utils-2.js` sprite branches, `combat-3.js`'s familiar-contact
