  suppression and `fromTurret`), `'shielded'` (`entities.js` initial `this.shielded`, `combat-3.js`'s
  shield/vulnerable timer flip, sprite cache key), `'splitter'` (`combat-2.js`'s `handleEnemyDeath`
  split into `type.splitInto`). Renaming any of those would silently drop a visual or a mechanic.

- **`CRYPT3_ID_AI`** (new, `ai-crypt3.js`) — `e.type.id` → AI function table for exactly those 5.
  **`cryptWrapById(fn)`** returns a wrapper that runs the id override when present and otherwise
  delegates to the original shared handler; the file's last two lines reassign the globals
  (`aiChase = cryptWrapById(aiChase); aiTurret = cryptWrapById(aiTurret);`). `'shielded'` and
  `'splitter'` both route through `aiChase` in the switch, the two turrets through `aiTurret`, so
  those two wraps cover all five with no edit to `combat-3.js`. Every other enemy in the game keeps
  the untouched original behavior through the delegate.
- Local helpers: **`cryptStep(game,e,dt,dx,dy,mul)`** (normalized `tryMoveEntity` step, returns its
  `{movedX,movedY}` so callers can detect wall hits), **`cryptRing(game,e,count,speed,opts,offset)`**
  (evenly spaced full-circle volley), **`cryptArc(game,e,ang,count,spread,speed,opts)`** (fan).
  Per-instance scratch state uses `cr3*`-prefixed fields so it can never collide with the shared
  fields in `entities.js`.

**`types-1.js` roster** — gravegrub `cr3Gravegrub` (burrow/surface cycle: submerged sprint, surfaces
to bite); bonepicker `cr3Bonepicker` (hover, 0.35s 2.4x sprint, retreat); cryptslinger
`cr3Cryptslinger` (breaks line of sight on cooldown, peeks to fire a 3-bolt fan); **shellbone**
(exception) advances 1.35x while shielded and vents a 6-bolt ring the instant it turns vulnerable;
skullcharger `cr3Skullcharger` (telegraphed charge that ricochets off walls up to 3 times);
**graveturret** (exception) rotating dual-beam sweep that reverses when the player crosses the line;
cryptcrawler `cr3Cryptcrawler` (perimeter wall-runner, cuts straight across on row/column alignment);
tombguardian `cr3Tombguardian` (slow advance, roots and stomps an 8-bolt shockwave ring inside 110);
skeletalarcher `cr3Skeletalarcher` (0.7s draw, leads the player's velocity with a fast arrow);
gravewisp `cr3Gravewisp` (flier: lateral drift dropping slow trail bolts behind it, retreats when
closed on); deathrattler `cr3Deathrattler` (fuse only arms inside 70px, disarms with a 4-bolt shriek
if the player escapes); **boneguard** (exception) shield-bash dash while shielded, backs off while
vulnerable; hollowknight `cr3Hollowknight` (charge, parry pause, 5-bolt sword arc); **witchlantern**
(exception) alternates dim (shielded, no fire) and flare (4 diagonal bolts + a slow homing flame);
sarcophaguscrawler `cr3Sarcophaguscrawler` (lid-slam leap with a 3-bolt landing cone); wailingspecter
`cr3Wailingspecter` (keeps distance, 12-bolt expanding wail ring); cryptcircler `cr3Cryptcircler`
(spirals in to 46px, bursts a 6-bolt ring, spirals back out firing tangentially); gravedigger
`cr3Gravedigger` (backpedaling 3-bolt dirt throws, periodically burrows and resurfaces behind the
player — deliberately *not* the pit-spawning `sexton` gimmick); bonecaller `cr3Bonecaller` (flees,
goes stationary + shielded while chanting a summon); gravetender `cr3Gravetender` (seeks the
most-wounded ally to heal and shield it, else fires a 5-bolt ring); cryptmarksman `cr3Cryptmarksman`
(slow-tracking laser lock for 1.2s, then 2 quick shots at the locked point); cryptmite `cr3Cryptmite`
(flocking swarm with separation, faster the bigger the flock); urnlurker `cr3Urnlurker` (plays dead
and shielded until the player is inside 120, bursts with a 6-bolt nova and chases 3s); barrowblink
`cr3Barrowblink` (blinks to the point-reflection across the player, fires on arrival); cryptwarden
`cr3Cryptwarden` (plants a ward point, walks to unshielded allies, shields everyone inside the ward
radius); bonelobber `cr3Bonelobber` (delayed-impact lob that bursts 6 bolts at a stored point);
boulderroller `cr3Boulderroller` (permanently rolling and accelerating, bounces off walls, briefly
stunned on impact); shadestalker `cr3Shadestalker` (cloaks, reappears behind the player and fires);
boneskirmisher `cr3Boneskirmisher` (strafes between 3 triangle anchors, fires on each arrival);
rattleraider `cr3Rattleraider` (straight-line pass through the player firing sideways both ways).

**`types-2.js` roster** — pallweaver `cr3Pallweaver` (strafes perpendicular leaving near-static web
bolts); ossuarysentry `cr3Ossuarysentry` (rooted; fires a 5-shot burst only while the player's speed
is above a threshold, otherwise creeps forward); **tombbloater** (exception) inflates over 6s (radius
and speed grow, random bolts) then self-detonates, which lets the untouched `'splitter'` death path
split it into cryptmites; miasmadrifter `cr3Miasmadrifter` (flier: fixed heading, slow turn, trails
static gas clouds, bounces off walls); dirgechanter `cr3Dirgechanter` (escalating 1/3/5-bolt verses,
then a vulnerable rest); shroudmoth `cr3Shroudmoth` (flier: fluttering sine approach, dive-bombs
inside 90); charnelmites `cr3Charnelmites` (conga chain — each follows the nearest closer mite, the
head chases the player); cryptleech `cr3Cryptleech` (telegraph, then latches on draining 1 HP per
0.5s for 1.5s and healing itself, then flees); tombtoller `cr3Tombtoller` (1.5s shielded charge, then
a 16-bolt toll ring); boneskitter `cr3Boneskitter` (short erratic bursts with 90-degree direction
snaps, stationary between them).

Audit: `feature-research/crypt-enemy-rework/audit-batch1.md`.

### Phase 21 — Crypt generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 2 (`ai-crypt4.js`)

Batch 2 finishes the generic `stage:0` roster: the 13 remaining Crypt enemies that live outside
`types-1.js` / `types-2.js` — 6 in `js/data/enemies/types-4.js`, 2 in `js/data/enemies/flies.js`,
5 in `js/data/enemies/legacy-extra.js` — now each have a bespoke decision loop instead of sharing
`aiChase` / `aiRanged` / `aiFlyer` / `aiSwarm` / `aiTeleporter` / `aiLobber` / `aiPouncer` /
`aiStrafer` / `aiSplitshot`. New file `js/systems/ai-crypt4.js`, loaded from `index.html`
immediately after `ai-crypt3.js`.

**No `CRYPT3_ID_AI`-style exceptions this time.** A full re-audit of every non-dispatch
`.behavior` string read confirmed that none of the 13 ids carries a load-bearing string: the
load-bearing set is still exactly `'turret'` (`utils-1.js` / `utils-2.js` sprite branches,
`combat-3.js` familiar-contact suppression and `fromTurret`), `'shielded'` (`entities.js` initial
`this.shielded`, `combat-3.js` shield/vulnerable flip, sprite cache key) and `'splitter'`
(`combat-2.js` `handleEnemyDeath` split), and no batch-2 id used any of them. The remaining
`utils-2.js` branches for `'ranged'` / `'swarm'` / `'teleporter'` / `'lobber'` are cosmetic
sprite ornament only, and `'flyer'` is not load-bearing because flight reads the `flies` / `canFly`
**fields** (`utils-2.js`: `const flyer = behavior === 'flyer' || !!e.flies;`) — every flier in this
batch keeps `flies:true`. So all 13 ids simply got their `behavior:` field repointed at a new
`ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS.cr4*` key, `ai-crypt3.js` was not touched, and `combat-3.js` needed no edit.

- Local helpers, deliberately **self-contained** rather than reusing `ai-crypt3.js`'s globals (no
  name clobbering, no load-order coupling): **`crypt4Step(game,e,dt,dx,dy,mul)`** (normalized
  `tryMoveEntity` step, returns its `{movedX,movedY}` so callers can detect wall hits),
  **`crypt4Ring(game,e,count,speed,opts,offset)`** (evenly spaced full-circle volley),
  **`crypt4Arc(game,e,ang,count,spread,speed,opts)`** (fan), **`crypt4Bounds(node)`**
  (`{minX,maxX,minY,maxY}` playable-area rect from `node.tileW` / `node.tileH`). Per-instance
  scratch state uses `cr4*`-prefixed fields so it can never collide with the shared fields in
  `entities.js` or with batch 1's `cr3*` fields.

**`types-4.js` roster** — ossuarysaint `cr4Ossuarysaint` (plants a relic anchor, orbits it firing
aimed bolts, and only re-anchors on the player when the player leaves the guarded radius);
reliquarymite `cr4Reliquarymite` (straight-line pinball that only re-aims at the player on each wall
bounce); pallbearer `cr4Pallbearer` (shielded 0.7x carry phase → heaves a casket that lands after a
delay and bursts an 8-bolt ring at the stored point → unshielded 1.6x light phase); candlewake
`cr4Candlewake` (snuffs out `submerged`, relights halfway between itself and the player with a
3-bolt fan; inside 90px it detonates a 10-bolt nova and resets to the far corner); batscout
`cr4Batscout` (wide sine-weave approach, periodic 6-bolt echolocation screech, then a 0.4s 2.2x
straight dive); ravenpicker `cr4Ravenpicker` (perches on a room corner firing aimed bolts, flaps to
the corner furthest from the player when closed on inside 140, shedding perpendicular feather bolts
en route).

**`flies.js` roster** — dnbmoth `cr4Dnbmoth` (orbits a drifting flame point that creeps toward the
player, firing tangentially; dives at 2x when the player crosses the orbit circle); dnbmayfly
`cr4Dnbmayfly` (lifespan fuse — speed ramps 0.6x → 2.2x and the weave tightens over an 11s life,
then it flashes, bursts a 4-bolt puff and dies on its own via `handleEnemyDeath`).

**`legacy-extra.js` roster** — gravelurker `cr4Gravelurker` (buried `submerged`+`shielded` until the
player is inside 160, telegraph → committed 5.2x leap → re-buries at a nearby random spot instead of
chasing); bonerattler `cr4Bonerattler` (circles at 170 building a rattle charge, releases a 3-round
fast burst at full charge, charge resets to zero if the player closes inside 110); sepulchertwin
`cr4Sepulchertwin` (tracks the point-reflection of the player across room center and fires its 2-bolt
V only once correctly mirrored); coffincrawler `cr4Coffincrawler` (crawls at 0.75x shielded with the
lid closed; every 2.4s the lid pops for 1.1s — vulnerable, 1.8x, spitting a 5-bolt cone);
wraitharcher `cr4Wraitharcher` (phases out `submerged`, repositions to a line-of-sight point ~210
from the player, materializes, draws for 0.6s, fires a tight 3-arrow spread, phases out again).

Audit: `feature-research/crypt-enemy-rework/audit-batch2.md`.

### Phase 36 — Crypt generic-enemy texture pass (`CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS` / `Util._cryptMark`)

Phases 20 and 21 gave all 53 generic `stage:0` Crypt ids bespoke AI but left them sharing one
silhouette: `Util.drawBrownHumanoid` in `js/core/utils-2.js` draws every non-bespoke enemy from the
same body, and its ornament layer keys off `behavior` (plus a tiny `type.id` precedent for
`bumblebee` / `forestwasp` and `hive` / `waspine`), so a marksman, a leech and a lantern all read
identically. This phase makes each id visually distinct **without** 72 hand-written draw functions.

**`const CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS`** (`js/core/utils-2.js`, declared between `PONY_BUILD` and the
`Object.assign(Util, …)` block) — a flat id-keyed table, one entry per Crypt id, describing a single
accent to layer on the shared body. 72 ids: the 40 batch-1 ids, the 13 batch-2 ids, and the 19
pre-existing bespoke-AI crypt ids from `crypt-extra.js` / `crypt-extra2.js` (none of which had a
bespoke renderer, so none could be skipped). Entry fields are terse by design:
`k` mark kind (the only required field), `s` scale multiplier, `n` element count, `sd` side sign
(`1` right / `-1` left), `t` accent tint delta passed to `Util.shadeColor` (default `0.45`),
`g` glow flag (enables a pulsing `shadowBlur`), `sp` pulse period in ms (default `520`), plus a few
kind-local fields (`b` blade shape, `w` wing type, `len` leg length, `up` slab carried overhead).

**`Util._cryptMark(ctx, e, flash, now, phase, col, dark, r, hx, hy, m)`** — one renderer, an
if/else-if chain over `m.k` with **66 kinds**, drawn live on top of the (possibly baked) body from
canvas primitives only. Colors come from the enemy's own `color` / `dark` via `Util.shadeColor`, so
marks inherit per-enemy palettes and stage tinting instead of hardcoding new colors; `flash`
swaps them to `Theme.enemy.flash` / `Theme.enemy.flashSoft` so hit-flash still reads correctly.
Because marks are live-drawn ornaments rather than sprite content, `Util._humanoidSprite`'s cache
key is unchanged. Animation is driven by the caller's existing `phase` (`(e.x + e.y) * 0.05`) and
`now`, so identical ids desync naturally.

The 66 kinds: `rift`, `staff`, `shieldSlab`, `flail`, `beak`, `blade`, `legs`, `boulder`, `orbit`,
`spiral`, `maw`, `bow`, `antennae`, `sling`, `crown`, `rattle`, `notes`, `segments`, `sprout`,
`barrel`, `wisptail`, `helm`, `cloud`, `ribs`, `threads`, `horns`, `slab`, `hood`, `shell`, `wings`,
`quiver`, `skullface`, `blisters`, `pauldrons`, `bell`, `urn`, `waves`, `lantern`, `halo`, `gem`,
`candles`, `plume`, `motes`, `glyph`, `mound`, `spikes`, `double`, `nails`, `hexcells`, `bigeye`,
`fuse`, `pads`, `drips`, `coil`, `ghosttail`, `flames`, `sack`, `boxlid`, `chains`, `stack`,
`claws`, `tablet`, `veil`, `keys`, `mask`, `plates`.

**Marks are gimmick-aligned**, so the accent doubles as a tell for the Phase 20/21 AI: archers get
a drawn `bow` (wraitharcher's glows, matching its phase-out), skeletalarcher a `quiver`, boneguard
and pallbearer a shield `slab`, graveturret a gun `barrel`, tombtoller a `bell`, witchlantern and
candlewake light sources, cryptstrider two very long `legs` versus boneskitter's three short ones,
cryptjumper a compression `coil`, cryptwallhugger adhesive `pads`, sepulchertwin a mirrored
`double` outline, dnbmayfly a lifespan `glyph`, sexton a keyring, coffinlid a `boxlid`.

**Two call sites**, both in `drawBrownHumanoid`:
1. After the existing `const tid = e.type && e.type.id;` ornament branches and before the `bomber` /
   `isBoss` blocks — `const cmark = CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS[tid]; if (cmark && !isBoss) Util._cryptMark(…)`.
2. Inside the `behavior === 'turret'` early-return block, before its `drawEnemyHealthBar` call.
   `graveturret` is `behavior:'turret'`, so it returns long before site 1 and would otherwise never
   get its mark; the turret site recomputes `hx` / `hy` / `phase` locally.

`!isBoss` keeps marks off boss variants (which have their own crown/aura treatment), and the `tid`
guard already handles `js/ui/roomEditor.js`'s synthetic enemy objects, which carry no `type`.

Rendering-only phase: no AI file (`ai-crypt.js` … `ai-crypt4.js`) and no non-visual enemy data field
was touched.

Audit: `feature-research/crypt-enemy-rework/audit-batch3.md`.

### Phase 37 — Crypt floor: 10 new enemies (batch 4)

Purely additive content batch: 10 brand-new `stage:0` crypt enemies, each with its own AI behavior
key and its own `CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS` accent. Nothing in `ai-crypt.js` … `ai-crypt4.js`,
`crypt-extra.js`, `crypt-extra2.js` or the existing 72 mark entries was modified. Bestiary `desc`
fields are deliberately absent — those land in a later batch.

**New data file `js/data/enemies/crypt-extra3.js`** — one `Object.assign(ENEMY_TYPES, {…})` with the
10 definitions, script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after `crypt-extra2.js` and therefore
before `lists.js`, so `ENEMY_LIST = Object.values(ENEMY_TYPES)` picks them up automatically. All are
`stage:0`, `onlyFloorNum:0`, not minions, hp 5-8 / dmg 1-2 / speed 0-96 / radius 10-13, `xpTier` 1-2,
with `weight` below 1 on the two heaviest (`rookossuary` 0.8, `vaultjailer` 0.7).

**New AI file `js/systems/ai-crypt5.js`** — script-tagged right after `ai-crypt4.js`. Local helpers
mirroring the `crypt4*` set plus one new one: `crypt5Step`, `crypt5Ring` (gains an optional `skip`
index so a ring can be fired with a gap), `crypt5Arc`, `crypt5Bounds`, and `crypt5FireFrom(game, e,
x, y, fn)` which temporarily relocates the shooter so a volley originates from an arbitrary point.
Per-entity scratch state uses the `cr5*` field prefix, lazily initialised the same way `cr4*` does.

The 10 behaviors (`ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS.cr5*`, all fresh keys, none colliding with the
load-bearing `.behavior ===` strings `shielded` / `turret` / `splitter` or the familiar behaviors):

- `tombscribe` — `cr5Inkscribe`: orbits the *player* at radius 108 dropping a stationary ink node
  every `nodeInterval`; on the 4th node every node fires a bolt at the player at once and the set
  clears. Mark `quill` (feather nib plus a pulsing ink drop).
- `grudgebell` — `cr5Grudgebell`: charge accumulates only while the player is *closing* distance
  (per-frame distance delta), and it backs away while charging; a full charge discharges two rings
  of different speed and offset. Mark `clapper` (arc with a swinging clapper, glowing).
- `ashenwidow` — `cr5Ashenwidow`: damage-reactive — watches its own `hp` and on any drop fires a
  5-shot spread at the player and hops backwards for `recoilTime`; otherwise a plain slow approach.
  Mark `spinneret` (four trailing web strands from the rear).
- `sableescort` — `cr5Sableescort`: picks the lowest-hp living non-`shielded` ally from
  `game.currentRoom.enemies`, closes to `escortRadius` and grants it `shielded` while in range
  (clearing the flag when it switches or loses its ward); with no ally alive it converts into a fast
  1.5x direct charger. Mark `banner` (waving flag on a pole).
- `cindermarrow` — `cr5Cindermarrow`: walks straight at the player laying delayed-fuse detonation
  markers along its own path; each expires into an `Explosion` plus a proximity `damagePlayer`.
  Mark `embers` (rising, fading glowing specks).
- `rookossuary` — `cr5Rookossuary`: cardinal-only movement — slides along one axis until it shares
  the player's row, fires a fast lane lance down it, then flips to the other axis. Mark
  `battlement` (crenellated block above the head).
- `boneloom` — `cr5Boneloom`: stationary lighthouse with a continuously rotating aim firing a steady
  0.16s stream along the sweep; the sweep reverses whenever it crosses the player's bearing. Mark
  `shuttle` (spinning six-spoke wheel).
- `vaultjailer` — `cr5Vaultjailer`: on cooldown fires an 11-projectile slow ring *centred on the
  player* with one random gap (via `crypt5FireFrom` + `crypt5Ring`'s `skip`), then closes distance,
  backing off inside 70px. Mark `cage` (bars arcing around the body).
- `gristlehound` — `cr5Gristlehound`: records the player's position every 0.1s and chases the
  breadcrumb that is `trailLag` seconds old rather than the player; catching the trail head at close
  range triggers a short direct lunge at `lungeSpeed`. Mark `snout` (long snout with nostril dots).
- `relicwarden` — `cr5Relicwarden`: territorial — remembers its spawn point and only engages
  (1.45x speed, 2-shot bursts) while the player is inside `territory` of that point; outside it
  walks home and idles with a slow bob. Mark `reliquary` (domed ark/chest, glowing).

**Ten new `CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS` entries and ten new `Util._cryptMark` `else if` branches** in
`js/core/utils-2.js`, appended after `armoredsarcophagus` / the `plates` branch respectively, using
the same descriptor fields (`k`, `s`, `n`, `t`, `g`, `sp`) and the same `acc`/`deep`/`pul`/`lw`
locals as every existing branch. New kinds: `quill`, `clapper`, `spinneret`, `banner`, `embers`,
`battlement`, `shuttle`, `cage`, `snout`, `reliquary` — bringing the table to 82 entries / 76 kinds.
Both existing call sites in `drawBrownHumanoid` are untouched and pick the new ids up by id lookup.

Audit: `feature-research/crypt-enemy-rework/audit-batch4.md`.

### Phase 38 — Forest generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 1 (`ai-forest1.js`)

The Crypt equivalent of this pass is Phases 20/21/37; this is the same treatment applied to the
Forest floor's generic `stage:1` roster in `js/data/enemies/types-1.js`. Before it, 33 forest ids
(everything except the already-bespoke `rootgrower` / `treeburner` / `oilrig` and the three minions
`sprout` / `bumblebee` / `forestwasp`) shared 13 generic behaviors — five ids were plain `chaser`,
four were plain `ranged`, three were `summoner`, and so on. All 33 now have their own AI.

**New file `js/systems/ai-forest1.js`** — script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after
`ai-crypt5.js` (and therefore after `ai-1.js`, which defines the generic AI functions it wraps).
Structure mirrors `ai-crypt3.js` exactly:

- **`const FOREST_ID_AI`** — id-keyed override table, consulted before the generic function body.
- **`forestWrapById(fn)`** — returns a wrapper that dispatches to `FOREST_ID_AI[e.type.id]` when an
  entry exists and otherwise calls `fn`. Installed at the bottom of the file by reassigning the two
  globals it needs to intercept: `aiChase = forestWrapById(aiChase); aiTurret = forestWrapById(aiTurret);`.
  Because this file loads after `ai-crypt3.js`, it composes *over* the crypt wrapper rather than
  replacing it, so `CRYPT3_ID_AI` ids still resolve through the inner wrapper. No change to
  `updateEnemy` in `combat-3.js` was needed.
- Local helpers, all `forest*`-prefixed so they cannot collide with the `crypt*` / `crypt5*` sets:
  `forestStep(game, e, dt, dx, dy, mul)` (normalised obstacle-aware step, returns the
  `tryMoveEntity` result so handlers can detect wall contact), `forestRing`, `forestArc`,
  `forestAim(e, player)`, and `forestSpawn(game, node, id, x, y)` (spawns a minion at the nearest
  floor tile to an arbitrary point and returns it, so seeders can place spawns away from themselves).
- Per-entity scratch state uses the `fr1*` field prefix, lazily initialised on first tick.

**Three ids keep their original `behavior` string** because it is load-bearing elsewhere, and get
their AI through `FOREST_ID_AI` instead:

- `sapling` (`splitter`, read by `combat-2.js:561` for split-on-death) — root/uproot cycle: stands
  still growing for ~1s, then sprints at 1.7x for ~1s, repeating.
- `brambleknight` (`shielded`, read by `entities.js`, `ai-1.js`'s shielder targeting skip and
  `combat-3.js`'s shield/vuln timer) — creeps at 0.6x while the shield is up; the moment it drops
  and the player is inside 240 it commits to a 0.7s spinning bramble sweep, advancing at 1.6x while
  throwing paired bolts on a rotating axis.
- `owlsentinel` (`turret`, read by `combat-3.js` for the no-contact-damage and from-turret
  projectile flags and by `utils-1.js`) — stationary gaze cone: slowly sweeps `fr1Gaze`, snaps onto
  the player when the aim error is under 0.35 rad, and only then fires a 2-shot burst.

**The other 30 ids** were renamed to fresh `fr1*` behavior keys with a dedicated handler each:
`fr1Sporepopper` (hop-and-rest approach, detonation adds an 8-bolt spore ring to the blast),
`fr1Firefly` (sine-strafing flier that stops dead for a 3-shot burst), `fr1Thornhide` (chases, then
curls up `shielded` and uncurls into a 4-way shrapnel cross), `fr1Frogtongue` (two-part attack: a
sideways flanking hop, then a straight lunge, alternating flank side), `fr1Vineslinger` (3-bolt
sweeping volley whose fan direction flips each time), `fr1Thornbeast` (velocity-integrating chaser
with momentum and wall bounce — turns slowly, overshoots), `fr1Mosshide` (alternates fast-unarmoured
and slow-`shielded` phases), `fr1Willowisp` (figure-eight drift, periodically fades out `submerged`
and rematerialises 130 from the player), `fr1Stingswarm` (zig-zag rush, bursts into 6 fast stings
instead of an explosion), `fr1Boarrusher` (double charge with wall-bounce redirect between the two
dashes), `fr1Direfox` (pounce-and-retreat: leap in, immediate backwards leap out), `fr1Fernstalker`
(closes only while line of sight is broken, strafes and fires a tight 2-bolt pair when it has it),
`fr1Creepervine` (anchors in place for several seconds; each volley widens its 2-bolt fan on a
3-step cycle), `fr1Thicketweaver` (sine-weaving approach that fires *backwards*, laying bolts behind
it), `fr1Barkwatcher` (dormant and `shielded` until the player is close with line of sight, then a
3-shot volley before going dormant again), `fr1Glowmoth` (orbit radius shrinks continuously; at 46
it bursts a 7-bolt ring, resets to full radius and reverses direction), `fr1Rootburrower` (burrows,
tracks under the player at 1.8x, surfaces with an explosion plus a 6-bolt ring), `fr1Sporeseeder`
(retreats and lobs a seed that spawns a `sprout` at the landing point, not at the seeder),
`fr1Hive` (`shielded` while releasing bees in timed pairs), `fr1Waspine` (spawns a fan of wasps and
rushes in alongside them for 1.1s), `fr1Mossmender` (seeks the *most wounded* ally rather than
fleeing the player, wanders when nothing is hurt), `fr1Treelinesniper` (long telegraph that latches
the aim point, then relocates ~120 to a new floor tile after every shot), `fr1Gnatcloud` (drifting
cloud that periodically condenses into a straight 2.1x dash), `fr1Bramblelurker` (hidden and
`shielded` until triggered, then a 3-dash frenzy), `fr1Wispblinker` (blinks around the player in a
fixed triangle, firing a 3-bolt arc at each corner and re-randomising the triangle each lap),
`fr1Rootroller` (rolls in straight lines that accelerate over time and bounce off walls, re-aiming
at the player every few seconds), `fr1Staticwisp` (kites, then roots itself for a 0.75s visible
charge before a 5-bolt static fan), `fr1Venomskitter` (erratic skitter with random 90-degree turns
and short freezes), `fr1Brambleflail` (circles at whip range, then a 2.2x orbiting sweep spraying
bolts), `fr1Vinewhip` (yanks itself at the player at 2.6x and cracks a wide 3-bolt arc on arrival).

Not in this batch: bestiary `desc` fields, and the forest equivalent of Phase 36's texture pass —
the 30 renamed ids no longer match the `behavior`-keyed ornament branches in `Util._humanoidStatic`,
so they currently render as the plain shared body until an id-keyed forest mark table lands.

Audit: `feature-research/forest-enemy-rework/audit-batch1.md`.

### Phase 39 — Forest generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 2 (`ai-forest2.js`)

Batch 2 of the same pass, covering the remaining `stage:1` generic ids that live outside
`types-1.js`: ten in `js/data/enemies/types-2.js` and seven in `js/data/enemies/types-4.js`.
Before it, these 17 ids shared nine generic behaviors (`ranged`, `summoner`, `weaver` and
`splitter` were each used twice).

**New file `js/systems/ai-forest2.js`** — script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after
`ai-forest1.js`. It deliberately declares no wrapper and no helpers of its own: it reuses
`FOREST_ID_AI`, `forestStep`, `forestRing`, `forestArc`, `forestAim` and `forestSpawn` from
`ai-forest1.js` (both are plain global scripts, so those file-scope bindings are visible), and
adds keys to the existing `FOREST_ID_AI` object rather than re-wrapping `aiChase`/`aiTurret`.
Per-entity scratch state uses the `fr2*` field prefix.

**Three ids keep their original `behavior` string** (load-bearing elsewhere) and get their AI
through new `FOREST_ID_AI` entries:

- `thistlepod` (`turret`) — closed/bloomed cycle: sits `shielded` and silent for 1.8–2.8s, then
  opens for 2.2s of vulnerability, alternating an aimed arc and a slow 7-bolt ring every 0.55s.
- `burrbloater` (`splitter`) — creeps at 0.6x, then commits to a 0.85s roll at 2.3x along a fixed
  vector; hitting a wall ends the roll early with a 6-bolt burr burst. Sheds a 3-bolt ring on an
  independent 1.5s timer regardless of state.
- `heartseedling` (`splitter`) — heartbeat locomotion: paired 0.26s bursts at 2.1x separated by a
  0.14s gap, then a 0.7–1.1s rest at 0.35x; each thump drops one slow spore bolt behind it.

**The other 14 ids** were renamed to fresh `fr2*` behavior keys with a dedicated handler each:
`fr2Bramblewarden` (picks one unshielded ally as a ward, sets its `shielded` flag and orbits it as
an escort, dropping the ward if it dies or drifts; kites and fires a wide 5-bolt arc when it has
nobody to guard), `fr2Acornmortar` (predictive mortar: strafes to hold `lobRange` with the strafe
direction flipping each shot, plants a timed shell at a lead-predicted point that detonates as an
`Explosion` with its own proximity damage check), `fr2Bristleback` (fires a narrow 3-shot at range,
but if the player closes it flees backwards at 1.4x for 0.45s and dumps a wide quill spray on
exit), `fr2Hivestump` (open/closed cycle: `shielded` and silent while repositioning, then 2.2s of
spitting `stingswarm` every 0.75s with a pollen ring per spawn), `fr2Puffcap` (inflates through
three stages on a 1.1s beat — each stage grows its radius, raises its speed and pops a 4-bolt ring
— and detonates with blast radius and ring count scaled by the stage reached), `fr2Loamweaver`
(alternates a weaving surface phase with burrowed `submerged` travel at 1.9x, surfacing on a timer
or on proximity with a 6-bolt ring plus close-range damage), `fr2Oaksentry` (holds still while it
has line of sight, accumulating a lock; past 2.5s of lock its bolts get 1.3x speed and 0.55x
cooldown; slams with an `Explosion` and a 10-bolt ring if the player gets close, and chases at 0.9x
when line of sight breaks), `fr2Sporechanter` (three-verse chant, each verse ending in a wider,
larger arc; the third verse also heals nearby allies for 1 and triggers a long cooldown),
`fr2Mistlestag` (ricochet charge — on wall contact it turns 90 degrees, emits a 3-bolt ring and
re-dashes, up to two bounces per charge), `fr2Fungalchoir` (three-beat song: two escalating pulse
rings, then a summon beat that places `swarmerdnb` around itself; moves at 0.4x mid-song),
`fr2Dewdancer` (figure-eight approach combining a lateral sine with a radial cosine, breaking into
a 0.4s perpendicular spin at 1.7x that ends in a droplet ring), `fr2Crowsentinel` (perch-and-snipe:
picks a floor perch at 0.7x `fireRange` on a randomised bearing from the player, flies there,
telegraphs and fires, and relocates after two shots), `fr2Owlstalker` (three-mode stalk/swoop/
retreat: creeps at 0.55x, dashes *past* a lead-predicted point firing a tight pair at closest
approach, then withdraws), `fr2Graveswift` (darts between random floor waypoints 120–260 from the
player and fires bolt pairs perpendicular to its own travel — it never aims at the player).

**Deliberately untouched**: `dnbdragonfly` (`strafer`) and `dnbcicada` (`orbiter`) in
`js/data/enemies/flies.js`. Both behaviors are shared cross-stage (`strafer` is defined in
`ai-newshared.js` and used by stage 1/2/3 ids; `orbiter` by dozens of ids across every stage file),
so renaming them is out of scope here for the same reason `legacy-extra.js`'s stage-1 ids are.

Not in this batch: bestiary `desc` fields, and the forest texture pass — the 14 renamed ids no
longer match the `behavior`-keyed ornament branches in `js/core/utils-2.js`, same regression noted
in Phase 38.

Audit: `feature-research/forest-enemy-rework/audit-batch2.md`.

### Phase 40 — Forest enemy texture pass, batch 3 (`FOREST_ENEMY_MARKS` / `Util._forestMark`)

Restores and supersedes the ornament regression flagged in Phases 38–39. Because batches 1–2 gave
44 stage-1 ids unique `fr1*`/`fr2*` behavior strings, the `behavior`-keyed ornament branches in
`js/core/utils-2.js` (`Util._humanoidStatic` and the chain inside `drawBrownHumanoid`) no longer
matched them. This batch replaces `behavior`-keyed forest ornaments with an **id-keyed** table,
mirroring the Crypt system exactly.

**`FOREST_ENEMY_MARKS`** (module scope in `js/core/utils-2.js`, immediately after
`CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS`): 60 entries — one per non-minion stage-1 Forest enemy id (the 3 minions
`sprout`/`bumblebee`/`forestwasp` are excluded and keep their own inline art). Entry shape is
identical to `CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS`: `{ k, s, n, t, g, sd, sp, len, w }` where `k` = accent kind,
`s` = scale, `n` = element count, `t` = `Util.shadeColor` tint for the accent colour, `g` = glow
flag, `sd` = side/direction (±1), `sp` = pulse period in ms, `len` = length multiplier, `w` =
variant selector string.

**`Util._forestMark(ctx, e, flash, now, phase, col, dark, r, hx, hy, m)`**: sibling of
`Util._cryptMark` with the same preamble (`acc`/`deep`/`pul`/`lw`, `ctx.save()`…`ctx.restore()`,
optional `m.g` shadow glow) and an if/else-if `k === '...'` chain of **57 kinds**:
`sporeburst`, `lampglow`, `thorns`, `saplingleaf`, `tongue`, `vinecoil`, `tusks`, `mosspatch`,
`wispflame`, `swarmdots`, `thornshield`, `snort`, `owleyes`, `foxears`, `fernfrond`, `tendrils`,
`weave`, `barkrings`, `mothwings`, `dirtmound`, `seedpods`, `honeycomb`, `papernest`, `rootlash`,
`emberpair`, `pumpjack`, `healcross`, `scope`, `gnats`, `ambushbush`, `blinkring`, `rollball`,
`sparkarc`, `venomdrip`, `thornflail`, `whipvine`, `brambleward`, `acorn`, `bristles`, `thistle`,
`stumprings`, `mushcap`, `loamthreads`, `oakcrown`, `burrs`, `chantglyph`, `antlers`,
`fungalnotes`, `dewdrops`, `heartseed`, `crowbeak`, `plume2`, `wings2`, `cicadashell`,
`stalkerclaws`, `twinspike`, `canopyleaf`. Three kinds are shared by two ids each and
differentiated purely by fields: `whipvine` (`vinewhip` `sd:1` / `vinewhipper` `sd:-1`),
`vinecoil` (`vineslinger` / `mossambusher`), `wings2` (`graveswift` `w:'swift'` /
`dnbdragonfly` `w:'dragon'`).

**Call sites** (both inside `drawBrownHumanoid`, added directly beside the existing
`CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS` lookups, additive only): the turret early-return path (needed because
`owlsentinel` and `thistlepod` use `behavior:'turret'`) and the main post-behavior path. Marks are
drawn live after any baked sprite blit, so they animate for baked and unbaked enemies alike.

**Fold-in of the 5 ad hoc DNB accents**: the previous one-off id/behavior-keyed blocks for
`rootgrower`, `treeburner`, `oilrig`, `hive` and `waspine` (added by the DNB forest-enemy pass)
were deleted from `drawBrownHumanoid` and reimplemented as the `rootlash`, `emberpair`,
`pumpjack`, `honeycomb` and `papernest` kinds, preserving their runtime-state visuals
(`e.submerged` root retraction, `e.lobTimer` telegraph ring, `e.burnFlash` ember shockwave,
`e.summonTimer` entrance glow) — `e` is a `_forestMark` parameter, so no state was lost. There is
now a single accent system for Forest instead of two overlapping ones. The `bumblebee`/
`forestwasp` minion branch that preceded the old `hive` block is unchanged.

**Cross-stage safety**: `bramblestalker`, `vinewhipper`, `twinthorn`, `mossambusher`,
`canopysniper` (`legacy-extra.js`) and `dnbdragonfly`/`dnbcicada` (`flies.js`) share *behavior*
strings with other stages but their *ids* are globally unique and each carries exactly one
`stage`, so id-keyed accents cannot leak into other stages. All seven receive entries.

Not in this batch: bestiary `desc` fields. `CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS` (82 entries) and `Util._cryptMark`
(76 kinds) are untouched.

### Phase 41 — Forest floor: 10 new enemies (batch 4)

Mirrors Crypt batch 4 (Phase 37): 10 brand-new stage-1 Forest enemies with bespoke AI and bespoke
textures, not retrofits of the existing roster. New ids: `mudstomper`, `pollenshaman`,
`beetleclutch`, `stumplurker`, `battlebloom`, `thicketguard`, `duskstalker`, `gourdcannon`,
`briertrap`, `hedgehowl`.

**`js/data/enemies/forest-extra.js`** (new file, `Object.assign(ENEMY_TYPES, {...})`): 10 `stage:1`
definitions, `hp` 6–10, `dmg` 1–3, `speed` 0–104 (`gourdcannon` is immobile, `duskstalker` is the
fastest), `radius` 10–14, `xpTier` 1–2. Each carries a unique `behavior:'fr4...'` string and its own
tuning fields (e.g. `chargeSpeed`/`stompRadius` on `mudstomper`, `orbitRadius`/`nodeCount` on
`pollenshaman`, `buffRadius`/`buffMul` on `battlebloom`). No `onlyFloorNum`, matching the existing
Forest convention (unlike Crypt's `onlyFloorNum:0`). Loaded in `index.html` right after
`crypt-extra3.js` and before `cbranch2-enemies.js`, i.e. before `lists.js`, so all 10 ids flow into
`ENEMY_LIST = Object.values(ENEMY_TYPES)` automatically — no manual spawn-pool registration needed.

**`js/systems/ai-forest4.js`** (new file): 10 `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS.fr4*` handlers, each with a
distinct pattern, reusing `ai-forest1.js`'s shared locals (`forestStep`/`forestRing`/`forestArc`/
`forestAim`/`forestSpawn`) rather than redeclaring them:

- `fr4Mudstomper` — 4-state machine (chase → telegraph flicker → charge dash → stomp AoE damage
  check → recover), state stored on `e.fr4State`/`e.fr4Timer`/`e.fr4Dir`.
- `fr4Pollenshaman` — orbits the player at `orbitRadius`, drops timed "nodes" at its own position;
  once `nodeCount` nodes are placed it fires a 3-bolt arc from each node's position simultaneously
  (temporarily relocates `e.x`/`e.y` to each node to reuse `forestArc`'s aim-from-`e` shape).
- `fr4Beetleclutch` — approaches until `eruptRange`, then spawns `gruBcount` existing `sprout`
  minions in a ring via `forestSpawn` and switches to permanent flee.
- `fr4Stumplurker` — idle "lurk" state (no movement, no flash) until the player enters
  `ambushRange`, then bursts at `burstSpeed` for a short window before returning to lurk.
- `fr4Battlebloom` — kites away from the player; each tick scans `node.enemies` within
  `buffRadius` and multiplies ally `speed`/`dmg` by `buffMul`, restoring the ally's base stats
  (cached on `ally.fr4BaseSpeed`/`ally.fr4BaseDmg`) the moment it leaves the radius.
- `fr4Thicketguard` — territorial: engages with a 3-bolt arc every 1.4s while the player is within
  `territory` of its remembered home point, otherwise walks back home and idles.
- `fr4Duskstalker` — samples the player's position every 0.1s into a trail buffer, chases the
  buffer point that is `trailLag` seconds old (not the player directly), then lunges directly at
  the player once close.
- `fr4Gourdcannon` — immobile (`speed:0`); continuously sweeps a rotating single-bolt turret at
  `sweepRate` rad/s, firing every 0.5s via `forestRing`.
- `fr4Briertrap` — approaches to mid-range, telegraphs (flicker), then teleport-fires a
  `ringCount`-bolt ring centered on the player's position with one random gap left open for the
  player to escape through, then goes on a `ringCooldown` cooldown.
- `fr4Hedgehowl` — reactive: compares `e.hp` to the previous tick's cached `e.fr4LastHp`; any HP
  loss triggers a 6-bolt full ring burst plus a brief knockback-recoil retreat.

**`FOREST_ENEMY_MARKS`** (in `js/core/utils-2.js`) grows from 60 to **70** entries; `Util._forestMark`
grows from 57 to **67** `k === '...'` kind branches — all 10 new kinds are unique, no reuse:
`mudclod`, `pollencloud`, `beetlebacks`, `barknub`, `bloompetals`, `guardvines`, `duskwisp`,
`gourdcap`, `briercoil`, `quillburst`.

Not in this batch: bestiary `desc` fields, matching the Crypt batch 4 precedent. See
`feature-research/forest-enemy-rework/audit-batch4.md` for the full roster table and verification
log.

Audit: `feature-research/forest-enemy-rework/audit-batch3.md`.

## Wave Defense mode — `js/systems/wavedefense.js`

An endless arena mode selected from the main menu's "🌊 Wave Defense" button. The
button rebuilds the existing class-select grid with `startWaveDefenseWithClass`
(`js/main.js`) as its pick handler; that helper does the normal
`new Game(canvas)` + `game.startRun(classId, readSeedInput())` and then calls
`startWaveDefense(game)`, which throws away the normal floor-0 dungeon and
installs a single-room arena instead.

### Game fields

- `game.mode` — `'story'` (set in `startRun`) or `'wavedefense'`. Every mode
  guard in the codebase tests this string.
- `game.waveDefenseMode` — boolean twin of the above, read by
  `currentPalette()` in `js/ui/render.js`.
- `game.wdWave` — current wave number, 1-based once the first wave starts.
- `game.wdStageIndex` — 0–3, which of the four arena themes / branch letters is
  active. Advances every 25 waves.
- `game.wdLoop` — how many full A→D cycles have completed; drives stat scaling.
- `game.wdDifficultyMult` — extra multiplier bumped +0.25 per loop.
- `game.wdBossPoolCursor` — round-robin index into the current boss pool, so
  boss waves cycle rather than repeat randomly.
- `game.wdSpawnTimer` — countdown to the next trickle spawn.
- `game.wdQuotaRemaining` — enemies left to dispatch this wave.
- `game.wdBossActive` — true while a boss wave is in progress (trash paused).
- `game.wdStarted` — false until the player first presses the arena control
  button; the arena spawns idle and no waves run until it flips true.
- `game.wdPaused` — true while wave pacing is halted (manual pause or the free
  automatic pause every `WD_AUTO_PAUSE_INTERVAL` waves).
- `game.wdInterWaveTimer` — counts down from `WD_INTERWAVE_BREAK` (15s) after a
  non-milestone wave completes; `updateWaveDefense` holds off `wdStartWave`
  until it reaches zero, but starts the next wave immediately (skipping the
  rest of the breather) once every enemy in the arena is already dead. Zero
  (no breather running) the rest of the time, including on milestone waves,
  which skip the timer entirely and go straight to the `wdPaused` hard pause
  instead.
- `game.wdPaletteIndex` — index into `STAGES` used by `currentPalette()` for
  the wave-defense arena's color palette; incremented by `wdCyclePalette` on
  every boss wave (every `WD_BOSS_WAVE_INTERVAL`, 10, waves), independent of
  `wdStageIndex`/arena regeneration.
- `game.wdNickelsUnlocked`, `game.wdDimesUnlocked` — set true by the wd-shop's
  upgrade station (tiers 1 and 3); while false, `spawnClearRoomPickup`'s
  wavedefense penny-pool roll filters `nickel`/`dime` out.
- `game.wdPoolBranch`, `game.wdEnemyPoolCache`, `game.wdBossPoolCache` — the
  branch letter and the enemy/boss pools computed for the current stage segment
  by `wdRefreshPools`.
- `game.runStats.waveDefenseBossKills` — per-run boss kill counter (added to the
  `runStats` object in `game.startRun`).

### Functions

- `startWaveDefense(game)` — initializes all `wd*` fields (`wdStarted:false`,
  `wdPaused:false`), builds arena 0, sets `game.dungeon`, calls
  `game.enterRoom(arena.start, null)`. It does **not** start wave 1 — the first
  control-button press does.
- `updateWaveDefense(game, dt)` — called from `loop()` in `js/main.js` right
  after `game.update(input, dt)`, only when `game.mode === 'wavedefense'`.
  While `wdBossActive` it watches for the boss's death (bumping
  `waveDefenseBossKills` and firing the boss-kill achievements) and then
  completes the wave; otherwise, while `game.wdInterWaveTimer > 0`, it counts
  the timer down and calls `wdStartWave(game)` once it reaches zero, holding
  off all spawn/quota logic for that 3s breather; otherwise it time-gates
  trickle spawns (`WD_SPAWN_INTERVAL` 0.55s) against a simultaneous-alive cap
  (`WD_MAX_ALIVE` 20) until `wdQuotaRemaining` hits zero. It early-returns when
  `game.currentRoom.type !== 'wavearena'` (the player is in the attached wd
  shop), when `!game.wdStarted`, or when `game.wdPaused` — combat, rendering and
  movement are untouched by a pause, only spawn/completion pacing stops.
- `generateWaveArena(game, stageIndex)` — picks a template from
  `wdWaveArenaPool(stageIndex)` (that branch's 5-template pool) via
  `stageIndex % pool.length`, calls
  `makeRoomInstance('wavearena', 0, 0, mask, tmpl)`, marks the node
  discovered/cleared/doorsOpen via `wdMarkRoomOpen`, attaches the wave shop
  (`wdAttachWaveShop`), recomputes `bounds` (`wdComputeBounds`), places the
  control button (`wdSetupControlButton`), refreshes the branch pools
  (`wdRefreshPools`), and returns a dungeon-shaped object
  `{ rooms, start, bossNode:null, treasureNode:null, bounds, floorNum }` where
  `floorNum` is synthetic (`wdSyntheticFloor`).

- `wdWaveArenaPool(stageIndex)` — resolves `wdBranchLetter(stageIndex)` and
  returns that theme's 5-template array off `ROOM_TEMPLATES.wavearena` (an
  `{A,B,C,D}` object, each a 5-entry array), falling back to `.A` or `[]` if
  the theme is missing. Shared by `generateWaveArena` and
  `wdRegenerateObstacles` so both index into the same branch-appropriate pool.

### Branch-scoped enemy/boss pooling

- `wdDefBranchLetter(def)` — the branch letter carried as the trailing character
  of `def.floorKey`, or `null` when the def has no lettered `floorKey`.
- `wdDefInBranch(def, letter)` — true when a def belongs to that branch: its own
  `floorKey` letter wins; `stage === 'universal'` matches every branch;
  everything else (numeric `stage`, unlettered `floorKey` like `'13'`) is
  main-route only, i.e. branches A and B.
- `wdDefEligible(def)` — mirrors `resolveGenericEnemy`'s filter set:
  `(!def.locked || isEnemyUnlocked(def.id)) && !def.neverRandom &&
  def.onlyFloorNum === undefined`.
- `wdEnemyPoolForBranch(letter)` / `wdBossPoolForBranch(letter)` — filter the
  full `ENEMY_LIST` / `BOSS_LIST` (enemies additionally `!isMinion`) down to
  eligible defs in that branch, pooling across every floor of the branch. There
  is no cross-branch fallback: an empty result falls back only to the
  `stage:'universal'` defs, which belong to every branch. Signature/branch
  filtering only — no floor/tier gating here, see `wdGateEnemyPoolByFloor`.
- `wdRefreshPools(game)` — resolves the branch via `wdBranchLetter(game.wdStageIndex)`
  and caches `game.wdPoolBranch` / `wdEnemyPoolCache` / `wdBossPoolCache`. Called
  once per stage segment from `generateWaveArena` (initial build and every
  `wdAdvanceStage` swap); `wdSpawnTrash` / `wdSpawnBoss` draw from the caches
  instead of resolving per spawn, `wdSpawnBoss` still round-robining through
  `game.wdBossPoolCursor`.
- `wdFloorKeyDepth(def)` — leading numeric prefix of `def.floorKey` (e.g.
  `'21C'` → `21`), or `null` when `def.floorKey` isn't a string.
- `wdDefDepth(def)` — a def's difficulty depth for gating: `wdFloorKeyDepth(def)`
  if it resolves, else `def.stage` when it's a number, else `null` (falls
  through to `wdGateEnemyPoolByFloor`'s `xpTier` fallback). Added because
  `xpTier` is an XP-reward tier, not a difficulty tier, and several late-game
  defs with no `floorKey` (e.g. `mrloop` `stage:12`, `hsdrone` `stage:13` in
  `stage10-13-enemies.js`) carry a misleadingly low `xpTier` — using `stage`
  first keeps them correctly gated to late waves.
- `wdGateEnemyPoolByFloor(pool, floorNum)` — trash-only difficulty gate applied
  on top of `game.wdEnemyPoolCache`, from `wdPickWaveEnemyTypes` (given
  `wdSyntheticFloor(game)`, called once per wave start, not per spawn — see
  `wdPickWaveEnemyTypes` below), so an early-wave low synthetic floor can't
  roll a deep-branch/high-tier enemy. Keeps entries with a `wdDefDepth` only if
  `depth <= floorNum + 2`; keeps entries with no resolvable depth only if
  `(e.xpTier || 1) <= tierCap`, where `tierCap` is 1 at `floorNum <= 5` else 2.
  Falls back to the ungated `pool` unchanged if gating would empty it, so the
  spawn pool is never starved. `wdEnemyPoolForBranch`'s own signature and
  `wdRefreshPools`'s branch cache are untouched by this — the gate is a
  separate filter recomputed fresh, not baked into the cached pool. Boss pool
  selection (`wdBossPoolForBranch`) is unaffected — bosses can't appear before
  wave 10 regardless.
- `wdPickWaveEnemyTypes(game)` — picks the trash-enemy roster for one wave:
  runs `wdGateEnemyPoolByFloor(game.wdEnemyPoolCache, wdSyntheticFloor(game))`
  (refreshing `wdEnemyPoolCache` first if empty) then returns up to 2 defs —
  the whole gated pool if it has ≤2 entries, else 2 random defs via
  `Util.shuffle(pool.slice()).slice(0, 2)`. Called once per non-boss wave from
  `wdStartWave`, result cached on `game.wdWaveEnemyTypes`; boss waves set it to
  `[]` instead, moot since `updateWaveDefense` never reaches `wdSpawnTrash`
  while `game.wdBossActive` is true. This caps each wave's trash variety at 2
  enemy types, deliberately narrower than the branch/depth-gated pool it draws
  from.

### Control button, attached shop

- `node.wdControlButton = {x, y}` — tile coords of the arena's start/pause
  button, placed at the room centre by `wdSetupControlButton(game, dungeon, arena)`
  (after `ensureRoomBuilt` + `populateRoom`, since `findClearFloorSpot` needs
  `node.obstacles`).
- `wdControlButtonState(game)` — `'running'` when started and not paused, else
  `'idle'`.
- `wdTryControlButton(game)` — explicit-keypress interaction in the
  `donationMachine`/`rerollAltar` convention, wired from `Game.tryArcadeInteract`
  (`js/game.js`) ahead of the arcade handler and therefore bound to the existing
  `[H]` arcade key. Within `WD_CONTROL_BUTTON_RANGE` (30px of `x*TILE, y*TILE`):
  first press starts the run (`wdStartWave`), a press while paused resumes
  free — and, if the pause landed between waves (`wdQuotaRemaining<=0`, no
  boss active, no interwave timer running — i.e. an auto-pause from
  `wdCompleteWave`'s `WD_AUTO_PAUSE_INTERVAL`), also calls `wdStartWave`
  itself so the next wave actually begins (resuming mid-wave or mid-interwave-
  countdown does not call it, since `updateWaveDefense` already drives those) —
  a press while running pauses and costs `WD_PAUSE_HEART_COST` (1) heart via
  `player.spendHearts` — which may legitimately kill the player.
- `drawWdControlButton()` (`js/ui/render.js`, mixed into `Game.prototype`) —
  draws the rounded button plus a play or pause glyph and an `[H]` label,
  guarded on `this.mode === 'wavedefense' && node.wdControlButton`.
- `wdMarkRoomOpen(room)` — sets discovered/seen/revealed/visited/cleared/doorsOpen.
- `wdComputeBounds(rooms)` — block-cell min/max over all rooms, for `dungeon.bounds`.
- `wdAttachWaveShop(game, dungeon, arena)` — builds a real `type:'shop'` room via
  `pickMaskForType('shop', …)` + `tryPlaceAdjacent` against a scratch
  `blockGrid` seeded with the arena, flags it `room.wdShop = true`, opens it,
  and populates it through the normal `ensureRoomBuilt`/`populateRoom` path so
  it gets `donationMachine` and `rerollAltar` like any shop. Then calls
  `wdBuildShopSlots(shop, dungeon.floorNum)` to lay out the fixed 8-slot wd
  shop (overwriting whatever `populateRoom` rolled into `shopSlots`), and adds
  a fourth corner fixture, `shop.upgradeStation = {x, y, tier: 0}`, found via
  `findNearestFloor(shop, tileW*0.82, tileH*0.18)`. Added to `dungeon.rooms`,
  so normal door traversal / `enterRoom` works.
- `WD_SHOP_CATEGORY_ORDER` — fixed 8-slot category layout for wd shops:
  `['heartRed', 'heartBlue', 'pickupOther', 'pillstar', 'item', 'item',
  'trinket', 'familiar']`. `WD_SHOP_PICKUP_OTHER_KINDS` — pool for the
  `pickupOther` slot (`bomb`/`key`/`sack`/`battery`/`trashbag`/`pearl`/
  `driftnet`/`tideflask`).
- `wdShopSlotPosition(shop, i)` — tile position for wd shop slot `i`:
  `frac = (i+1)/9`, `x = round(1 + frac*(tileW-2))`, `y = floor(tileH/2)`,
  evenly spacing all 8 slots along the shop's horizontal midline.
- `wdPushShopCategorySlot(shop, category, x, y, floorNum, pickupKind)` —
  builds and pushes one wd shop slot for `category` onto `shop.shopSlots`:
  `heartRed`/`heartBlue` forward to `addShopSlot(shop, {kind:'forced',
  specific: category}, …)`; `pickupOther` rolls (or reuses `pickupKind`) from
  `WD_SHOP_PICKUP_OTHER_KINDS`; `pillstar` rolls (or reuses `pickupKind`)
  from `['pill','star']` — both of these also stamp `wdPickupKind` on the
  pushed slot so a restock can redraw the same category; `item`/`trinket`/
  `familiar` roll via `pickItemFromPool('shop')`/`pickTrinketFromPool()`/
  `pickFamiliarFromPool()` and push the slot object directly (mirroring
  `addShopSlot`'s shape). Every pushed slot is stamped `wdCategory = category`
  so a later restock knows what to redraw.
- `wdBuildShopSlots(shop, floorNum)` — resets `shop.shopSlots = []`, stores
  `shop.shopFloorNum = floorNum`, and calls `wdPushShopCategorySlot` once per
  entry of `WD_SHOP_CATEGORY_ORDER` at its `wdShopSlotPosition`. Always
  produces exactly 8 slots in that fixed order.
- `wdRestockShopSlot(node, slot)` — rerolls a single emptied wd shop slot in
  place: re-derives `slot`'s array index, calls `wdPushShopCategorySlot(node,
  slot.wdCategory, slot.x, slot.y, node.shopFloorNum)` to build a fresh slot
  of the same category (redrawing `pickupOther`/`pillstar` from their pools
  rather than reusing the old specific kind), resets the new slot's
  `playerWasNear = false`, and swaps it into the original array index so slot
  order/position is preserved. Called from `updateShop` (`js/systems/items-2.js`)
  the moment the player walks away from a bought slot they emptied — not on
  room exit — so each pedestal restocks independently. Normal story shops are
  untouched — every path is gated on the `wdShop` flag.

Internal helpers: `wdBranchLetter(stageIndex)` (0→'A', 1→'B', 2→'C', 3→'D'),
`wdSyntheticFloor(game)` (`min(13, 2 + floor(wave/3) + loop*4)` — the value fed
to `Enemy`/`Boss` constructors so all existing floor-driven scaling applies),
`wdWaveQuota(wave)` (`min(40, 4 + floor(wave*1.5))`), `wdLoopMult`,
`wdApplyLoopScale` (post-construct hp/maxHp/dmg/speed multiply),
`wdPickSpawnSpot` (14 tries of `findClearFloorSpot` preferring spots >200px from
the player), `wdSpawnTrash`, `wdSpawnBoss`, `wdAdvanceStage`,
`wdGrantWaveRewards`, `wdCompleteWave`, `wdStartWave`, `wdCyclePalette(game)`
(increments `game.wdPaletteIndex`, called from `wdStartWave`'s boss-wave
branch so the arena palette changes every `WD_BOSS_WAVE_INTERVAL` waves; also
resolves `STAGES[wdPaletteIndex % STAGES.length].id` through
`STAGE_MUSIC_TRACKS` and calls `Sound.startMusic(trackId)` to swap the track
to match the new palette, then calls `wdRegenerateObstacles(game)`),
`wdRegenerateObstacles(game)` (no-ops unless `game.currentRoom.type ===
'wavearena'`; clears `node.obstacles` and repopulates it from
`wdWaveArenaPool(game.wdStageIndex)[wdPaletteIndex % pool.length]`'s `s` list
— same branch-themed pool `generateWaveArena` used to build the room, so
palette cycling stays within that branch's 5 layouts — re-running each raw
spawner through `expandLineSpawner`/`decodeSpawner`/`rollRockKind`
and pushing `new Obstacle(kind, x, y)` — leaves the room mask, shop, control
button, player position, and any live enemies/boss untouched, so it's safe to
call mid-fight).

Branch letter routing into `resolveGenericEnemy(floorNum, branch, floorPath)`:
'A'/'B' pass as `branch`, 'C'/'D' pass as `floorPath`, matching
`floorKeyFor`'s convention.

### Pacing constants

`WD_MAX_ALIVE` 20, `WD_SPAWN_INTERVAL` 0.55, `WD_STAGE_SWAP_INTERVAL` 25,
`WD_BOSS_WAVE_INTERVAL` 10, `WD_ITEM_WAVE_INTERVAL` 10,
`WD_AUTO_PAUSE_INTERVAL` 5, `WD_COIN_DROP_MIN` 2, `WD_COIN_DROP_MAX` 3,
`WD_CONTROL_BUTTON_RANGE` 30, `WD_PAUSE_HEART_COST` 1, `WD_INTERWAVE_BREAK` 15.
Every 10th wave is boss-only and also grants
`applyItemToPlayer(game, pickItemFromPool('treasure'))`;
**every** wave drops `Util.randi(2,3)` coins via
`spawnResolvedPickup(node, 'coin', …)` around the arena's clear centre spot; every
5th completed wave sets `game.wdPaused = true` for free, so the player must walk
back to the button to resume; every other completed wave instead gets a free,
non-interactive `WD_INTERWAVE_BREAK` (15s) breather via `game.wdInterWaveTimer`
before the next wave auto-starts, cut short immediately once every enemy in
the arena is already dead. On stage swap the
arena is regenerated and `enterRoom` re-centers the player, discarding leftover
trash; a D→A wrap increments `wdLoop` and `wdDifficultyMult`.

### `wavearena` room type — `js/data/roomTemplates/wavearena.js`

`ROOM_TEMPLATES.wavearena` is keyed by `WD_STAGE_BRANCHES` letter (`{A, B, C,
D}`), each holding 5 layout variants (20 templates total) sharing
`WAVE_ARENA_MASK`, a 4x4 all-ones block mask → a 42x42-tile (1344px) arena,
larger than any `ROOM_SHAPES` entry. `wdWaveArenaPool(stageIndex)`
(`js/systems/wavedefense.js`) resolves which theme array a given stage draws
from, and both `generateWaveArena` (initial room build) and
`wdRegenerateObstacles` (boss-wave palette cycle) index into that same
5-entry pool, so a stage only ever cycles through its own theme's layouts.
Each variant's `s` list is obstacle-only (`"o"` entries), using plain
4-element spawner entries and 6-element line-shorthand entries
(`[x1,y1,"o",kind,x2,y2]`) for hazard rows, drawn from a palette themed to its
branch: **A** (crypt/desert) — `rock`, `tallrock`, `hardrock`, `pit`,
`cactus`; **B** (swamp) — `mud`, `bluefire`, `spiketrap`, `thornbush`,
`stunspore`; **C** (water) — `currente`/`currentw`/`currentn`/`currents`,
`quicksand`, `hardrock`, `pit`, `rock`; **D** (inferno) — `blackfire`,
`spikedrock`, `tallhardrock`, `thornbush`, `spiketrap`. `'wavearena'` is added
to `ROOM_LABELS`
(`js/game.js`, "Wave Arena") and to `AUTO_OPEN_ROOM_TYPES` (`js/systems/dungeon.js`);
it is deliberately **not** in `SPECIAL_ROOM_TYPES`. Unconnected door slots stay
`type:null`, so `buildRoomTiles` carves no door holes and the arena is sealed.

### Mode guards in existing files

- `js/game.js` — `startRun` sets `this.mode = 'story'` and seeds
  `waveDefenseBossKills: 0`; the `update` tail guards `this.checkStairs()` with
  `if (this.mode !== 'wavedefense')`; `onBossDefeated()` skips its
  `node.stairsSpot` assignment entirely when `this.mode === 'wavedefense'` (no
  "next floor" to descend to in wave defense — see `wdCyclePalette` above for
  the replacement palette/music/obstacle-cycle behavior on boss kill).
- `js/systems/combat-3.js` — `checkRoomCleared` early-returns `false` in wave
  defense, so the challenge/bosschallenge/room-clear reward chain never fires.
- `js/ui/render.js` — `currentPalette()` early-returns
  `STAGES[(this.wdPaletteIndex||0) % STAGES.length].palette`.
- `js/main.js` — `buildRunSummary` and `showGameOver` branch on
  `game.mode === 'wavedefense'` to report "Survived to Wave N" and the boss-kill
  count. There is no win condition, so `showWin` is never reached.

### Achievements — `js/achievements/defs-wavedefense.js`

Loaded after `defs-mastery.js`. Four `statKey:'bestWaveReached'` /
`threshold` milestones (`wd_wave10/25/50/100`, category `Challenge`) plus two
per-run boss-kill achievements (`wd_bosses5`, `wd_bosses15`). Because
`setStatMax` does not fire statKey watchers, `wdCompleteWave` calls
`unlockAchievement` directly for any milestone already reached (the call is
idempotent), mirroring the speedrun-threshold pattern in `js/main.js`.
`statDefaults` in `achievements/logic.js` gains `bestWaveReached:0` so the
achievement panel can show progress before the first Wave Defense run.

Audit: `feature-research/wavedefense/audit.md`.

### Turret/wisp tear-fidelity + status-chance exclusivity fix — `items-1.js`, `entities.js`, `combat-1.js`, `combat-3.js`

- **Status-chance exclusivity removed** (`items-1.js`'s `recalcPlayerStats`) — the
  `STATUS_EXCLUSIVITY_FIELDS` loop that used to force-zero every status-chance field
  except the single numerically-highest one (`freezeChance`/`stunChance`/
  `vulnerableChance`/`charmChance`/`fearChance`/`venomChance`) is gone; all of a
  player's status chances can now be simultaneously nonzero. This was the root cause
  of some characters' secondary status chances (e.g. Crystal Pony's charm chance)
  never being able to proc at all whenever a different status field outranked it.
  `winningStatus`/`player.primedStatus`/`player.tearColor` computation is unchanged —
  the player's own ranged/charged tears still pick and visually commit to exactly one
  status per shot via `rollTearStatus`, and melee/turret/wisp hits (which call
  `applyOnHitStatuses` without a `tearStatus` arg) now correctly roll ALL of a
  player's status chances independently instead of only ever having one nonzero
  field to roll against.
- **`player.turretDamageMult`** (`entities.js`) default lowered from 0.7 to 0.5 per
  "turrets at 50% the players damage" — per-class skill-tree `uniqueField` bonuses on
  top of this base (engineerpony/dnbpony/crystalpony/alicorn/ponybot) are additive and
  untouched.
- **`combat-1.js`'s `updatePlayerTurrets`** now calls `resolveTearMods(player)` and
  builds its `Projectile` the same way `playerRangedAttack` does — real tear color/
  shape/size/radius and all `player.tearFlags` (pierce/homing/spectral/explosive/
  chainLightning/splitOnHit/knockbackPulse/pullPulse/creepOnHit) instead of a fixed
  `{color:'#7fc1e3', radius:4}` — plus a new `statusScale: TURRET_STATUS_SCALE` (0.5)
  option so turret hits "follow the effect chances". `mods.shapeDef.onSpawn` is
  invoked same as the player's own tears. `turret.dmg` itself is still computed once
  at build time (`player.rangedDamage * player.turretDamageMult`, unchanged quirk) —
  `mods.damageMult` is intentionally NOT applied a second time on top of it, to keep
  turret damage at exactly the stated 50%.
- **`combat-3.js`'s projectile-hit resolution** — the `isPlayerBolt` branch now checks
  `pr.statusScale` before falling back to the deterministic `pr.appliedStatus` path:
  `if (pr.statusScale) applyOnHitStatuses(game, e, pr.statusScale); else
  applyOnHitStatuses(game, e, undefined, pr.appliedStatus);`. The player's own tears
  never set `statusScale` so their one-status-per-shot behavior is unchanged; turret
  bolts (owner `'player'`, now carrying `statusScale`) take the independent multi-roll
  branch while keeping `owner:'player'`'s side effects (`onHitLanded`, `rangedKills`,
  the `'turret'` hit-layer trigger via `attackTrigger`).
- **Wisps** (`familiars.js`) needed no change — already fire the player's real tear
  (`resolveTearMods(player, true)`, forced round shape) at `player.wispDamageRatio`
  (default 0.25) and already pass `statusScale: WISP_STATUS_SCALE` (0.2) into both
  their melee contact hit and their ranged wisp-shot hit, so they now correctly
  "follow the effect chances" too now that the exclusivity zeroing is gone.

### `rollTearStatus` multi-status redesign — `items-1.js`, `combat-1.js`, `combat-2.js`, `entities.js`

Supersedes the "player's own tears still pick and visually commit to exactly one
status per shot" behavior described in the two sections above — that was itself
still a bug: even after status-chance exclusivity was removed from
`recalcPlayerStats`, the player's own ranged tears still only ever rolled
`player.primedStatus` (the single highest-chance field) via the old
`rollTearStatus`, so a character with multiple simultaneously-nonzero status
chances (e.g. Crystal Pony with charm alongside another status) still never saw
the non-primed ones apply from their own direct attacks, even though melee/
turret/wisp hits (independent multi-roll `applyOnHitStatuses`) were already
correct.

- **`rollTearStatus(player)`** (`items-1.js`) now rolls every field in
  `STATUS_EXCLUSIVITY_FIELDS` (now a module-level const, hoisted out of
  `recalcPlayerStats` so both it and `rollTearStatus` share one declaration)
  independently — `RNG.random() < player[field]` per field — and returns an
  **array** of every field name that hit (possibly empty), instead of a single
  field name or `null`. `player.primedStatus`/`player.tearColor` are unaffected
  (still computed the same way, still used for non-per-tear purposes).
- **`combat-1.js`'s `playerRangedAttack`** and **`combat-2.js`'s volley/shard
  spawn** both rename their local to `appliedStatuses` (the array) and derive a
  `primaryStatus` for display purposes only —
  `appliedStatuses.includes(player.primedStatus) ? player.primedStatus :
  (appliedStatuses[0] || null)` — used for the tear's `color`/`statusColor`
  Projectile options (so the ring/tint shows the primed status when it's one of
  the ones that hit, otherwise whichever other status hit, otherwise no ring).
  The full `appliedStatuses` array is passed through as the Projectile's
  `appliedStatus` option so every rolled status still gets applied on hit, not
  just the displayed one.
- **`Projectile.appliedStatus`** (`entities.js`) default changed from `null` to
  `[]` (an empty array is the correct "no status" sentinel now; the old `|| null`
  fallback would never have triggered for `[]` since empty arrays are truthy in
  JS, but the field itself is now always an array so the default must match).
- **`applyOnHitStatuses(game, enemy, scale, tearStatus)`** (`combat-2.js`) — the
  deterministic `tearStatus !== undefined` branch now normalizes
  `tearStatus`/array (`Array.isArray(tearStatus) ? tearStatus : [tearStatus]`)
  and loops the same `if/else if` field-matching over every entry, applying
  every status that was rolled for that tear rather than at most one.
  `combat-3.js`'s call site (`applyOnHitStatuses(game, e, undefined,
  pr.appliedStatus)`) needed no change — it already just forwards whatever
  `pr.appliedStatus` holds.

#### DNB Desert set (2026) — 9 new `stage:2` enemies + `quicksand` Creep kind + the `DustDevil` roaming-hazard system

**`js/data/enemies/desert-extra.js`** (new file, `Object.assign(ENEMY_TYPES, {...})`): 9 `stage:2`
enemies (`duneburrower`, `sandwraith`, `scarabswarm`, `cactusguard`, `mirageduplicate`,
`sandviper`, `quicksandbloom`, `dunecrawler`, `sirocco`) — same template as the Forest/Crypt
extra-enemy files. `sirocco` sets `isElite:true`. Each declares its own `behavior:` id, dispatched
through `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS`.

**New file `js/systems/ai-desert1.js`** — script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after
`ai-forest4.js`. Follows the exact Forest-batch idiom: file-scope wrapper helpers
(`desertStep`/`desertAim`/`desertRing`/`desertArc`/`desertSpawn`) built on the same primitives
(`tryMoveEntity`, `fireProjectileAngle`, `findNearestFloor`, `Util.rand`/`Util.dist`, `RNG.random`,
`aiWander`), then 9 handlers registered on `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS`:

- **`ds1Duneburrower`** — burrows underground (invisible-in-fiction via `e.burrowed`) until a
  timer expires or the player gets within 40px, then after `fuseTime` erupts at the player's
  position, deals a blast (manual `Util.dist` check within `blastRadius` → `damagePlayer`) and
  pushes `game.explosions.push(new Explosion(e.x, e.y, e.blastRadius))` for the visual, matching
  the universal `Explosion` calling convention (`constructor(x, y, radius)` only, always pushed
  into `game.explosions`).
- **`ds2Sandwraith`** — teleports near the player on a cooldown, fires one bolt on arrival, keeps
  its distance (backpedals under 140px) or wanders otherwise.
- **`ds3Scarabswarm`** — chases directly, periodically fires a full `desertRing` burst
  (`ringCount` bolts) at a random offset angle.
- **`cactusguard`** (`ds4Cactusguard`) — stationary; continuously rotates an aim angle
  (`sweepAng`) and periodically fires a `desertRing` volley of spines along it.
- **`ds5Mirageduplicate`** — a decaying illusion: counts down `decayLeft` from `decayTime` and
  calls `handleEnemyDeath(game, e)` (matching its real 2-arg signature) when it expires; while
  alive, chases and fires single bolts on a timer.
- **`ds6Sandviper`** — cooldown-gated lunge: dashes at `lungeSpeed` toward the player for a fixed
  `dashTimer` window when in range, otherwise approaches slowly.
- **`ds7Quicksandbloom`** — stationary; on a cooldown, drops
  `game.creep.push(new Creep(e.x, e.y, e.patchRadius, e.patchLife, 'quicksand', 'enemy'))` — the
  first live spawn site of the new `'quicksand'` Creep kind (see below).
- **`ds8Dunecrawler`** — cooldown-gated charge (like `sandviper` but slower/heavier), otherwise
  slow approach.
- **`ds9Sirocco`** (elite) — wanders while periodically spawning a roaming
  `game.dustDevils.push(new DustDevil(spot.x, spot.y, e.devilRadius, e.devilLife, 'enemy'))` near
  itself — the first live spawn site of the new `DustDevil` system (see below).

**The `quicksand` Creep kind** — a straight extension of the existing `Creep` ground-hazard
system (`js/entities/entities.js`, `class Creep { constructor(x, y, radius, life, kind, source) }`,
see the DNB Forest set entry above for the base system). No new class or update loop: `updateCreep`
already treats any kind generically. Two integration points:
- **`combat-1.js`'s `onTar` check** (player-slow/status trigger) now matches
  `c.kind === 'tar' || c.kind === 'quicksand'` so standing in a quicksand patch slows the player
  exactly like tar.
- **`CREEP_PALETTE`** (`js/ui/render.js`, `drawCreep()`) gained a `quicksand: { base:'#c2a05a',
  hi:'#e8cf8e' }` entry for a sandy-tan render distinct from tar/venom.

**The `DustDevil` system** (new, `js/entities/entities.js` next to `Creep`) — a roaming wind
hazard, distinct from `Creep` (which is stationary): it wanders under its own steering rather than
sitting still.
- `class DustDevil { constructor(x, y, radius, life, source) }` → `x`,`y`,`radius`,`life`,`maxLife`,
  `source` (`'enemy'` default), plus self-owned wander state: `ang` (random initial heading),
  `turnRate` (random ±0.6–1.5 rad/s), `speed` (34–60px/s), `pullRadius` (`radius + 90`),
  `tickTimer`, `seed` (render-only jitter).
- **`updateDustDevils(game, dt)`** (`js/systems/combat-4.js`, alongside `updateCreep`) — each tick,
  ages `life`, turns by `turnRate`, steps forward via `findNearestFloor`-validated movement
  (reverses on a blocked step). When `source === 'enemy'` and the player is within `pullRadius`, it
  pulls the player toward itself (strength scales with proximity) and, once the player is inside
  `radius`, ticks 1 damage per second via `damagePlayer(..., 'dustdevil')`.
- **`Renderer.drawDustDevils()`** (`js/ui/render.js`) — drawn once per frame from the world-space
  draw pass, alongside `drawCreep`/`drawExplosions`.
- **`game.dustDevils`** array — initialized alongside `creep`/`explosions` in both `Game`
  constructor sites in `js/game.js`, updated via `updateDustDevils(this, dt)` in the main loop.

#### Desert generic-enemy unique-AI rework (2026) — `ai-desert2.js`/`ai-desert3.js`/`ai-desert4.js`

Same rework pattern as the Crypt (`ai-crypt3/4/5.js`) and Forest (`ai-forest1/2/4.js`) batches
above, applied to every remaining legacy `stage:2` (desert) enemy that still used a generic shared
`behavior:` name (`chaser`/`charger`/`strafer`/`pouncer`/`splitshot`/`swarm`/`flyer`/etc). Combined
with the pre-existing `ai-desert1.js` (`ds1`–`ds9`, the `desert-extra.js` set), every legacy desert
enemy across every data file now has its own bespoke handler. All three files are plain global
scripts, script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after `ai-desert1.js` (before `ai-mirrorboss.js`)
so their handlers can freely call `ai-desert1.js`'s file-scope helpers (`desertStep`, `desertAim`,
`desertRing`, `desertArc`, `desertSpawn`) alongside the universal combat primitives (`seekVector`,
`fireProjectileAt`, `fireProjectileAngle`, `handleEnemyDeath`, `playerDamageAmount`, `damagePlayer`,
`findNearestFloor`, `tryMoveEntity`, `aiWander`). No new shared helpers were added — each file
composes over `ai-desert1.js`'s locals rather than redeclaring its own.

- **`js/systems/ai-desert2.js`** — 31 handlers (`ds10Duneskitter` through `ds40Scarabswarm`),
  covering every `stage:2` enemy in `js/data/enemies/types-1.js`. Notable ones: `ds25Sandmortar`
  lobs an arcing projectile by writing to a new `game.pendingLobs` array (checked elsewhere in the
  lob-resolution pass, same pattern as other lobber-style enemies) rather than a direct
  `fireProjectileAngle` call; `ds39Sandwraith`/`ds40Scarabswarm` are the `types-1.js` enemies
  literally named `sandwraith`/`scarabswarm` — distinct ids from the unrelated `desert-extra.js`
  enemies of similar theme, so despite the naming overlap in flavor these are separate `ENEMY_TYPES`
  entries with separate handlers.
- **`js/systems/ai-desert3.js`** — 16 handlers (`ds41Chitinhusk` through `ds56Banshee`), covering
  every `stage:2` enemy across `js/data/enemies/types-2.js` (10) and `js/data/enemies/types-4.js`
  (6) combined into one file. `ds42Quicksandlurker` and `ds48Sandtrapper` establish the
  buried/telegraph/leap pattern (`e.buried`/`e.telegraphing`/`e.leaping` state machine driving a
  short wind-up then a committed dash) that `ai-desert4.js`'s ambush handlers reuse.
- **`js/systems/ai-desert4.js`** — 7 handlers (`ds57Dunepouncer` through `ds63Dnbfirefly`), the
  final batch: 5 from `js/data/enemies/legacy-extra.js` (`dunepouncer`, `miragestrafer`,
  `twinfangviper`, `sandambusher`, `heatwavegunner` — the `stage:2` row of that file's
  pouncer/strafer/splitshot desert set) and 2 from `js/data/enemies/flies.js`
  (`dnbgnatswarm`, `dnbfirefly` — the file's only two `stage:2` entries; its many `stage:'universal'`
  flies were left untouched as out of scope). `ds57Dunepouncer`/`ds60Sandambusher` reuse the same
  buried/telegraph/leap pattern as `ai-desert3.js`'s ambushers; `ds59Twinfangviper` fires a
  diverging bolt pair (`desertAim(e,player) ± e.splitAngle`) replacing the generic `splitshot`
  behavior.

Each file's enemy data entries had their `behavior:` field repointed from the old generic name
(e.g. `'pouncer'`, `'strafer'`, `'swarm'`, `'flyer'`) to the new bespoke handler id
(`ds<N><CapitalizedName>`); no other fields changed. `combat-3.js` needed no edit — its
`ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS[e.behavior]` fallback dispatch already resolves any unrecognized
`behavior:` string as a handler-table lookup.

## Skill tree Phase C3 — render polish for the 260-node tabs (`js/achievements/skilltree.js`)

Rendering-only pass; no node data, cost, gating or effect semantics changed.

**Synergy marker.** Every node carrying a `synergyStat` effect now renders a `◈` badge
(`.skilltree-node-synergy`, mid-left of the node box so it never collides with the existing
cost/rank/gate/unique/lock/refund badges) and gains the `synergy` node class. Its `title` string
gains a `[SYNERGY — ...]` clause listing the tag(s) the payoff counts. A `Synergy` entry was added
to `#skillTreeFilterBar` (`data-filter="synergy"`, matched in the node loop's `matchesFilter`
chain) and a `◈` row to `#skillTreeLegend`. Previously a synergy payoff node was visually
indistinguishable from a plain node.

**Radial layout retune.** `computeSkillTreeLayout` now assigns angles *before* ring radii, so ring
radius can be driven by the real minimum angular gap at that depth instead of the old uniform
`count × MIN_ARC / 2π` estimate (which under-counted crowding because angles are allocated by
subtree weight, not evenly). Per ring: `r = max(base, uniformEstimate, min(packedNeed,
base × SKILL_TREE_MAX_RING_INFLATE))` where `packedNeed = MIN_ARC / (2·sin(gap/2))`. Residual
collisions are then resolved by a radial stagger pass — nodes at one depth are walked in angle
order and pushed into tier 0/1/2 (`tier × SKILL_TREE_STAGGER_STEP` extra radius) whenever the chord
to the previous node in that tier is under `SKILL_TREE_MIN_ARC`. New constants:
`SKILL_TREE_MAX_RING_INFLATE = 1.6`, `SKILL_TREE_MIN_ANGLE_GAP = 0.0035`,
`SKILL_TREE_STAGGER_STEP = 84`, `SKILL_TREE_MAX_STAGGER_TIERS = 3`; retuned
`SKILL_TREE_RING_BASE 240→260`, `SKILL_TREE_RING_STEP 190→210`, `SKILL_TREE_MIN_ARC 120→128`.

**Zoom-to-branch.** New `#skillTreeBranchBar` strip (between the filter bar and the tree body),
rebuilt each `buildSkillTreePanel()` from the *visible* nodes grouped by the existing
`skillNodeBranchKey(id)` (`tab|letter`). Each button shows `LETTER owned/total`, is tinted by
`skillTreeBranchHue(key)` (deterministic hash → hue, also used by the minimap), and calls the new
`focusOnRect(x0,y0,x1,y1)` which fits `skillTreeZoom` to that branch's pixel bounding box
(`SKILL_TREE_BRANCH_FOCUS_PAD` padding, clamped to `SKILL_TREE_ZOOM_MIN/MAX`) and centres the pan
on it. A leading `Whole tree` button fits the entire canvas. The active branch is tracked in the
module-level `skillTreeFocusedBranch`, cleared by `resetSkillTreeCamera()` (tab switch) and by the
Recenter button.

**Minimap legibility.** `#skillTreeMinimap` grew 170×130 → 240×180 (HTML attributes and the CSS
box; `.skilltree-zoom-readout` moved up to match). `drawMinimap()` brightened the owned/buyable
colours, scales dot radius by density (`minimapPoints.length > 180`), tints *unowned* dots by
branch hue instead of one flat grey, rings buyable dots in white, and rings synergy nodes in green
(`minimapPoints` entries gained `synergy` and `branch` fields).

### Phase 42 — Inferno generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 1 (`ai-inferno1.js`)

The same treatment Phases 20/21 gave the Crypt and Phases 38/39 gave the Forest, now applied to the
Inferno floor's generic `stage:3` roster in `js/data/enemies/types-1.js`. Before it, the 25 inferno
ids shared 18 generic behaviors — three ids were plain `chaser`, three plain `ranged`, two `sentry`,
two `whiplash`, and so on. All 25 now have their own AI.

**New file `js/systems/ai-inferno1.js`** — script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after
`ai-desert4.js` and before `ai-mirrorboss.js` (and therefore after `ai-1.js`/`ai-2.js`, which define
the generic AI functions it wraps). Structure mirrors `ai-forest1.js` exactly:

- **`const INFERNO_ID_AI`** — id-keyed override table, consulted before the generic function body.
- **`infernoWrapById(fn)`** — returns a wrapper that dispatches to `INFERNO_ID_AI[e.type.id]` when an
  entry exists and otherwise calls `fn`. Installed at the bottom of the file by reassigning the two
  globals it needs to intercept: `aiChase = infernoWrapById(aiChase); aiTurret = infernoWrapById(aiTurret);`.
  Because this file loads after `ai-crypt3.js`, `ai-forest1.js`, `ai-forest2.js` and `ai-desert1..4.js`,
  it reads whatever `aiChase`/`aiTurret` currently are and composes *over* those wrappers rather than
  replacing them, so `CRYPT3_ID_AI` / `FOREST_ID_AI` ids still resolve through the inner wrappers.
  Lookup order at call time is inferno → desert → forest → crypt → original `ai-1.js` body. No change
  to `updateEnemy` in `combat-3.js` was needed; renamed ids reach their handler through the existing
  `default:` branch's `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS[String(e.behavior)]` lookup.
- Local helpers, all `inferno*`-prefixed so they cannot collide with the `crypt*` / `forest*` sets:
  `infernoStep(game, e, dt, dx, dy, mul)` (normalised obstacle-aware step, returns the `tryMoveEntity`
  result so handlers can detect wall contact), `infernoRing`, `infernoArc`, `infernoAim(e, player)`,
  `infernoSpawn(game, node, id, x, y)`, plus two inferno-specific additions:
  `infernoScorch(game, e, x, y, radius, dmg)` (pushes an `Explosion` and applies its damage to the
  player if in radius — the shared fire-patch primitive used by the trail/crater/vent handlers) and
  `infernoTrack(e, player, dt)` (per-enemy smoothed estimate of player velocity in `e.inf1VX/inf1VY`,
  since `Player` has no `vx`/`vy` field; used by the lead-prediction handlers).
- Per-entity scratch state uses the `inf1*` field prefix, lazily initialised on first tick.

**Two ids keep their original `behavior` string** because it is load-bearing elsewhere, and get their
AI through `INFERNO_ID_AI` instead:

- `infernoguardian` (`shielded`, read by `combat-3.js:103` for the shield/vuln timer, `entities.js:409`
  for initial spawn state, `ai-1.js:420`'s shielder-targeting skip and `ai-crypt5.js:129`) — plants
  itself while shielded and pulses a slowly rotating 3-bolt ring every 0.75s, then abandons all ranged
  attack and charges at 1.9x for the whole vulnerable window.
- `obsidiansentinel` (`turret`, read by `combat-3.js:479` for the `fromTurret` bolt flag and
  `utils-1.js:1404/1409` for sprite caching / static pose) — heat-building turret: each shot with the
  player in LOS shortens its own cooldown (1.5s → floor 0.42s); after 6 shots it overheats, vents a
  10-bolt ring and goes shielded and inert for 1.4s. Losing LOS bleeds the heat counter back down.

**The other 23 ids** were renamed to fresh `inf1*` behavior keys with a dedicated handler each:
`inf1Emberling` (heat meter ramps speed 1.0x→1.9x near the player, vented to zero on any wall bump),
`inf1Cinderhound` (flank-orbit then 0.3s pounce, flank side flipping each pounce),
`inf1Ashwraith` (alternates solid firing passes with an intangible `submerged`+`shielded` drift
straight through the player, resolidifying into a 2-bolt ash spray),
`inf1Brimstonebomber` (drips a half-damage scorch patch every 0.85s along its approach before the
full fuse blast + 8-bolt ring),
`inf1Hellcharger` (charge that explodes on wall impact and chains up to 2 more charges, but is spent
outright if the dash times out in open floor),
`inf1Magmaleaper` (leaps to a lead-predicted point with flight time scaled to distance, cratering on
landing with a scorch + 4-bolt splash),
