`inf1Emberarcher` (0.5s draw during which it backsteps, releasing 3 arrows at staggered speeds down
one line so they arrive in sequence),
`inf1Soulflame` (golden-angle spiral: each volley is an aimed bolt plus an opposed pair on an axis
advanced 2.4 rad, while it orbits at keep-distance),
`inf1Ashlurker` (buried `submerged`+`shielded` until tripped, erupting with a scorch + 6-bolt ring
and 2 chained dashes; re-buries if the player gets past 400),
`inf1Flamewalker` (leaves a flame pillar at the departure tile and arrives on a fixed triangle of
blink points around the player with a 5-bolt fan),
`inf1Cinderwarden` (0.8s charge-up, then hands out shields one ally at a time nearest-first, up to 3,
and is itself shielded for the whole grant sequence),
`inf1Magmamortar` (3-shell straddle salvo whose landing points are spaced along the player's tracked
movement bearing),
`inf1Emberweaver` (weave amplitude grows as it closes, and it drops a perpendicular bolt at each
weave crossing, laying a fire corridor),
`inf1Slagsentry` (dormant and shielded until damaged *or* approached in LOS; re-hardens and regains
1 hp when it loses the player),
`inf1Flarecircler` (orbit radius oscillates ±38 and it fires a tangent-leading 2-bolt spread on
entering every third orbit quadrant),
`inf1Magmadelver` (leaves periodic half-damage magma gouts along its underground path before the
surface eruption),
`inf1Pyrecaller` (1.2s shielded pyre build, then releases its whole summon batch in a ring plus a
6-bolt ring in the same beat),
`inf1Embertender` (tethers to the single most wounded ally and only heals in contact range, for
double the normal amount, emitting a damaging heat ring on every heal),
`inf1Cinderwisp` (fires only at the crest of its bob cycle, and creeps its keep-distance 22 closer
per shot until it resets out at 100),
`inf1Ashskitter` (chains short straight dashes with micro-rests; every 4th dash is a diagonal
overshoot past the player),
`inf1Moltensentinel` (alternates an armored immobile 3-bolt-spread phase with a 1.3s unshielded
1.6x molten advance that ends in a scorch),
`inf1Cinderlash` (whip resolves as a 180° frontal arc locked to the facing captured at telegraph
start, plus 3 slow bolts along that arc; strafes at whip range between swings),
`inf1Emberwhip` (double crack: a short first hit, then a 0.2s re-wind and a lunging second crack at
1.6x reach with a 2-bolt spray).

Each handler is a distinct movement/attack pattern rather than a parameter tweak of the generic
behavior it replaced — the three former `ranged` ids now differ structurally (staggered-speed volley
vs. golden-angle spiral vs. bob-crest sniping), and the two former `sentry` ids differ in wake
condition and in what the awake state does.

**Known cosmetic regression, carried forward from the crypt/forest precedent.** `Util._humanoidStatic`
/ `Util.drawBrownHumanoid` in `utils-2.js` branch on `e.behavior` to add per-behavior ornaments, so
the 23 renamed ids no longer match any branch and fall back to the plain shared body. The fix is the
id-keyed mark table pattern (`CRYPT_ENEMY_MARKS` / `FOREST_ENEMY_MARKS`); an `INFERNO_ENEMY_MARKS`
pass is explicitly a later batch and was not done here.

### Phase 43 — Inferno generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 2 (`ai-inferno2.js`)

Batch 2 of the Inferno pass, covering the 18 `stage:3` generic ids that live in
`js/data/enemies/types-2.js`. Before it those 18 ids shared 13 generic behaviors — `splitter` was
used three times, `sniper`, `swarm` and `leaper` twice each.

**New file `js/systems/ai-inferno2.js`** — script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after
`ai-inferno1.js` and before `ai-mirrorboss.js`. It follows the `ai-forest2.js` precedent exactly:
it declares no wrapper and no helpers of its own, reusing `INFERNO_ID_AI`, `infernoStep`,
`infernoRing`, `infernoArc`, `infernoAim`, `infernoScorch` and `infernoTrack` from `ai-inferno1.js`
(both are plain global scripts, so those file-scope bindings are visible), and adds keys to the
existing `INFERNO_ID_AI` object rather than re-declaring it or re-wrapping `aiChase`/`aiTurret` —
the two wrapper installs at `ai-inferno1.js`'s tail already cover the new entries, since the
wrapper reads the table at call time. Per-entity scratch state uses the `inf2*` field prefix,
lazily initialised on first tick.

**Two ids keep their original `behavior` string** (load-bearing elsewhere) and get their AI through
new `INFERNO_ID_AI` entries:

- `magmaspire` (`turret`, read by `combat-3.js` for the `fromTurret` bolt flag and by `utils-1.js`
  for sprite caching / the static pose) — rotating spire head: a bearing sweeps at 1.35 rad/s and
  fires its 4-bolt spread down the *head* angle rather than at the player, so the spread only
  connects as the sweep crosses; the sweep reverses every time it passes the player's bearing, and
  every 4th reversal the spire erupts a 10-bolt ring plus a ground scorch.
- `cindershielded` (`shielded`, read by `combat-3.js:103` for the shield/vuln timer, `entities.js`
  for initial spawn state, `ai-1.js`'s shielder-targeting skip and `ai-crypt5.js`) — heat battery:
  advances slowly and silently while shielded, banking one heat stack per second (cap 4); the
  instant `combat-3.js` flips the shield off it dumps the bank as a nova whose scorch radius and
  ring density scale with the stacks, then kites backwards at 1.5x and plinks single bolts for the
  whole vulnerable window.

**The other 16 ids** were renamed to fresh `inf2*` behavior keys with a dedicated handler each:
`inf2Slagbloater` (swell cycle — radius grows and speed drops over ~2.2s, then it bursts a scorch
plus an 8-bolt slag ring and deflates, without dying), `inf2Cindermites` (true flocking — steers
toward the centroid of same-id mites within 110 and gains up to 1.55x speed with pack size, but
panics and flees when isolated), `inf2Pyremarksman` (locks its aim vector at telegraph *start* and
fires 3 bolts 0.11s apart down that frozen line, so strafing beats it; flips its strafe side each
burst), `inf2Cinderdrone` (pressure fuse — spirals in while revving, and once armed the fuse burns
2.6x faster while the player is inside the blast radius and 0.7x slower outside),
`inf2Charhusk` (cracks at each third of hp lost, each crack venting a widening ring plus a scorch
and, past two cracks, switching locomotion from a steady chase to 0.3s lunges),
`inf2Emberchanter` (stationary 3-beat chant firing a 1→3→5-bolt widening arc, releasing a 7-bolt
fan plus a 6-bolt ring on the third beat; the whole chant is cancelled and reset if the player
closes inside 130), `inf2Obsidianpouncer` (goes `shielded` for the entire telegraph and pounce, then
shatters on landing into 6 obsidian shards and runs hot at 1.5x for 1s while unshielded),
`inf2Sootmarksman` (veiled sniper — spends its cooldown `submerged`+`shielded` walking to a firing
post at least ~100° around the player, surfaces only for the telegraph and the shot, and drops a
soot scorch as it re-veils), `inf2Sparkmites` (static charge — high-frequency zigzag while charging
for 1.5s, then a short-range zap that damages the player inside 62 and a 4-bolt spark ring, followed
by a 0.28s recoil away), `inf2Slagorbiter` (decaying orbit — spirals in from 200 to 70 at 34/s
firing tangentially with cooldown scaled by current radius, slams a scorch at the inner radius and
springs back out with its orbit direction reversed), `inf2Ashsentry` (ash pile — `submerged` and
`shielded` until the player enters range in LOS, waking with an eruption scorch; awake it fires
cardinal/diagonal 4-bolt rings that alternate each shot instead of aiming, and re-buries with +2 hp
after 3s without LOS), `inf2Pyreburrower` (fire tunnel — lays a half-damage scorch every 0.28s along
its `submerged` path, then surfaces into a 3-stage geyser: three rings 0.18s apart with rising bolt
speed and scorch radius), `inf2Brimstoneskirmisher` (dashes *through* the player at 1.9x dash speed
rather than retreating, firing a 3-bolt spray backwards over its shoulder at the crossing point,
then re-engages from the far side; a plain 3-bolt shotgun on its own fire timer between passes),
`inf2Embersplitter` (bounce roll — 0.6s wind-up then a 2.6x roll that ricochets off walls up to 3
times, reflecting the component that was blocked and dropping a scorch plus a 4-bolt burst at each
impact), `inf2Sootstrafer` (flies a randomly-tilted lemniscate around the player rather than a
circle, firing a 2-bolt spread and dropping a soot scorch each time it crosses the figure-eight's
centre), `inf2Cinderleaper` (hop chain — three leaps in quick succession with only a 0.1s re-wind
between them; the first two are short 0.16s hops leaving small scorches, the third is a long 0.3s
leap that craters with a scorch plus a 5-bolt ring).

Each handler is a distinct movement/attack pattern rather than a parameter tweak — the two former
`sniper` ids differ structurally (frozen-line burst vs. submerged repositioning veil), the two
former `swarm` ids differ in what drives their motion (neighbour flocking vs. a charge/discharge
cycle), the two former `leaper` ids differ in leap structure (single shielded shatter-pounce vs. a
three-hop chain), and the three former `splitter` ids share nothing but their `splitInto` field,
which was left untouched. Per-entity scratch fields all use the `inf2` prefix.

**Known cosmetic regression, carried forward.** As in batch 1, the 16 renamed ids no longer match
the `behavior`-keyed ornament branches in `Util._humanoidStatic` / `Util.drawBrownHumanoid` and fall
back to the plain shared body; an `INFERNO_ENEMY_MARKS` pass remains a later batch.
`magmaspire`'s turret sprite/`fromTurret` flag and `cindershielded`'s shield timer and
shielder-targeting exclusion all keep working untouched, because their `behavior:` fields are
preserved.

Audit: `feature-research/inferno-enemy-rework/audit-batch2.md`.

### Phase 44 — Inferno generic-enemy unique-AI rework, batch 3 (`ai-inferno3.js`)

Batch 3 — the **final** Inferno batch — covering the last 14 `stage:3` generic ids, which live
outside `types-1.js`/`types-2.js`: seven in `js/data/enemies/types-4.js`, two in
`js/data/enemies/flies.js` and five in `js/data/enemies/legacy-extra.js`. Before it those 14 shared
nine generic behaviors — `strafer` was used three times, `sniper` and `pouncer` twice each.

**New file `js/systems/ai-inferno3.js`** — script-tagged in `index.html` immediately after
`ai-inferno2.js` and before `ai-mirrorboss.js`. It follows the `ai-crypt4.js` precedent: a batch
spanning several non-`types-1/2` data files in which **no id's `behavior` string is load-bearing**,
so the file contains nothing but 14 `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS.inf3*` handlers — no `INFERNO_ID_AI`
entries, no wrapper install and no helper declarations. Like `ai-inferno2.js` it reuses
`infernoStep`, `infernoRing`, `infernoArc`, `infernoAim`, `infernoScorch` and `infernoTrack` from
`ai-inferno1.js` (plain global scripts, so those file-scope bindings are visible). All 14 renamed
ids reach their handler through the existing `default:` branch of `combat-3.js`'s dispatch switch,
so `combat-3.js` was not touched. Per-entity scratch state uses the `inf3*` field prefix, lazily
initialised on first tick; `infernoTrack`'s own `inf1VX`/`inf1VY` player-velocity fields are read
directly by the four handlers that lead their shots.

**The 14 handlers:**

- `inf3Cinderchoir` (was `healer`) — choral heal: banks one "verse" per beat (cap 3) and, at three
  verses, heals *every* wounded ally inside `healRadius` at once instead of the single nearest one,
  then vents a bolt ring. Harmony: each other Cinder Choir within 240 speeds the beat and raises the
  heal amount and ring density, so choirs stack superlinearly.
- `inf3Pyrecircler` (was `orbiter`) — draws a fire ring: orbits at a fixed radius laying a
  half-damage scorch every 0.5 rad of arc, so a full lap literally encircles the player in burning
  ground; on closing the lap it erupts an 8-bolt ring plus a scorch and reverses direction.
- `inf3Slagmarksman` (was `sniper`) — predictive slug gun with a heat budget: leads the shot by the
  player's tracked velocity scaled to bolt travel time, and each shot shortens both its telegraph
  and its cooldown until the third, which forces a 1.3s vent (backing away, ending in a scorch).
- `inf3Emberwarden` (was `shielder`) — stationary ward: plants at long range and, while planted,
  refreshes `shielded`/`grantedShield` on *all* eligible allies inside `shieldRadius` every 0.3s
  rather than granting to one ally at a time. It cannot move while warding and breaks with a
  repulse nova if the player pushes inside 55% of the ward radius.
- `inf3Wraithbat` (was `sniper`) — punishes standing still: drifts `submerged`+`shielded` around a
  250 ring biased against the player's movement, accumulating "stillness" only while the player's
  tracked speed is under 40; at 0.45s of stillness it materialises, telegraphs and fires a
  twin-bolt soul shot, then fades again.
- `inf3Phantomhawk` (was `skirmisher`) — stooping dive: circles at engage range plinking bolts,
  then telegraphs and dives at 3.4x dash speed to the player's *predicted* position, craters with a
  scorch plus a 3-bolt spray, and climbs back out `shielded` on a wider ring with its circle
  direction reversed.
- `inf3Duskfalcon` (was `ranged`) — range-cycling burst kiter: kites the wide `keepDistance` ring
  firing single bolts, and after four of them folds into a stoop, dropping to 42% of the ring to
  dump a five-bolt burst 0.09s apart before pulling back out and flipping its circle direction.
- `inf3Dnbhornet` (was `charger`) — stinger chain: buzzes in on a weaving approach, dashes, and
  instead of resetting on landing follows with three rapid 0.13s jab-lunges separated by short
  sidesteps, then retreats hard for 0.45s before the next charge.
- `inf3Dnbwasp` (was `strafer`) — damage-reactive harrier: strafes a tight fast ring, but every
  point of hp it loses instantly flips its orbit direction, kicks the ring out to 1.7x for 0.7s at
  1.6x speed and sprays a 3-bolt arc — so hitting it is what makes it dangerous.
- `inf3Cinderpouncer` (was `pouncer`) — coil charge: buries in the ash (`submerged`) building coil
  at 0.5/s; the coil widens its trigger range and scales leap speed, leap duration and landing
  scorch radius, with a full coil adding a 6-bolt ring on impact.
- `inf3Ashstrafer` (was `strafer`) — pincer pairing: seeks the nearest other Ash Strafer and holds
  the point on the ring exactly opposite it, so pairs cross-fire from both sides; while paired it
  fires a 3-bolt arc at 0.6x cooldown, alone it falls back to a plain ring strafe with single bolts.
  Every shot also drops a small ash scorch under itself.
- `inf3Twinflameimp` (was `splitshot`) — closing scissor, a reimagining of the old static diverging
  pair: it still fires two jets at `±splitAngle`, but the gap *narrows* by 32% each volley for as
  long as the player's bearing barely changes, and resets to full width the moment they swing more
  than 0.35 rad. When the jets converge below 0.08 rad they merge into one fast heavy lance, then
  the scissor resets on a long cooldown. Alternating lead head staggers the two bolts' speeds.
- `inf3Slagambusher` (was `pouncer`) — hurl-and-follow: lobs a slag marker at the player's predicted
  position (`lobX`/`lobY`/`lobTimer`, so the existing lob telegraph renders), then leaps along its
  own lob for the last 0.55s so it arrives exactly as the slag detonates into a scorch plus a
  7-bolt ring.
- `inf3Embermarksman` (was `strafer`) — sighting discipline: builds "sight" only while it holds LOS
  at long range, bleeding it off 2.5x as fast when LOS breaks or the player closes; at 1.3s of
  uninterrupted sight it locks the aim angle and fires a 3-bolt stagger of accelerating bolts down
  that frozen line. Breaking LOS is the counter, not dodging.

The repeated old behaviors now differ structurally: the three former `strafer` ids diverge into
partner-pincer, damage-reactive flip and LOS-gated sighting; the two former `sniper` ids into
velocity-leading heat management vs. a stillness-punishing phase sniper; the two former `pouncer`
ids into a coil-charged ambush vs. a lob-and-follow slam.

**No exceptions.** None of these 14 ids uses `shielded`, `turret` or any other `behavior` string
read outside AI dispatch, so this batch adds no `INFERNO_ID_AI` entries, redeclares nothing, and
leaves `ai-inferno1.js`'s wrapper install untouched. `pouncer`, `strafer` and `splitshot` remain
live `ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS` entries in `ai-newshared.js` for the other biomes' enemies that still
use them.

**Inferno rework complete.** With this batch all 57 generic `stage:3` enemies — 25 in batch 1
(`ai-inferno1.js`), 18 in batch 2 (`ai-inferno2.js`) and 14 here — now run bespoke per-id AI, the
same end-state the Crypt reached at `ai-crypt4.js` and the Forest at `ai-forest2.js`.

**Known cosmetic regression, carried forward.** As in batches 1 and 2, the renamed ids no longer
match the `behavior`-keyed ornament branches in `Util._humanoidStatic` / `Util.drawBrownHumanoid`
and fall back to the plain shared body; an `INFERNO_ENEMY_MARKS` pass remains deferred.

Audit: `feature-research/inferno-enemy-rework/audit-batch3.md`.

## Procedural room generation batch 2 — new `js/systems/procgen-rooms.js`

**Purpose.** A standalone, side-effect-free helper module for the procedural
room-generation revamp: a weighted room-shape/mask picker, a door-clearance
tile helper, and a room pathability validator. Loaded in `index.html` between
`systems/room.js` and `entities/entities.js`. **Nothing calls into it yet** —
batch 2 only lands the module and its exports; batch 3 wires
`pickProceduralMask` into `dungeon.js`'s `normal`-room generation and runs the
clearance/connectivity checks over scattered obstacles.

It reads globals defined elsewhere: `ROOM_SHAPES` (`data/core.js`), `BLOCK`/
`TILE` (`data/core.js`), `OBSTACLES` (`data/collectibles.js`), `Util`,
`computeDoorSlots`/`isDoorDisabled` (`systems/dungeon.js`), and the `T_VOID`/
`T_WALL`/`T_SECRET` tile constants (`systems/room.js`). It defines no new mask
format — every shape it returns is an existing `ROOM_SHAPES` mask.

### Shape table

- **`PROCGEN_MASK_GROUPS`** — weighted groups over `ROOM_SHAPES` names, picked
  group-first (`Util.weighted`) then uniformly inside the group
  (`Util.choice`):
  Rebalanced by the visual-overhaul **batch A** shape pass from the original
  70/10/10/6/4 so that irregular and large rooms are common rather than rare
  (70% single → 30% single; the notched + big groups go from 10% combined to
  40% combined):
  - weight 30 — `single` (`[[1]]`)
  - weight 15 — `wideDom` (`[[1,1]]`)
  - weight 15 — `tallDom` (`[[1],[1]]`)
  - weight 25 — the notched set: `lA`/`lB`/`lC`/`lD`/`tShape`/`tShape2`/
    `sShape`/`zShape` plus batch A's `plus`/`uShape`
  - weight 15 — the big set: `lBig1`/`lBig2` plus batch A's `bigNotch`/
    `hallWide`/`hallTall`
- **`PROCGEN_FREE_ROOM_TYPES`** = `{'normal', 'floorfeature', 'boss',
  'miniboss'}` — the room types allowed a multi-block mask. `boss` and
  `miniboss` were added by the visual-overhaul **batch A** shape pass: unlike
  every fixture/special type, their `populateRoomProcedural` branches place
  exactly one enemy at `findNearestFloor(node, tileW/2, tileH/2)`, which
  already resolves to a real floor tile for any mask (including one whose
  geometric centre falls in a notch), so they took zero code change. Every
  other type stays forced to the single block.
- **`procgenShapeByName(name)`** — `ROOM_SHAPES` lookup, falls back to entry 0
  (`single`).
- **`cloneMask(mask)`** — row-wise copy, so callers never alias the shared
  `ROOM_SHAPES` mask arrays.
- **`pickProceduralMask(roomType)`** → `{ mask, template: null }` — the same
  return shape as `dungeon.js`'s `pickMaskForType`, so it is a drop-in
  replacement at that call site. Any type outside `PROCGEN_FREE_ROOM_TYPES`
  (boss, miniboss, shop, treasure, petshop, shrine, vault, karma, arcade,
  curse, sacrifice, challenge, bosschallenge, crystal, sombra, secret,
  supersecret, mirror, start, …) is **forced to the single block**: those
  rooms' fixture placement in `room.js` is written against one rectangular
  block (shop's 0.82/0.82 corners, karma's quadrants, mirror's top/bottom
  split), and an L/T/S/Z/plus mask can collapse those fractions into one
  surviving block or a missing one. This is strictly safer than today, where
  `chooseShapeForNode`'s no-template fallback can already hand such a type a
  multi-block shape.
- `tileW`/`tileH` are deliberately **not** set here — `room.js`'s
  `buildRoomTiles` still derives them from the mask bounding box
  (`mask[0].length * BLOCK + 2` / `mask.length * BLOCK + 2`).

### Door clearance

- **`doorFrontZoneTiles(col, row, dir)`** — the 2x2 room-tile block just
  inside a door on block cell `(col,row)`, in room-tile space: N →
  `x ∈ {c*BLOCK+5, +6}, y ∈ {r*BLOCK+1, +2}`; S → same xs, `y ∈ {+9, +10}`;
  W → `x ∈ {+1, +2}, y ∈ {r*BLOCK+5, +6}`; E → `x ∈ {+9, +10}`, same ys. This
  is the runtime port of `tools/lint-room-templates.js`'s `doorFrontZone`, and
  the offsets line up with `room.js`'s `doorSlotCells` plus the 1-tile wall
  border `buildRoomTiles` adds.
- **`doorInteriorTile(slot)`** — the single tile of that zone nearest the door
  (the BFS entry point).
- **`procgenActiveDoorSlots(node)`** — `node.doorSlots` (computing them via
  `computeDoorSlots` if the node has none yet), filtered to slots that are
  neither `slot.disabled` nor `isDoorDisabled(node.template, …)`.
- **`doorClearanceTiles(node)`** → deduped array of `{x,y}` tiles that must be
  left free of obstacles (2x2 per active door).

### Pathability

- **`procgenObstacleBlockKeys(obstacles)`** → `Set` of `"x,y"` tile keys for
  every non-destroyed obstacle whose `OBSTACLES[kind].walkable` is falsy.
  Walkable kinds (currents, mud, sandtrap, …) never block, even the `hazard`
  ones. Accepts either real `Obstacle` instances or plain `{kind, tx, ty}` /
  `{kind, x, y}` records (pixel coords are floored by `TILE`).
- **`procgenTileBlocked(node, x, y, obstacleKeys)`** — out of bounds, or
  `T_VOID`/`T_WALL`/`T_SECRET` (the same tile test `combat-1.js`'s
  `isTileSolidForEntity` applies — not a copy of that function, just the same
  three tile types), or an obstacle key hit. `T_DOOR` is walkable here, since
  connectivity is about layout, not about whether doors are currently open.
- **`roomIsFullyConnected(node, obstacles)`** — BFS over 4-neighbours from the
  first active door's interior tile; returns `true` iff every active door's
  interior tile is unblocked and reachable. Rooms with fewer than two active
  doors trivially return `true`.

**Verification.** `feature-research/procedural-room-generation/harness-batch2.js`
is a Node/`vm` harness that loads the real source files and exercises all three
helpers; see `audit-batch2.md` for counts.

## Room generation completeness pass — `systems/room.js`, `ui/render.js`

User request: "heavily improve room generation... binding of isaac esque rooms, they need to feel complete." Four independent, purely-additive batches (D-G), all inside the existing `populateRoomProcedural` pipeline — no new room types, no `ROOM_TEMPLATES` revival (confirmed dead outside `wavearena`).

### Batch D — boss/miniboss arena scatter — `room.js`

`ARENA_SCATTER_MAX = 6`, `arenaScatterCount(node)` → `min(ARENA_SCATTER_MAX, 1 + floor(roomBlockCount(node) * 1.5))`. The `boss` and `miniboss` branches (previously bare beyond the boss/miniboss spawn) now each call `enforcePathability(scatterObstacles(Util.randi(ceil(arenaCount*0.5), arenaCount)))` right after spawning the enemy, where `arenaCount = arenaScatterCount(node)`. Safe by construction: `spots` already excludes near-door and near-center tiles (`roomFloorTiles(node, {avoidDoors:2.5, avoidCenter:1.2})`), so the boss spawn point is never overwritten.

### Batch E — reward framing — `room.js`

**`frameReward(node, cx, cy, flavor, opts)`** — places a small symmetric flanking decoration pair around a reward pedestal tile `(cx,cy)`, pushing `{kind, tx, ty, x, y, seed, scale, flip}` records into `node.rewardFrame` (a new node array, seeded from `spots`-adjacent tiles, skipped silently if none are free). Wired into the `treasure`, `curse` (pedestal sub-branch), `supersecret`, and `star` branches, each calling `frameReward(...)` right after placing their pedestal. Deliberately **not** applied to `vault` (no single anchor — rewards come from generic `takeSpot()`, no pedestal) or `crystal`/`sombra` (already place their own multi-pedestal symmetric pattern; framing each individually was judged likely to clutter).

`generateRoomDecor(node, flavor, spots)`'s first line changed from `node.decorProps = []` to `node.decorProps = (node.rewardFrame || []).slice()`, and its prop-count cap changed from `Math.min(DECOR_MAX_PROPS, ...)` to `Math.min(DECOR_MAX_PROPS - node.decorProps.length, ...)` so frame props count against the same budget instead of stacking on top of it. `decorBlockedTiles(node)` extended with `for (const f of node.rewardFrame || []) add(f.tx, f.ty)` so the generic decor scatter can't double-place on frame tiles. No render.js changes needed — `decorProps` was already drawn generically by kind/position/seed/scale/flip.

### Batch F — wall focal props (torches) — `render.js`

`ROOM_TORCH_TYPES` — `Set` of room types considered "important" enough to get wall torches (boss, miniboss, treasure, shop, curse, star, supersecret, vault, crystal, sombra). `roomTorchTiles(node)` — scans the room's tile grid for the bounding box of floor/door/secret-open tiles, returns a `Set` of up to 2 wall-tile keys (`"x,y"`) directly above the leftmost and rightmost bbox columns, or `null` if the room's type isn't in `ROOM_TORCH_TYPES` or it has no floor tiles. Degrades gracefully (0-2 torches) on irregular/notched shapes where the exact wall tile above the column doesn't exist. `drawWallTorch(ctx, px, py, pal, x, y)` — hand-drawn bracket+flame silhouette, using `tileRand(x,y,231)` for a static per-tile "lean" jitter (baked once, not animated — see below), colored from `pal.wall`/`pal.accent`, with a `ctx.shadowBlur` glow.

Wired into `rebuildTileLayer(node, pal)`: `const torchTiles = roomTorchTiles(node)` computed once per bake, and inside the `T_WALL`/`T_SECRET` tile-draw branch, `if (torchTiles && torchTiles.has(x+','+y)) drawWallTorch(...)` right before that branch's `continue`. Since `rebuildTileLayer` only runs when the room's tile cache is dirty, torches are genuinely zero runtime cost per frame — but this also means they're static (no time-based flicker), hence the `tileRand`-seeded jitter instead of an animated flame.

### Batch G — macro set-pieces for normal rooms — `room.js`

`PROCGEN_SETPIECE_CHANCE = 0.2`. `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_SHAPE_BUILDERS` is a 10-entry library of `(r,cx,cy) => [[x,y],...]` shape families (diagonal-corner diamond, cardinal cross, two pillar orientations, an 8-point ring, corners+center, two staggered-pair variants, and two double-line variants), each parameterized only by a radius `r`. `buildSetpiecePatternPool(radii)` cross-multiplies every builder against a radius list into a flat array of zero-arg-free pattern functions `(cx,cy) => positions`; `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_POOL_GENERIC` uses `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_RADII_GENERIC = [2]` (10 patterns — 10 builders × 1 radius) and `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_POOL_CORE` uses `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_RADII_CORE = [2..11]` (100 patterns — 10 builders × 10 radii). `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_CORE_KINDS` (`rock`/`hardrock`/`tallrock`/`tallhardrock`/`pit`/`redfire`/`yellowfire`/`turretn`/`turrete`/`turrets`/`turretw`) is the "core object" list that gets the 100-pattern pool; every other scatterable kind gets the 10-pattern pool. This is a deliberate combinatorial generator (radius sweep × shape family) rather than ~800 hand-authored coordinate arrays — verified via a standalone Node script confirming exactly 10/100 entries and zero duplicate patterns in the core pool.

`applyRoomSetPiece()` (closure inside `populateRoomProcedural`) — reads `procgenRoomFloorBounds(node)` for the room's floor bounding box (bails if missing or smaller than 4x4 tiles), picks one obstacle kind via the same candidate/flavor-gating logic as `scatterObstacles` (`procgenScatterCandidates` filtered to non-strong kinds, then `PROCGEN_FLAVOR_RESTRICT`-filtered by `roomDecorFlavor`), picks the core or generic pool based on `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_CORE_KINDS.has(kind)`, and draws one random pattern function from it via `Util.choice`. For each position in the pattern: skips it if it's in `doorClearanceTiles`, or not present in the room's `spots` pool (guarantees no collision with anything already placed/reserved); otherwise splices it out of `spots` and pushes a `new Obstacle(kind, tx, ty)` onto `node.obstacles`. After placement, requires at least 2 obstacles landed and calls `roomIsFullyConnected(node, node.obstacles)` (from `procgen-rooms.js`); rolls back (removes every obstacle it just placed and returns its tile to `spots`) if either check fails — same tentative-place/verify/rollback pattern as `floorfeature`'s hazard-line placement, extended to restore `spots` so a rolled-back attempt doesn't shrink the room's remaining scatter pool. Returns the count actually placed (0 on rollback/failure).

Wired into the `normal` room branch: `PROCGEN_SETPIECE_CHANCE` chance to call `applyRoomSetPiece()` before the branch's existing `scatterObstacles` call, subtracting whatever it placed from the organic scatter budget (`Math.max(0, budget - placed)`) so a set-piece room isn't over-cluttered — it reads as "motif + a little incidental scatter," not "motif on top of a full normal room." Larger-radius core patterns naturally place fewer (or zero) obstacles in small rooms since most of their positions fall outside `spots` — this degrades gracefully rather than erroring, so small rooms still mostly get the smaller-radius/generic-shaped patterns in practice.

**Verification (all 4 batches + set-piece expansion)**: `node --check` on both `room.js` and `render.js` — pass. Standalone Node script confirmed pool sizes (10/100) and pattern uniqueness. No live playtest performed (standing convention — user verifies visual/feel result in-game).

### 50 new stage-restricted obstacles — `collectibles.js`, `room.js`

50 new `OBSTACLES` entries added to `js/data/collectibles.js` (right after `warpstreamw`, before the turret block), each carrying a `floorRules` restriction following the existing convention (`obstacleAllowedOnFloor` in `dungeon.js`). All 50 are built from three archetypes that need zero new rendering code in `Util.drawObstacle` (`utils-1.js`) — they fall through every exact-kind-name branch and land on one of the generic property-driven paths: `hazard:true` (`attackable:true,maxHp:2` two-hit-clears, or `attackable:false,destructible:true` bomb-only, matching `thornbush`/`glowbloom` precedent) and `freeze:true` (`freezeDuration`, matching `sandtrap`/`quicksand` precedent) both render via the final fallback plain-shaded-circle branch; `current:true,pushX,pushY` renders via the `ob.def && ob.def.current` generic branch (matching `currentn`/`iceslide*`/`tidesurge*`/`riptide*`/`warpstream*` precedent). No turret-family kinds were added in this pass (turret wiring needs `PROCGEN_WALL_AFFINITY_KINDS`/back-dir handling, out of scope for a pure-data content pass).

Coverage, by `floorRules`:
- **Main path (`pathExclude:'C'` for floorNum ≤ 14, no path filter for floorNum ≥ 15 — matching existing `cactus`/`thornbush`/`iceslide*` convention exactly)**: 2 each for crypt(0-1)/forest(2-3)/desert(4-5)/inferno(6-7), 3 for the floorNum 8-14 mid-fork stages, 2 each for frozendesert(15-16)/badlands(17-18)/beach(19-20)/ocean(21-22)/seafloor(23-24)/trench(25-26)/trenchdepths(27-28)/deepdark(29-30)/metarealm(31-32)/hyperspace(33-34) — 31 total.
- **C-branch (`path:'C'`)**: 1 each for all 10 C-branch stages (gutters/sewers/rainforest/mangroves/floodedundercity/coralboneyard/abyssalvents/drownedcathedral/blackcurrent/leviathansmaw) — 10 total.
- **D-branch (`path:'D'`)**: 9 across observatory(3-4)/orrery(5-6)/voidbetween(7-9) — the D-branch had zero stage-restricted obstacles before this pass (confirmed via grep), so this is its first bespoke hazard content.

All 50 ids added to `PROCGEN_SCATTER_KINDS` (so `procgenScatterCandidates` can select them) and to `PROCGEN_OPEN_AFFINITY_KINDS` (ground-hugging hazards, matching `sandtrap`/`mud`/`cactus`/`thornbush`/`stunspore` precedent — none are wall-mounted). Not added to `PROCGEN_CURRENT_DIRS` (that map is specifically for the 4-cardinal `currentn/s/e/w` family's directional-line clustering logic) or any cluster/blob family set — the new kinds scatter individually rather than clustering into lines, which is an acceptable simplification for single-direction (non-cardinal-family) current hazards.

**Verification**: `node --check` on `collectibles.js` and `room.js` — pass. Grepped all 50 new ids against the full `OBSTACLES` table to confirm no id collisions before adding. Manually traced `Util.drawObstacle`'s branch order to confirm none of the 50 new ids match any exact-kind-name branch ahead of the generic `current`/fallback branches. No live playtest performed (standing convention).

### The Final Reckoning (floorKey `9A`/`9B`) enemy rework — `ai-reckoning1.js`, `ai-reckoning2.js`, `ai-reckoning3.js`, `reckoning-new.js`

Discovered via `resolveGenericEnemy`/`resolveGenericBoss` (`room.js`) that enemy selection checks a finer-grained `floorKeyFor(floorNum, branch, floorPath)` → `e.floorKey` match *before* falling back to the coarse `stageIndexForFloor` pool — this is the mechanism (already used by every `bossXXX`-behavior boss on this stage) that scopes content to one specific floor+branch instead of the whole stage-3 bucket Inferno also lives in. Floor 9 ("The Final Reckoning") already had a full 65-enemy roster tagged `floorKey:'9A'`/`'9B'` across `types-1.js`/`types-2.js`/`types-4.js` (35 on 9A, 30 on 9B) — but every one of them was still running a stock generic behavior (`chaser`/`ranged`/`flyer`/`bomber`/`shielded`/`charger`/`turret`/`leaper`/`swarm`/`ambusher`/`teleporter`/`shielder`/`lobber`/`weaver`/`sentry`/`orbiter`/`burrower`/`sniper`/`splitter`/`summoner`/`healer`) via `combat-3.js`'s generic dispatch switch. Bosses on this stage (`shadowstalker`/`stormbringer`/`frostsentinel`/`brickgolem`, `graveChorus`/`duneravager`/`slagbound`/`glassscorpion` reused as 9A/9B pool) were already bespoke — no boss work needed.

- **`ai-reckoning1.js`** — all 35 `floorKey:'9A'` enemies given a bespoke `reck1*` handler (id-matched, e.g. `shadowcreeper` → `reck1Shadowcreeper`). Shared helpers `reckStep`/`reckAim`/`reckArc`/`reckSpawn` (same shape as `ai-inferno*.js`'s `infernoStep`/etc.) defined once here and reused by `ai-reckoning2.js`/`ai-reckoning3.js` since all three load after it.
- **`ai-reckoning2.js`** — all 30 `floorKey:'9B'` enemies given a bespoke `reck2*` handler. Frost/stone-flavored mechanics apply brief `player.freezeTimer` root taps (matching the `TIDE_ROOT_DURATION`/obstacle-freeze precedent) instead of inventing a new slow status.
- **`reckoning-new.js`** (new `js/data/enemies/` file, `Object.assign(ENEMY_TYPES, {...})`) — the 10 brand-new enemy ids requested alongside the rework: 5 for 9A (`voidrend`, `stormherald`, `hollowmarch`, `nightveil`, `voidcarver`) and 5 for 9B (`frostbastion`, `rimewarden`, `glaciermaw`, `stonechant`, `shatterbrand`), each with its own from-scratch `reck3*` handler in **`ai-reckoning3.js`** — none reuse a generic behavior name.
- Every renamed/new behavior is picked up by `combat-3.js`'s existing `default:` case (`ENEMY_BEHAVIOR_HANDLERS[String(e.behavior)]`) with zero dispatch-table changes needed.

Renames were done with a small Python script that locates each enemy's exact multi-line data block (from its `  id: { id:'id'...` opening line to the next such line) and replaces the first `behavior:'...'` occurrence inside that block only, so shared generic-behavior words (e.g. two different `'chaser'` enemies) couldn't cross-contaminate. `index.html` script order: `ai-reckoning1.js` → `ai-reckoning2.js` → `ai-reckoning3.js` right after `ai-inferno3.js`; `reckoning-new.js` right after `desert-extra.js` (before `lists.js` builds `ENEMY_LIST` from `Object.values(ENEMY_TYPES)`).

**Known cosmetic regression** (same accepted tradeoff as every prior generic-behavior rework batch): `Util._humanoidStatic`/`Util.drawBrownHumanoid` in `utils-2.js` special-case a handful of generic behavior names for extra ornament sprites; renamed ids lose those ornaments and fall back to the plain body-shade render. Not fixed — deferred, matching crypt/forest/desert/inferno precedent.

**Verification**: `node --check` on all 3 new `ai-reckoning*.js` files, `reckoning-new.js`, `types-1.js`, `types-2.js`, `types-4.js` — pass. Grepped `floorKey:'9A'`/`floorKey:'9B'` across all three enemy-data files afterward to confirm 0 lines still carry a generic behavior name. Also fixed two unrelated latent bugs found while reading nearby summoner-style handlers: `ai-desert2.js`'s `ds30Scarabcaller` and `ai-desert3.js`'s `ds45Carrioncaller` both guarded their one-time init on `e.summonTimer === undefined`, but `Enemy`'s constructor (`entities.js`) always pre-sets `summonTimer` for every enemy — so the guard never fired, leaving `e.summons`/`e.summonsOut` permanently `undefined` (a crash on `.filter` for the former, a silent "never summons" for the latter). Both now guard on their own field instead. No live playtest performed (standing convention — user verifies in-game).

`ai-c15.js` registers `c15*` handlers for all 25 non-boss `floorKey:'15C'` enemies (renamed in `cbranch2-enemies.js`) plus 15 new ones in `js/data/enemies/c15-new.js`, using `FWF_ARCH` (from `ai-waveform2.js`) via a `C15SPECS` archetype+params table. Total 40.

### Stages 16C-24C, 13C, 11C, 10C/D, 9C/D, 8C/D, 7C/D, 6C/D, 5C/D, 4C/D, 3C enemy rework (auto-generated)

Each floorKey has `js/systems/ai-c<N>.js` (`ai-k<key>.js` for 13C and below) with a `<PFX>SPECS` archetype+params table registering `<pfx><Id>` handlers via `FWF_ARCH` (`ai-waveform2.js`), plus `js/data/enemies/<tag>-new.js` with new enemies (`floorKey` set) topping the stage to >=40 non-boss enemies. Existing enemies' `behavior` was renamed in place. Generated by scratchpad scripts (`gen.py`/`auto.py`); archetype choice maps the old generic behavior to a `FWF_ARCH` type with seeded random parameters, so variety is parametric, not hand-tuned. Some pre-existing ids (`eventhorizon`, `bonecaller`, `pressurewraith`) are still defined twice.

### A/B stage top-up to 40 (9B, 10A, 11A, 11B, 12A, 12B)

`ai-t<key>.js` + `js/data/enemies/t<key>-new.js` add generated `FWF_ARCH`-based enemies (`t<key>*` handlers, `floorKey` set) so each stage has 40 non-boss enemies (9A and 10B already had >=40). Existing rosters untouched.

### C-path modifier layer (`ai-cmods.js`, `ai-cmodassign.js`)

`CMODS` holds 20 add-on behaviors (ringPulse, trailMine, enrage, regen, spiral, burst, dash, backstep, shieldPulse, slowField, fan, blades, leech, flicker, cross, snipe, grow, tinySummon, knock, accel; state in `e.fwm*`, trail mines in `node.fwmTrail`). `CMOD_ASSIGN` (generated) maps each C-path handler id (`c15*`-`c24*`, `k<stage>c/d*`) to two modifiers with params; `ai-cmods.js` wraps the base `FWF_ARCH` handler so it runs the archetype then both modifiers. Each (archetype, modifier A, modifier B) triple is unique across the C path. Loaded after all `ai-c*`/`ai-k*` files.

### Stat-converted items (`js/data/statConversions.js`)

Finishing the item-synergy rework: 254 of the 467 remaining candidate items (after `hiddenpassagecharm`) whose desc was a single pure stat bump and that had at most 3 code references were converted to protected-style stat items. `STAT_CONVERTED_ITEMS` maps id -> category (damage, luck, speed, fireRate, range, critChance/stunChance/freezeChance/venomChance/charmChance/fearChance/lifestealChance, heart) and `STAT_CONVERTED_DESC` holds the standard descs (the items' data `desc` fields were rewritten to match). Scaling matches the protected items: +1 damage, +1 Luck, +20 speed, +0.02 shots/sec, +1 tile, +1% per chance stat, +1 heart container.
`applyPassiveEffect` (`items-2.js`) stores these in `player.statPassives` instead of `player.passives`, so every legacy `p.<id>` effect check is inert; `statConvBonus(player)` sums counts per category and `recalcPlayerStats` (`items-1.js`) adds `sc.<category>` terms into the luck, speed, damage (both sums), fire-rate, range and 7 chance sums. The passives bar in `ui.js` shows both maps. The remaining 214 candidates were kept as-is (multi-effect, tradeoff, dodge/bomb-radius/shop/utility, or bespoke code).

### `balance-lab.html` + `tools/balance-lab.js` — Balance Lab
Standalone browser page (not linked from the game). Loads the real game scripts (index.html chain minus main.js/menu-backdrop/music-test/settings) with a Proxy dummy fallback for missing DOM lookups. `Lab.run()` performs: static enemy audit per floorKey (count<40, bad stats, HP outliers, unknown behaviors), item-stack audit (recalcPlayerStats with all protected/converted items per category), and an optional per-enemy duel sim (one enemy vs a centered player via `game.update`, `damagePlayer` wrapped to log damage; records TTK, dps, projectiles, NaN, exceptions, idle). Output is markdown + JSON in a textarea (Copy button) for the user to send back.

### Balance Lab follow-up fixes
- Enemy constructor (entities.js) now copies every numeric type field not already set on the instance (e.g. telegraphTime, leapCooldown, leapSpeed) so handlers reading `e.<param>` work; previously ~20 desert enemies (ds22-ds60) stayed idle.
- ai-forest4.js uses `game.runElapsed` instead of the nonexistent `game.time`.
- ai-cmods.js keeps per-modifier `fwm*` state in `e._fs[slot]`, so stacked modifiers no longer clobber each other.
- js/systems/ai-t14c.js + js/data/enemies/t14c-new.js: 16 extra floorKey 14C enemies (24 to 40).
- `Lab.simEnemy` and `Lab.makeGame` are exported for isolated single-enemy runs.

### Balance Lab: synergy mode, baseline diff, download
- Synergy mode (checkbox, `Lab.synergyLab`): picks 5 stage-3 reference enemies (`refEnemies`), builds a player per item via `playerFor` (`applyPassiveEffect`), scores `eff` (1/ttk, or hpFrac/T when unkilled) with `score`, and reports gain over the no-item baseline. Solo pass covers all non-protected passives; optional pair pass (Pair top-N) duels the N best solo items and reports ratio = pair gain / sum of solo gains.
- New problem types: itemCrash, pairCrash, itemOP, itemHarmful, playerProjSpam (player projectiles > 150), synergyError.
- `simEnemy` now also returns `maxPProj` (player projectiles) and `hpFrac`.
- Save as baseline (localStorage `balanceLabBaseline`) stores compact enemy/item/problem data; later runs append a "Diff vs baseline" section (`diffLines`). Download saves the results box as a .txt file.
- Use a non-Earth class for synergy mode; Earth's 0.5 damage makes gains noisy.

### Balance Lab: real damage, moving player, boss duels, cross-class, triggers
- `simEnemy(game, d, seconds, {boss, real, move, lowHp, floor})`: `real` uses real `damagePlayer` (no invuln reset) and counts heart loss; `move` kites/strafes; `boss` spawns via `new Boss`.
- `bossLab(opts)`: duels every BOSS_TYPES + SUPERBOSSES entry (moving, ~45s); flags bossTrivial / bossTooTanky / bossProjSpam / bossNaN / bossException.
- `synergyLab`: with `classCount>1` also runs solo items on classes spread by damage rate (`cross`, flags classDisparity); inert items retried under real/lowHp/moving/long scenarios (`triggered`), still-inert become `itemDead`.
- UI: checkboxes `#real`, `#move`, `#boss`, inputs `#clscount`, `#bosssecs`.
